sentences.zh: 吳山，字曰靜，高安人。

translations.literal: Wu Shan, styled Yuejing, was a native of Gao'an.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Shan, courtesy name Yuejing, came from Gao'an.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖十四年進士及第，授編修。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year of Jiajing he passed the jinshi examination with highest honors and was appointed Compiler.
translations.idiomatic: In 1535 he took first place among the jinshi graduates and was appointed a Hanlin Compiler.

sentences.zh: 累官禮部左侍郎。

translations.literal: He rose through offices to Left Vice Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through the ranks to become Left Vice Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 三十五年，改吏部。

translations.literal: In the thirty-fifth year he was transferred to the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: In 1556 he was transferred to the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 尋代王用賓為禮部尚書。

translations.literal: Soon he replaced Wang Yongbin as Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he succeeded Wang Yongbin as Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 明年，加太子太保。

translations.literal: The next year he was given the additional title Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was made Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 山與嚴嵩鄉里。

translations.literal: Shan and Yan Song were from the same native place.
translations.idiomatic: Shan was a fellow townsman of Yan Song.

sentences.zh: 嵩子世蕃介大學士李本飲山，欲與為婚姻。

translations.literal: Song's son Shifan had Grand Secretary Li Ben invite Shan to drink, wishing to arrange a marriage alliance.
translations.idiomatic: Song's son Shifan had Grand Secretary Li Ben host Shan at a banquet, hoping to arrange a marriage between their families.

sentences.zh: 山不可，世蕃不悅而罷。

translations.literal: Shan would not agree; Shifan was displeased and let the matter drop.
translations.idiomatic: Shan refused, and Shifan, displeased, dropped the proposal.

sentences.zh: 帝欲用山內閣，嵩密阻之。

translations.literal: The emperor wished to use Shan in the Grand Secretariat; Song secretly obstructed it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wanted to bring Shan into the Grand Secretariat, but Song secretly blocked the appointment.

sentences.zh: 府丞朱隆禧者，考察罷官，獻方術，得加禮部侍郎。

translations.literal: Assistant Prefect Zhu Longxi, dismissed after evaluation, presented occult arts and was promoted to Vice Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: Assistant Prefect Zhu Longxi had been removed from office after an evaluation but won promotion to Vice Minister of Rites by presenting occult arts to the throne.

sentences.zh: 及卒請恤，山執不與。

translations.literal: When he died and posthumous favors were requested, Shan firmly refused to grant them.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhu died and his family petitioned for posthumous honors, Shan steadfastly refused.

sentences.zh: 裕、景二邸並建，國本未定。

translations.literal: The households of the Princes of Yu and Jing were both established, and the succession remained unsettled.
translations.idiomatic: With establishments for both the Prince of Yu and the Prince of Jing, the question of the imperial succession remained unresolved.

sentences.zh: 三十九年冬，帝忽諭禮部，具景王之藩儀。

translations.literal: In the winter of the thirty-ninth year the emperor suddenly instructed the Ministry of Rites to prepare the Prince of Jing's investiture ceremony for departure to his fief.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of 1560 the emperor suddenly ordered the Ministry of Rites to draw up the ceremonies for sending the Prince of Jing to his princely domain.

sentences.zh: 嵩知帝激於郭希顏疏，欲覘人心，諷山留王。

translations.literal: Song knew the emperor had been provoked by Guo Xiyan's memorial and wished to probe public sentiment, and he hinted that Shan should keep the prince.
translations.idiomatic: Song knew the emperor had been stirred by Guo Xiyan's memorial and wanted to test public opinion; he urged Shan to keep the prince at court.

sentences.zh: 山曰：「中外望此久矣」，立具儀以奏，王竟之藩。

translations.literal: Shan said, "Court and country have long awaited this," and at once prepared the ceremony and memorialized; the prince in the end went to his fief.
translations.idiomatic: Shan replied, "Court and country have long awaited this," promptly drew up the ceremonies and memorialized the throne, and the prince was sent to his domain.

sentences.zh: 司禮監黃錦嘗竊語山曰：「公他日得為編氓幸矣；

translations.literal: Director of Ceremonial Huang Jin once whispered to Shan, "Your Excellency will be fortunate one day to become a common subject;
translations.idiomatic: Huang Jin of the Directorate of Ceremonial once confided to Shan, "Your Excellency will be fortunate if you one day become an ordinary subject again;

sentences.zh: 王之藩，非帝意也。」

translations.literal: the prince's going to his fief was not the emperor's intent."
translations.idiomatic: sending the prince to his domain was not what the emperor wanted."

sentences.zh: 明年二月朔，日當食，微陰。

translations.literal: The next year, on the first day of the second month, an eclipse was due; there was slight overcast.
translations.idiomatic: On the first day of the second month the following year an eclipse was expected, but the sky was only slightly overcast.

sentences.zh: 歷官言：「日食不見，即同不食。」

translations.literal: The calendar officials said, "If the solar eclipse is not seen, it is the same as no eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: The calendar officials reported, "If the solar eclipse cannot be seen, it counts as if there were no eclipse.

sentences.zh: 嵩以為天眷，趣部急上賀，侍郎袁煒亦為言。

translations.literal: Song took this as heaven's favor and urged the ministry to hurry congratulations; Vice Minister Yuan Wei also spoke in favor.
translations.idiomatic: Song took this as a sign of heaven's favor and pressed the ministry to submit congratulations at once; Vice Minister Yuan Wei agreed.

sentences.zh: 山仰首曰：「日方虧，將誰欺耶？」

translations.literal: Shan looked up and said, "The sun is still in eclipse—whom do you mean to deceive?
translations.idiomatic: Shan looked up and said, "The sun is still in eclipse—whom do you think you can deceive?

sentences.zh: 仍救護如常儀。

translations.literal: He still carried out the protective rites as usual.
translations.idiomatic: He still ordered the usual protective rites observed.

sentences.zh: 帝大怒，山引罪。

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly angered; Shan took blame upon himself.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was furious, and Shan took the blame upon himself.

sentences.zh: 帝謂山守禮無罪，而責禮科對狀。

translations.literal: The emperor said Shan had observed ritual without guilt, but blamed the Rites Bureau for formal response.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said Shan had done no wrong in upholding ritual, but held the Rites Bureau staff accountable.

sentences.zh: 給事中李東華等震懼，劾山，請與同罪。

translations.literal: Supervising Secretaries Li Donghua and others, in alarm, impeached Shan and asked to share his punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Alarmed, Supervising Secretaries Li Donghua and others impeached Shan and asked to be punished along with him.

sentences.zh: 帝乃責山賣直沽名，停東華俸。

translations.literal: The emperor then reproached Shan for selling integrity to buy reputation and suspended Donghua's salary.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then accused Shan of parading integrity for fame and suspended Donghua's salary.

sentences.zh: 嵩言罪在部臣。

translations.literal: Song said the fault lay with ministry officials.
translations.idiomatic: Song said the fault lay with the ministry staff.

sentences.zh: 帝乃貰東華等，命姑識山罪。

translations.literal: The emperor then pardoned Donghua and the others and ordered Shan's offense merely noted for the time being.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then pardoned Donghua and the others and ordered that Shan's offense be recorded but not yet punished.

sentences.zh: 吏科梁夢龍等見帝怒山甚，又惡專劾山，乃並吏部尚書吳鵬劾之。

translations.literal: Personnel Bureau officials Liang Menglong and others, seeing the emperor's great anger at Shan and disliking the exclusive impeachment of Shan, also jointly impeached Minister of Personnel Wu Peng.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing how angry the emperor was with Shan and resenting a memorial that singled Shan out, Liang Menglong and others of the Personnel Bureau also impeached Minister of Personnel Wu Peng.

sentences.zh: 詔鵬致仕，山冠帶閑住。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Peng to retire; Shan was suspended with his cap and belt.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered Peng to retire and allowed Shan to remain at home in official dress but without duties.

sentences.zh: 時皆惜山而深快鵬之去。

translations.literal: At the time all regretted Shan and deeply rejoiced at Peng's departure.
translations.idiomatic: At the time everyone regretted Shan's fall and was deeply glad to see Peng go.

sentences.zh: 穆宗即位，召為南京禮部尚書，堅辭不赴，卒，贈少保，謚文端。

translations.literal: When Muzong took the throne, Shan was summoned as Nanjing Minister of Rites; he firmly declined and did not go. He died and was posthumously made Junior Guardian, posthumous name Wenduan.
translations.idiomatic: When the Longqing Emperor came to the throne, Shan was summoned as Minister of Rites at Nanjing, but he firmly declined. He died and was posthumously made Junior Guardian with the posthumous name Wenduan.

sentences.zh: 陸樹聲，字與吉，松江華亭人。

translations.literal: Lu Shusheng, styled Yuji, was a native of Huating in Songjiang.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Shusheng, courtesy name Yuji, was a native of Huating in Songjiang.

sentences.zh: 初冒林姓，及貴乃復。

translations.literal: At first he bore the surname Lin; when he rose to eminence he restored his own.
translations.idiomatic: He had originally taken the surname Lin and only restored his own when he rose to prominence.

sentences.zh: 家世業農。

translations.literal: His family for generations practiced farming.
translations.idiomatic: His family had farmed for generations.

sentences.zh: 樹聲少力田，暇即讀書。

translations.literal: Shusheng in youth worked the fields; in spare time he read books.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth Shusheng worked the fields and read whenever he had spare time.

sentences.zh: 舉嘉靖二十年會試第一。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year of Jiajing he took first place in the metropolitan examination.
translations.idiomatic: In 1541 he placed first in the metropolitan examination.

sentences.zh: 選庶吉士，授編修。

translations.literal: He was selected as a Hanlin bachelor and appointed Compiler.
translations.idiomatic: He was selected as a Hanlin bachelor and appointed Compiler.

sentences.zh: 三十一年，請急歸。

translations.literal: In the thirty-first year he requested leave on urgent family grounds and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: In 1552 he asked leave on urgent family grounds and returned home.

sentences.zh: 遭父喪，久之，起南京司業。

translations.literal: He suffered his father's death; after a long interval he was recalled as Nanjing Vice Director of Studies.
translations.idiomatic: After his father's death he remained in mourning for a long time, then was recalled as Vice Director of Studies at Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 未幾，復請告去。

translations.literal: Before long he again requested leave and departed.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he again asked leave and went home.

sentences.zh: 起左諭德，掌南京翰林院。

translations.literal: He was raised to Left Tutor and directed the Nanjing Hanlin Academy.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Left Tutor and put in charge of the Nanjing Hanlin Academy.

sentences.zh: 尋召還春坊，不赴。

translations.literal: Soon he was summoned back to the Eastern Palace staff but did not go.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon summoned back to the Heir Apparent's staff but declined to go.

sentences.zh: 久之，起太常卿，掌南京祭酒事。

translations.literal: After a long time he was raised to Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and directed Nanjing libationer affairs.
translations.idiomatic: After a long interval he was made Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and Chancellor of the Nanjing National University.

sentences.zh: 嚴敕學規，著條教十二以勵諸生。

translations.literal: He strictly enjoined academic regulations and composed twelve articles of instruction to encourage the students.
translations.idiomatic: He strictly enforced academic regulations and wrote twelve articles of instruction to guide the students.

sentences.zh: 召為吏部右侍郎，引病不拜。

translations.literal: He was summoned as Right Vice Minister of Personnel but pleaded illness and did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned as Right Vice Minister of Personnel but pleaded illness and declined the appointment.

sentences.zh: 隆慶中，再起故官，不就。

translations.literal: In the Longqing reign he was again raised to his former office but did not take it.
translations.idiomatic: During the Longqing reign he was offered his former post again but refused.

sentences.zh: 神宗嗣位，即家拜禮部尚書。

translations.literal: When Shenzong succeeded, he was appointed Minister of Rites at his home.
translations.idiomatic: When the Wanli Emperor succeeded, Shusheng was appointed Minister of Rites while still at home.

sentences.zh: 初，樹聲屢辭朝命，中外高其風節。

translations.literal: At first Shusheng repeatedly declined court appointments; within and without the court his integrity was esteemed.
translations.idiomatic: Because Shusheng had repeatedly declined court appointments, men inside and outside government admired his integrity.

sentences.zh: 遇要職，必首舉樹聲，唯恐其不至。

translations.literal: When important posts arose, he was always the first recommended, lest he not come.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever an important post opened, officials would recommend Shusheng first, fearing he might not accept.

sentences.zh: 張居正當國，以得樹聲為重，用後進禮先謁之。

translations.literal: When Zhang Juzheng held power, he regarded winning Shusheng as weighty and, though the junior in office, went first to call on him.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Juzheng was chief minister he prized winning Shusheng's support and, though the junior in rank, paid him the first visit.

sentences.zh: 樹聲相對穆然，意若不甚接者，居正失望去。

translations.literal: Shusheng received him with grave composure, as if not very receptive; Juzheng left disappointed.
translations.idiomatic: Shusheng received him with grave reserve, as if unwilling to be drawn close, and Zhang left disappointed.

sentences.zh: 一日，以公事詣政府。

translations.literal: One day, on public business, he went to the chief minister's office.
translations.idiomatic: One day he called at the chief minister's office on public business.

sentences.zh: 見席稍偏，熟視不就坐，居正趣為正席。

translations.literal: Seeing the seat slightly askew, he gazed fixedly and would not sit; Juzheng hurried to set the seat straight.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing the seat placed slightly off-center, he stared at it and refused to sit until Zhang hurried to set it properly.

sentences.zh: 其介介如此。

translations.literal: He was so punctilious in this way.
translations.idiomatic: Such was his punctiliousness.

sentences.zh: 北部要增歲幣，兵部將許之，樹聲力爭。

translations.literal: The northern frontier sought increased annual payments; the Ministry of War was about to agree, but Shusheng argued forcefully against it.
translations.idiomatic: When the northern frontier demanded higher annual payments and the Ministry of War was ready to agree, Shusheng argued forcefully against it.

sentences.zh: 歲終，陳四方災異，請帝循舊章，省奏牘，慎賞賚，防壅蔽，納讜言，崇儉德，攬魁柄，別忠邪。

translations.literal: At year's end he presented disasters and portents from the four quarters and asked the emperor to follow old statutes, reduce memorials, be cautious in rewards, guard against obstruction, accept candid speech, honor frugal virtue, grasp the chief handles of power, and distinguish loyal from treacherous.
translations.idiomatic: At year's end he memorialized on disasters and portents throughout the realm, urging the emperor to follow established precedent, reduce paperwork, be sparing with rewards, guard against blocked channels of information, heed candid counsel, practice frugality, hold the reins of power firmly, and distinguish loyal ministers from the treacherous.

sentences.zh: 詔皆嘉納。

translations.literal: An edict praised and accepted all.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's reply praised and accepted every point.

sentences.zh: 萬歷改元，中官不樂樹聲，屢宣詣會極門受旨，且頻趣之。

translations.literal: At the change of reign title in Wanli, eunuchs disliked Shusheng and repeatedly summoned him to the Gate of Gathering Excellence to receive instructions, pressing him frequently.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Wanli reign the eunuchs disliked Shusheng and repeatedly summoned him to the Gate of Gathering Excellence to receive instructions, pressing him again and again.

sentences.zh: 比趨至，則曹司常事耳。

translations.literal: When he hurried there, it was only routine bureau business.
translations.idiomatic: When he hurried there, the matter proved to be nothing more than routine bureau business.

sentences.zh: 樹聲知其意，連疏乞休。

translations.literal: Shusheng knew their intent and submitted successive memorials asking to retire.
translations.idiomatic: Shusheng understood their intent and submitted repeated memorials asking to retire.

sentences.zh: 居正語其弟樹德曰：「朝廷行相平泉矣。」

translations.literal: Juzheng said to his younger brother Shude, "The court is about to make Pingquan chief minister.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang told Shusheng's younger brother Shude, "The court is about to make Pingquan chief minister.

sentences.zh: 平泉者，樹聲別號也。

translations.literal: Pingquan was Shusheng's style name.
translations.idiomatic: Pingquan was Shusheng's sobriquet.

sentences.zh: 樹聲聞之曰：「一史官，去國二十年，豈復希揆席耶？

translations.literal: Shusheng heard and said, "A mere historiographer, away from court twenty years—would he still covet the chief minister's seat?
translations.idiomatic: When Shusheng heard this he said, "A mere historiographer who has been away from court for twenty years—would he still covet the chief minister's seat?

sentences.zh: 且虛拘何益。」

translations.literal: Besides, what good is empty detention?
translations.idiomatic: Besides, what good does it do to detain me in name only?

sentences.zh: 其冬，請愈力，乃命乘傳歸。

translations.literal: That winter his requests grew stronger, and he was ordered to return home by post-horse relay.
translations.idiomatic: That winter his requests grew more insistent, and he was ordered home with relay horses.

sentences.zh: 辭朝，陳時政十事，語多切中，報聞而已。

translations.literal: Bidding farewell at court, he set forth ten points on current policy; the words mostly hit the mark, but the reply was merely acknowledgment.
translations.idiomatic: On leaving court he presented ten points on current policy, most of them telling; the reply was merely acknowledgment.

sentences.zh: 居正就邸舍與別，問誰可代者。

translations.literal: Juzheng came to his lodging to take leave and asked who could replace him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang called at his lodging to take leave and asked whom he would recommend as his successor.

sentences.zh: 舉萬士和、林燫。

translations.literal: He recommended Wan Shihe and Lin Yan.
translations.idiomatic: He named Wan Shihe and Lin Yan.

sentences.zh: 比出國門，士大夫傾城追送，皆謝不見。

translations.literal: When he passed out the city gate, officials and gentry turned out in force to see him off; he thanked them all and would not receive them.
translations.idiomatic: As he left the capital, officials and gentry turned out in force to see him off, but he thanked them all and refused to receive them.

sentences.zh: 樹聲端介恬雅，翛然物表，難進易退。

translations.literal: Shusheng was upright, punctilious, tranquil, and elegant, detached above worldly things, hard to advance and easy to withdraw.
translations.idiomatic: Shusheng was upright, reserved, and refined, aloof from worldly things, slow to enter office and quick to leave it.

sentences.zh: 通籍六十余年，居官未及一紀。

translations.literal: On the registers more than sixty years, in office not yet twelve.
translations.idiomatic: He had been on the rolls for more than sixty years but had actually held office for less than twelve.

sentences.zh: 與徐階同里，高拱則同年生。

translations.literal: He was from the same district as Xu Jie; Gao Gong was a classmate.
translations.idiomatic: He was a fellow townsman of Xu Jie and a jinshi classmate of Gao Gong.

sentences.zh: 兩人相繼柄國，皆辭疾不出。

translations.literal: The two in succession held state power; both pleaded illness and did not emerge.
translations.idiomatic: Both men in turn dominated the government, yet Shusheng pleaded illness and would not serve under either.

sentences.zh: 為居正所推，卒不附也。

translations.literal: Recommended by Juzheng, in the end he did not attach himself.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Juzheng recommended him too, yet in the end he never cast in his lot with him.

sentences.zh: 已，給廩隸如制，加太子少保，再遣存問。

translations.literal: Thereafter grain allotments and attendants were granted by regulation; he was made Junior Guardian of the Crown Prince, and envoys were again dispatched to inquire after him.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward the court granted him grain and attendants by regulation, promoted him to Junior Guardian of the Crown Prince, and again sent envoys to inquire after his health.

sentences.zh: 弟樹德，自有傳。

translations.literal: His younger brother Shude has his own biography.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Shude has a separate biography.

sentences.zh: 子彥章，萬歷十七年進士。

translations.literal: His son Yanzhang was a jinshi in the seventeenth year of Wanli.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yanzhang passed the jinshi examination in Wanli 17 (1589).

sentences.zh: 樹聲誡毋就館選，隨以行人終養。

translations.literal: Shusheng admonished him not to accept Hanlin selection; he then ended his career as a courier official while completing filial retirement.
translations.idiomatic: Shusheng warned him not to accept a Hanlin appointment; he served instead as a courier official until he retired to complete filial mourning.

sentences.zh: 詔給月俸，異數也。

translations.literal: An edict granted him monthly salary—an exceptional favor.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered that he receive a monthly salary—an exceptional honor.

sentences.zh: 樹聲年九十七卒。

translations.literal: Shusheng died at the age of ninety-seven.
translations.idiomatic: Shusheng died at ninety-seven.

sentences.zh: 贈太子太保。

translations.literal: Posthumously honored as Grand Guardian of the Crown Prince.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously honored as Grand Guardian of the Crown Prince.

sentences.zh: 謚文定。

translations.literal: Posthumous title Wending.
translations.idiomatic: He was given the posthumous title Wending.

sentences.zh: 彥章有節概，官至南京刑部侍郎。

translations.literal: Yanzhang possessed integrity and moral courage; he reached the post of Vice Minister of Justice at Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: Yanzhang was known for integrity and principled conduct; he rose to Vice Minister of Justice at Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 瞿景淳，字師道，常熟人。

translations.literal: Qu Jingchun, courtesy name Shidao, was a native of Changshu.
translations.idiomatic: Qu Jingchun, whose courtesy name was Shidao, was a native of Changshu.

sentences.zh: 八歲能屬文。

translations.literal: At eight he could compose literary pieces.
translations.idiomatic: At eight he could already write essays.

sentences.zh: 久困諸生間，教授里中自給。

translations.literal: Long held down among licentiates, he supported himself by teaching in his home district.
translations.idiomatic: Long stuck among licentiates, he supported himself teaching in his home district.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖二十三年，舉會試第一，殿試第二，授編修。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year of Jiajing he placed first in the metropolitan examination and second in the palace examination, and was appointed Compiler.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiajing 23 (1544) he ranked first in the metropolitan examination and second in the palace examination, and was appointed a Hanlin Compiler.

sentences.zh: 鄭王厚烷以言事廢，徙鳳陽。

translations.literal: The Prince of Zheng, Houwan, was deposed for speaking on state affairs and was relocated to Fengyang.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Houwan of Zheng was deposed for memorializing on state affairs and was relocated to Fengyang.

sentences.zh: 景淳奉敕封其子載堉為世子，攝國事。

translations.literal: Jingchun received an imperial command to invest his son Zaiyu as heir apparent and to administer state affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Jingchun received orders to invest the prince's son Zaiyu as heir apparent and administer state affairs in his stead.

sentences.zh: 世子內懼，贐重幣，景淳卻之。

translations.literal: The heir was inwardly fearful and sent lavish gifts; Jingchun declined them.
translations.idiomatic: The heir, inwardly afraid, sent him lavish gifts, but Jingchun refused them.

sentences.zh: 時恭順侯吳繼爵為正使，已受幣，慚景淳，亦謝不納。

translations.literal: At the time the Marquis of Gongshun, Wu Jijue, was chief envoy; having already accepted gifts, he was ashamed before Jingchun and also declined to keep them.
translations.idiomatic: The chief envoy, Marquis Wu Jijue of Gongshun, had already accepted gifts but, ashamed before Jingchun, likewise refused to keep them.

sentences.zh: 既而語景淳曰：「上遣使密诇狀，微公，吾幾中法。」

translations.literal: Later he said to Jingchun, "The emperor sent envoys to investigate the situation in secret; but for you, I nearly fell afoul of the law."
translations.idiomatic: Later he told Jingchun, "The emperor sent men to investigate in secret; but for you, I would nearly have run afoul of the law."

sentences.zh: 滿九載，遷侍讀，請急歸。

translations.literal: After nine full years he was promoted to Reader and requested urgent leave to return home.
translations.idiomatic: After nine years he was promoted to Reader and urgently petitioned to return home.

sentences.zh: 江南久苦倭，總督胡宗憲師未捷。

translations.literal: Jiangnan had long suffered from wokou raids; Grand Coordinator Hu Zongxian's army had not yet won a victory.
translations.idiomatic: Jiangnan had long been ravaged by wokou pirates, and Grand Coordinator Hu Zongxian's troops had still not scored a victory.

sentences.zh: 景淳還京，謁大學士嚴嵩。

translations.literal: Jingchun returned to the capital and called on Grand Secretary Yan Song.
translations.idiomatic: When Jingchun returned to the capital he called on Grand Secretary Yan Song.

sentences.zh: 嵩語之曰：「倭旦夕且平。

translations.literal: Song said to him, "The pirates will be pacified any day now.
translations.idiomatic: Song told him, "The pirates will be subdued before long.

sentences.zh: 胡總督才足辦，南中人短之，何也？」

translations.literal: Governor-General Hu's talent is enough to handle it—why do people in the south speak ill of him?"
translations.idiomatic: Governor-General Hu is fully capable of handling them—why do southerners speak ill of him?"

sentences.zh: 景淳正色曰：「相公遙度之耳。

translations.literal: Jingchun said sternly, "Minister, you are judging from afar.
translations.idiomatic: Jingchun replied sternly, "Minister, you are pronouncing from a distance.

sentences.zh: 景淳自南來，目睹倭患。

translations.literal: Jingchun came from the south and witnessed the pirate calamity with his own eyes.
translations.idiomatic: Jingchun had just come from the south and had seen the pirate scourge firsthand.

sentences.zh: 胡君坐擁十萬師，南中人不得一安枕臥。

translations.literal: Lord Hu sits idle with a hundred thousand troops, yet the people of the south cannot sleep a single night in peace.
translations.idiomatic: Lord Hu sits with a hundred thousand troops at his command, yet no one in the south can sleep through the night.

sentences.zh: 相公不欲聞，誰為言者？」

translations.literal: If you, Minister, do not wish to hear it, who will speak of it?"
translations.idiomatic: If you will not listen, Minister, who is left to tell you the truth?"

sentences.zh: 嵩愕然謝之。

translations.literal: Song was startled and apologized to him.
translations.idiomatic: Song was taken aback and apologized to him.

sentences.zh: 歷侍讀學士，掌院事。

translations.literal: He served as Reader and Academician and managed Hanlin affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Reader and Academician and directed Hanlin Academy affairs.

sentences.zh: 改太常卿，領南京祭酒事，就遷吏部右侍郎。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Minister of Ceremonies, took charge of the Nanjing Chancellor of the Directorate of Education, and was thereupon promoted to Vice Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Minister of Ceremonies and put in charge of the Nanjing Directorate of Education, then promoted to Vice Minister of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 隆慶元年，召為禮部左侍郎。

translations.literal: In the first year of Longqing he was summoned as Vice Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: In Longqing 1 (1567) he was recalled as Vice Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 用總校《永樂大典》勞，兼翰林院學士，支二品俸，侍經筵，修《嘉靖實錄》。

translations.literal: For his labors as chief collator of the Yongle Dadian, he was concurrently made Hanlin Academician, paid second-rank salary, attended the classics lecture, and compiled the Veritable Records of Jiajing.
translations.idiomatic: Rewarded for supervising collation of the Yongle Encyclopedia, he was concurrently made a Hanlin Academician on second-rank pay, attended the classics lecture, and helped compile the Veritable Records of Jiajing.

sentences.zh: 疾作，累疏乞骸骨歸。

translations.literal: When illness struck he repeatedly memorialized asking to retire and return home.
translations.idiomatic: When he fell ill he memorialized repeatedly asking to retire.

sentences.zh: 逾年卒。

translations.literal: More than a year later he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died a little over a year later.

sentences.zh: 贈禮部尚書，謚文懿。

translations.literal: Posthumously honored as Minister of Rites; posthumous title Wenyi.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously honored as Minister of Rites and given the posthumous title Wenyi.

sentences.zh: 為編修時，典制誥。

translations.literal: When he was a Compiler he managed the drafting of patents and edicts.
translations.idiomatic: As a Compiler he was in charge of drafting imperial patents and edicts.

sentences.zh: 錦衣陸炳先後四妻，欲封最後者，屬景淳撰詞，不可。

translations.literal: The Embroidered-Uniform Guard Lu Bing had four wives in succession and wished to ennoble the last; he asked Jingchun to draft the patent, but he would not.
translations.idiomatic: Embroidered-Uniform Guard Lu Bing had taken four wives in succession and wanted to ennoble the last; he asked Jingchun to draft the patent, but Jingchun refused.

sentences.zh: 介嚴嵩為請，亦不應。

translations.literal: Yan Song interceded on his behalf; still he would not agree.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Song interceded for him, but Jingchun still would not comply.

sentences.zh: 橐金以投，卒笑謝之。

translations.literal: He sent gold in a bag; in the end Jingchun smiled and declined it.
translations.idiomatic: Lu sent him a bag of gold; Jingchun only smiled and courteously refused.

sentences.zh: 子汝稷、汝說。

translations.literal: Sons Ruji and Ruoshuo.
translations.idiomatic: He had two sons, Ruji and Ruoshuo.

sentences.zh: 汝稷字元立。

translations.literal: Ruji, courtesy name Yuanli.
translations.idiomatic: Ruji, whose courtesy name was Yuanli.

sentences.zh: 好學，工屬文，以陰補官。

translations.literal: Fond of learning and skilled at composition, he entered office through yin privilege.
translations.idiomatic: He loved learning and wrote well, and entered office through yin privilege.

sentences.zh: 三遷刑部主事。

translations.literal: Promoted three times to Principal Clerk in the Ministry of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted three times to Principal Clerk in the Ministry of Justice.

sentences.zh: 扶溝知縣抶宗人，神宗令予重比。

translations.literal: The magistrate of Fugou beat a clansman; Shenzong ordered a heavier sentence.
translations.idiomatic: When the magistrate of Fugou beat a clansman, Shenzong ordered a heavier penalty.

sentences.zh: 汝稷曰：「是微服至邑庭，官自抶扶溝民耳。」

translations.literal: Ruji said, "He went in plain clothes to the county court—the official himself beat a commoner of Fugou."
translations.idiomatic: Ruji said, "The man went to the county court in plain clothes—the magistrate simply beat a commoner of Fugou."

sentences.zh: 讞上，竟得釋。

translations.literal: The case report was submitted, and in the end he was released.
translations.idiomatic: When the case report went up, the clansman was released after all.

sentences.zh: 歷黃州知府，徙邵武，再守辰州。

translations.literal: He served as Prefect of Huangzhou, was transferred to Shaowu, and again governed Chenzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He served as prefect of Huangzhou, was transferred to Shaowu, and later governed Chenzhou again.

sentences.zh: 永順土司彭元錦助其弟保靖土司象坤，與酉陽冉躍龍相仇殺。

translations.literal: Yongshun native chieftain Peng Yuanjin aided his younger brother, Baojing chieftain Xiang Kun, in feuding and mutual killing with Youyang's Ran Yuelong.
translations.idiomatic: Peng Yuanjin, chieftain of Yongshun, backed his younger brother Xiang Kun, chieftain of Baojing, in a feud and blood feud with Ran Yuelong of Youyang.

sentences.zh: 汝稷馳檄元錦解兵去，三土司皆安。

translations.literal: Ruji urgently dispatched a proclamation ordering Yuanjin to disband his troops and withdraw; all three chieftains were pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Ruji sent an urgent dispatch ordering Yuanjin to stand down; all three chieftains were pacified.

sentences.zh: 尋遷長蘆鹽運使，以太仆少卿致仕。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he was promoted to Salt Transport Commissioner of Changlu and retired as Vice Minister of the Court of the Imperial Stud.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon promoted to Salt Transport Commissioner of Changlu and later retired as Vice Minister of the Court of the Imperial Stud.

sentences.zh: 尋卒。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died not long after.

sentences.zh: 汝說字星卿。

translations.literal: Ruoshuo, courtesy name Xingqing.
translations.idiomatic: Ruoshuo, whose courtesy name was Xingqing.

sentences.zh: 五歲而孤。

translations.literal: Orphaned at five.
translations.idiomatic: He lost his father at five.

sentences.zh: 構文成，輒跪薦父木主前。

translations.literal: Whenever he finished a literary composition, he would kneel and offer it before his father's spirit tablet.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he finished a piece of writing, he knelt and presented it before his father's spirit tablet.

sentences.zh: 萬歷中舉進士，官至湖廣提學僉事。

translations.literal: Mid-Wanli he passed the provincial and metropolitan examinations and became a jinshi; he reached the post of Surveillance Commissioner for Education in Huguang.
translations.idiomatic: In the Wanli era he passed the examinations and became a jinshi, eventually rising to Surveillance Commissioner for Education in Huguang.

sentences.zh: 亦以剛正聞。

translations.literal: He too was known for stern uprightness.
translations.idiomatic: He too was known for uncompromising integrity.

sentences.zh: 子式耜，別有傳。

translations.literal: His son Shisi has a separate biography.
translations.idiomatic: His son Shisi has a biography elsewhere.

sentences.zh: 田一俊，字德萬，大田人。

translations.literal: Tian Yijun, courtesy name Dewan, was a native of Datian.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Yijun, whose courtesy name was Dewan, was a native of Datian.

sentences.zh: 隆慶二年會試第一。

translations.literal: In the second year of Longqing he placed first in the metropolitan examination.
translations.idiomatic: In Longqing 2 (1568) he topped the metropolitan examination.

sentences.zh: 選庶吉士，授編修，進侍講。

translations.literal: Selected as Hanlin Bachelor, appointed Compiler, and advanced to Lecturer.
translations.idiomatic: He was selected as a Hanlin Bachelor, appointed Compiler, and promoted to Lecturer.

sentences.zh: 萬歷五年，吳中行攻張居正奪情，趙用賢等繼之，居正怒不測。

translations.literal: In Wanli 5, Wu Zhonghang attacked Zhang Juzheng over refusing mourning leave; Zhao Yongxian and others followed, and Juzheng's wrath was unpredictable.
translations.idiomatic: In Wanli 5 (1577), Wu Zhonghang attacked Zhang Juzheng for holding office without observing mourning; Zhao Yongxian and others followed, and Juzheng's anger knew no bounds.

sentences.zh: 一俊偕侍講趙誌臯、修撰沈懋學等疏救，格不入。

translations.literal: Yijun together with Lecturer Zhao Zhigao, Compiler Shen Maoxue, and others memorialized in their defense, but the memorials were blocked and not accepted.
translations.idiomatic: Yijun joined Lecturer Zhao Zhigao, Compiler Shen Maoxue, and others in memorials on their behalf, but the petitions were blocked.

sentences.zh: 乃會王錫爵等詣居正，陳大義。

translations.literal: They then joined Wang Xijue and others in visiting Juzheng to set forth the great principles.
translations.idiomatic: They then went with Wang Xijue and others to see Juzheng and argue the larger principles at stake.

sentences.zh: 一俊詞尤峻，居正心嗛之。

translations.literal: Yijun's words were especially sharp; Juzheng inwardly resented him.
translations.idiomatic: Yijun's language was especially cutting, and Juzheng came to resent him.

sentences.zh: 未幾，誌臯等皆逐，一俊先請告歸，獲免。

translations.literal: Before long Zhigao and the others were all expelled; Yijun had already requested leave and returned home and so escaped punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Zhigao and the others were all driven out; Yijun had already asked to retire and so escaped.

sentences.zh: 居正歿，起故官。

translations.literal: When Juzheng died, he was restored to his former office.
translations.idiomatic: After Juzheng's death he was recalled to his former post.

sentences.zh: 屢遷禮部左侍郎，掌翰林院。

translations.literal: Repeatedly promoted to Vice Minister of Rites, he managed the Hanlin Academy.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Vice Minister of Rites and directed the Hanlin Academy.

sentences.zh: 辭疾歸，未行卒。

translations.literal: He pleaded illness and asked to return home; before he could leave, he died.
translations.idiomatic: He asked to retire on grounds of illness but died before he could leave.

sentences.zh: 一俊禔身嚴苦，家無贏貲。

translations.literal: Yijun cultivated himself with strict austerity; the household had no surplus wealth.
translations.idiomatic: Yijun lived with stern austerity; his household had no spare funds.

sentences.zh: 贈禮部尚書。

translations.literal: Posthumously honored as Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously honored as Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 懋學，字君典，宣城人。

translations.literal: Maoxue, courtesy name Jundian, was a native of Xuancheng.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Maoxue, whose courtesy name was Jundian, was a native of Xuancheng.

sentences.zh: 父寵，字畏思。

translations.literal: His father Chong, courtesy name Weisi.
translations.idiomatic: His father Shen Chong, whose courtesy name was Weisi.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖中舉鄉試，授行唐知縣。

translations.literal: Mid-Jiajing he passed the provincial examination and was appointed magistrate of Xingtang.
translations.idiomatic: In the Jiajing era he passed the provincial examination and was appointed magistrate of Xingtang.

sentences.zh: 以民不諳織纴，置機杼教之。

translations.literal: Because the people did not know spinning and weaving, he set up looms to teach them.
translations.idiomatic: Finding the people unskilled at spinning and weaving, he installed looms and taught them.

sentences.zh: 調獲鹿，征授御史，官至廣西參議。

translations.literal: Transferred to Huolu, summoned and appointed censor; he reached Assistant Administrator of Guangxi.
translations.idiomatic: After transfer to Huolu he was summoned and made a censor, eventually rising to Assistant Administrator of Guangxi.

sentences.zh: 師貢安國、歐陽德，又從王畿、錢德洪遊。

translations.literal: He studied under Gong Anguo and Ouyang De, and also associated with Wang Ji and Qian Dehong.
translations.idiomatic: He studied under Gong Anguo and Ouyang De and also traveled in the company of Wang Ji and Qian Dehong.

sentences.zh: 知府羅汝芳創講會，御史耿定向聘寵與梅守德共主其席。

translations.literal: When Prefect Luo Rufang founded a lecture society, Censor Geng Dingxiang engaged Chong together with Mei Shoude to preside jointly over it.
translations.idiomatic: When Prefect Luo Rufang founded a lecture society, Censor Geng Dingxiang invited Chong and Mei Shoude to chair it together.

sentences.zh: 懋學少有才名。

translations.literal: Maoxue in his youth had a reputation for talent.
translations.idiomatic: Maoxue was noted for talent from a young age.

sentences.zh: 舉萬歷五年進士第一，授修撰。

translations.literal: In Wanli 5 he ranked first among jinshi and was appointed Compiler.
translations.idiomatic: In Wanli 5 he came out first among the jinshi and was appointed Compiler.

sentences.zh: 居正子嗣修，其同年生也。

translations.literal: Juzheng's son Siziu was a classmate of his.
translations.idiomatic: Juzheng's son Siziu was his examination cohort.

sentences.zh: 疏既格不入，乃三貽書勸嗣修諫，嗣修不能用。

translations.literal: After his memorial was blocked, he thrice sent letters urging Siziu to remonstrate, but Siziu could not act on it.
translations.idiomatic: When his memorial was blocked, he wrote Siziu three times urging him to remonstrate, but Siziu could not bring himself to do it.

sentences.zh: 以工部尚書李幼滋與居正善，復貽書為言。

translations.literal: Because Minister of Works Li Youzi was on good terms with Juzheng, he again sent letters appealing to him.
translations.idiomatic: Since Minister of Works Li Youzi was close to Juzheng, he wrote him as well.

sentences.zh: 幼滋報曰：「若所言，宋人腐語，趙氏所以不競也。

translations.literal: Youzi replied, "What you say is stale Song-dynasty platitudes—the reason the house of Zhao could not prevail.
translations.idiomatic: Youzi answered, "That is Song-dynasty cant—the very reason the Zhao house could not compete.

sentences.zh: 張公不奔喪，與揖讓征誅，並得聖賢中道，賢儒安足知之。」

translations.literal: Master Zhang's not rushing home for mourning, together with yielding by courtesy and punitive expeditions, both attain the sages' middle way—how could petty Confucians know enough to judge?"
translations.idiomatic: Master Zhang's refusal to leave office for mourning, like yielding by ritual and launching punitive campaigns, holds to the sages' middle way—what do narrow Confucians know of it?"

sentences.zh: 幼滋初講學，盜虛名，至是縉紳不與焉。

translations.literal: Youzi had at first lectured on learning and stolen a hollow reputation; from this point the gentry would have nothing to do with him.
translations.idiomatic: Youzi had built a reputation lecturing on Neo-Confucian learning; after this the gentry would have nothing to do with him.

sentences.zh: 懋學遂引疾歸。

translations.literal: Maoxue then pleaded illness and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: Maoxue thereupon pleaded illness and went home.

sentences.zh: 居數年，卒。

translations.literal: After several years he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died several years later.

sentences.zh: 福王時，追謚文節。

translations.literal: Under the Prince of Fu he was posthumously given the title Wenjie.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Prince of Fu he was posthumously granted the title Wenjie.

sentences.zh: 從孫壽民，字眉生，為諸生有聲。

translations.literal: Grandnephew Shoumin, courtesy name Meisheng, as a licentiate had a good reputation.
translations.idiomatic: Maoxue's grandnephew Shoumin, courtesy name Meisheng, was a licentiate of some renown.

sentences.zh: 崇禎九年，行保舉法，巡撫張國維以壽民應詔。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Chongzhen the recommendation system was enacted; Grand Coordinator Zhang Guowei recommended Shoumin in response to the imperial call.
translations.idiomatic: In Chongzhen 9 (1636), when the recommendation system was introduced, Grand Coordinator Zhang Guowei nominated Shoumin at the emperor's request.

sentences.zh: 甫入都，疏劾兵部尚書楊嗣昌奪情。

translations.literal: Just after entering the capital he memorialized impeaching Minister of War Yang Sichang for holding office while in mourning.
translations.idiomatic: Hardly had he reached the capital when he memorialized to impeach Minister of War Yang Sichang for resuming office without observing mourning.

sentences.zh: 復攻總督熊文燦，言：「嗣昌挈軍旅權，付文燦兵十二萬，餉二百八十余萬。

translations.literal: He also attacked Grand Coordinator Xiong Wencan, saying, "Sichang seized military authority and entrusted Wencan with a hundred and twenty thousand troops and more than 2.8 million in rations.
translations.idiomatic: He also assailed Grand Coordinator Xiong Wencan, writing, "Sichang has taken military authority upon himself and handed Wencan a hundred and twenty thousand men and more than 2.8 million taels in pay.

sentences.zh: 使賊面縛輿櫬，猶應宣布皇威，而後待以不死；

translations.literal: Even if the bandits came bound, with coffins on their shoulders, imperial majesty should still be proclaimed first, and only then should they be spared death;
translations.idiomatic: Even if rebels came bound with coffins on their shoulders to surrender, the court should first proclaim imperial majesty and only then grant mercy;

sentences.zh: 今乃講盟結約，若與國然。

translations.literal: yet now treaties and alliances are being negotiated as if with an equal state.
translations.idiomatic: yet now pacts are being negotiated as though with a foreign power.

sentences.zh: 天下有授柄於賊而能制賊者乎？」

translations.literal: In all under Heaven, has anyone ever handed the reins to bandits and still been able to control them?"
translations.idiomatic: Who in the realm ever handed leverage to bandits and still controlled them?"

sentences.zh: 通政張紹先寢不上。

translations.literal: Transmission Commissioner Zhang Shaoxian suppressed it and did not submit it.
translations.idiomatic: Transmission Commissioner Zhang Shaoxian shelved the memorial and never forwarded it.

sentences.zh: 壽民以書責，紹先乃請上裁，嗣昌皇恐待罪。

translations.literal: Shoumin reproached him in a letter; Shaoxian then asked the emperor to decide, and Sichang was terrified and awaited punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Shoumin rebuked him by letter; Shaoxian then sought the emperor's ruling, and Sichang was terrified and waited to be punished.

sentences.zh: 帝以疏違式，命勿進。

translations.literal: The emperor, finding the memorial irregular in form, ordered that Shoumin not be advanced.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ruled that the memorial violated protocol and ordered that Shoumin not be promoted.

sentences.zh: 壽民遂隱括兩疏上之，留中。

translations.literal: Shoumin then secretly combined the two memorials and submitted them; they were kept at court without action.
translations.idiomatic: Shoumin then secretly condensed both memorials and submitted them; they were received but left undecided.

sentences.zh: 少詹事黃道周嘆曰：「此何等事，在朝者不言而草野言之，吾輩愧死矣。」

translations.literal: Junior Guardian Huang Daozhou sighed and said: "What sort of affair is this—that those in court do not speak while those in the wilds do speak? We ought to die of shame.
translations.idiomatic: Junior Guardian Huang Daozhou sighed and said, "What kind of affair is this—that court officials keep silent while common folk speak out? We ought to die of shame.

sentences.zh: 後道周及何楷等相繼抗疏，要自壽民發之。

translations.literal: Later Daozhou and He Kai and others in succession submitted remonstrating memorials; the essential point originated with Shoumin.
translations.idiomatic: Later Daozhou, He Kai, and others submitted remonstrances in succession—the movement owed its origin to Shoumin.

sentences.zh: 壽民名動天下。

translations.literal: Shoumin's name shook all under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Shoumin's fame shook the realm.

sentences.zh: 未幾移疾去，講學姑山，從遊者數百人。

translations.literal: Before long he cited illness and departed; he lectured at Mount Gu, and those who followed him numbered several hundred.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he cited illness and left office. He lectured at Mount Gu, and several hundred students followed him.

sentences.zh: 福王時，阮大鋮用事，銜壽民劾嗣昌疏有「大鋮妄陳條畫，鼓煽豐芑」語，必欲殺之。

translations.literal: During the Prince of Fu's time, Ruan Dacheng wielded power; he bore a grudge because Shoumin's memorial impeaching Sichang contained the words "Dacheng recklessly set forth schemes, inciting the Feng-Qi faction," and was determined to kill him.
translations.idiomatic: During the reign of the Prince of Fu, Ruan Dacheng held power. He nursed a grudge because Shoumin's memorial impeaching Sichang contained the phrase "Dacheng recklessly put forward schemes, inciting the Feng-Qi faction," and was determined to kill him.

sentences.zh: 壽民乃變姓名避之金華山。

translations.literal: Shoumin then changed his name and surname and took refuge on Mount Jinhua.
translations.idiomatic: Shoumin then changed his name and hid himself on Mount Jinhua.

sentences.zh: 國變乃歸，不復出。

translations.literal: When the state changed he returned; he did not go out again.
translations.idiomatic: When the dynasty fell he returned home and never went out again.

sentences.zh: 黃鳳翔，字鳴周，晉江人。

translations.literal: Huang Fengxiang, courtesy name Mingzhou, was a man of Jinjiang.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Fengxiang, courtesy name Mingzhou, was a native of Jinjiang.

sentences.zh: 隆慶二年進士及第，授編修。

translations.literal: In Longqing 2 he passed the jinshi examination with highest honors and was appointed Compiler.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Longqing he passed the jinshi examination with highest honors and was appointed Compiler.

sentences.zh: 教習內書堂，輯前史宦官行事可為鑒戒者，令誦習之。

translations.literal: He instructed at the Inner Calligraphy Hall, compiled from earlier histories eunuch conduct that could serve as warnings, and had them recited and studied.
translations.idiomatic: He taught at the Inner Calligraphy Hall, compiled from earlier histories episodes of eunuch conduct that could serve as warnings, and had them recited and studied.

sentences.zh: 《世宗實錄》成，進修撰。

translations.literal: When the Veritable Records of Emperor Shizong were completed, he was promoted to Senior Compiler.
translations.idiomatic: When the Veritable Records of Emperor Shizong were completed, he was promoted to Senior Compiler.

sentences.zh: 萬歷五年，張居正奪情，杖諸諫者。

translations.literal: In Wanli 5, Zhang Juzheng declined mourning leave; those who remonstrated were beaten with the cane.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Wanli, Zhang Juzheng declined mourning leave, and those who remonstrated were beaten with the cane.

sentences.zh: 鳳翔不平，誦言於朝，編纂章奏，盡載諸諫疏。

translations.literal: Fengxiang was displeased; he spoke openly at court, and when compiling memorials he fully recorded all remonstrances.
translations.idiomatic: Fengxiang took offense and spoke openly at court; when compiling memorials he included every remonstrance in full.

sentences.zh: 及居正二子會試，示意，鳳翔峻卻之。

translations.literal: When Juzheng's two sons took the metropolitan examination, he made his wishes known; Fengxiang sternly refused.
translations.idiomatic: When Juzheng's two sons took the provincial examination, he made his wishes known; Fengxiang sternly refused.

sentences.zh: 當主南畿試，以王篆欲私其子，復謝不往。

translations.literal: When he was to preside over the southern capital region examination, because Wang Zhuan wished to favor his own son, he again declined and did not go.
translations.idiomatic: When he was to preside over the southern capital region examination and Wang Zhuan wished to favor his own son, Fengxiang again declined and did not go.

sentences.zh: 屢遷南京國子祭酒。

translations.literal: After repeated promotions he became Chancellor of the Nanjing Imperial Academy.
translations.idiomatic: After several promotions he became Chancellor of the Nanjing Imperial Academy.

sentences.zh: 省母歸，起補北監。

translations.literal: He went home to visit his mother, then was recalled to fill a post at the northern academy.
translations.idiomatic: He went home to visit his mother, then was recalled to fill a post at the northern academy.

sentences.zh: 時方較刻《十三經註疏》，鳳翔言：「頃陛下去《貞觀政要》，進講《禮經》，甚善。

translations.literal: At that time they were proofreading and printing the Commentaries on the Thirteen Classics. Fengxiang said: "Recently Your Majesty set aside the Essentials of Governance of the Zhenguan Era and advanced to lecturing on the Classic of Rites—this is very good.
translations.idiomatic: At that time they were proofreading and printing the Commentaries on the Thirteen Classics. Fengxiang said, "Your Majesty recently set aside the Essentials of Governance of the Zhenguan Era and took up lecturing on the Classic of Rites—this is very good.

sentences.zh: 陛下讀曾子論孝曰敬父母遺體，則當思珍護聖躬。

translations.literal: When Your Majesty reads Zengzi's discourse on filial piety, which says one must honor the body one's parents bequeathed, then You should consider cherishing and guarding Your sacred person.
translations.idiomatic: When Your Majesty reads Zengzi's discourse on filial piety—how one must honor the body one's parents bequeathed—You should consider cherishing and guarding Your sacred person.

sentences.zh: 誦《學記》言學然後知不足，則當思緝熙聖學。

translations.literal: When You recite the Record of Learning, which says that only through study does one know one's insufficiencies, then You should consider brightening and advancing Your sacred learning.
translations.idiomatic: When You recite the Record of Learning, which says that only through study does one know one's insufficiencies, You should consider brightening and advancing Your sacred learning.

sentences.zh: 察《月令》篇以四時敷政、法天行健，則可見聖治之當勤勵。

translations.literal: When You examine the Monthly Ordinances, how the four seasons distribute governance and imitate Heaven's vigorous course, then You can see that sage governance should be diligently exerted.
translations.idiomatic: When You examine the Monthly Ordinances, how the seasons distribute governance and imitate Heaven's vigorous course, You can see that sage governance demands diligent exertion.

sentences.zh: 繹《世子》篇陳保傅之教、齒學之儀，則可見皇儲之當早建豫教。」

translations.literal: When You expound the chapter on the Heir Apparent, which sets forth the tutelage of guardians and tutors and the rites of learning by age, then You can see that the imperial heir should early receive preparatory instruction.
translations.idiomatic: When You expound the chapter on the Heir Apparent, which sets forth the tutelage of guardians and tutors and the rites of learning by age, You can see that the imperial heir should early receive preparatory instruction.

sentences.zh: 疏入，報聞。

translations.literal: The memorial was submitted; acknowledgement was returned.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was submitted; acknowledgement was returned.

sentences.zh: 尋擢禮部右侍郎。

translations.literal: Soon he was promoted to Vice Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was promoted to Vice Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 洮、河告警，抗疏言：「多事之秋，陛下宜屏遊宴，親政事，以實圖安攘。

translations.literal: Alarm came from the Tao and Yellow River regions. He submitted a remonstrance saying: "In this season of many affairs, Your Majesty should set aside pleasure and banquets, attend personally to government, and with real action seek to pacify and repel the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: Alarm came from the Tao and Yellow River regions. He submitted a remonstrance saying, "In this season of many troubles, Your Majesty should set aside pleasure and banquets, attend to affairs of state, and with real action seek to pacify the realm and repel the enemy.

sentences.zh: 為今大計，惟用人、理財二端。

translations.literal: For the present grand plan, only two matters matter: employing men and managing finances.
translations.idiomatic: For the present grand strategy, only two things matter: employing men and managing finances.

sentences.zh: 宋臣有言：『平居無極言敢諫之臣，則臨難無敵愾致命之士。』

translations.literal: A Song minister once said: "In peaceful times, if there are no ministers who speak to the utmost and dare to remonstrate, then in crisis there will be no men who hate the enemy and give their lives."
translations.idiomatic: A Song minister once said, "In peaceful times, if there are no ministers who speak boldly and dare to remonstrate, then in crisis there will be no men who hate the enemy and give their lives."

sentences.zh: 鄒元標直聲勁節，銓司特擬召用。

translations.literal: Zou Yuanbiao has an upright reputation and firm integrity; the Board of Appointments specially proposed to summon and employ him.
translations.idiomatic: Zou Yuanbiao is known for upright reputation and firm integrity; the Board of Appointments specially proposed to summon and employ him.

sentences.zh: 其他建言遷謫，如潘士藻、孫如法亦擬量移，而疏皆中寢。

translations.literal: Others who had offered counsel and been transferred or demoted—such as Pan Shizao and Sun Rufa—were also proposed for gradual reassignment, yet every memorial was shelved midway.
translations.idiomatic: Others who had offered counsel and been transferred or demoted—such as Pan Shizao and Sun Rufa—were also proposed for gradual reassignment, yet every memorial was shelved midway.

sentences.zh: 士氣日摧，言路日塞。

translations.literal: Official morale daily withers; the avenue of speech daily narrows.
translations.idiomatic: Official morale daily withers; the avenue of speech daily narrows.

sentences.zh: 平居只懷祿養交，臨難孰肯捐軀為國家盡力哉？

translations.literal: In peaceful times they only cherish salary and cultivate connections—when crisis comes, who will willingly sacrifice their body and strive with all their strength for the state?
translations.idiomatic: In peace they hold to salary and cultivate connections—when crisis comes, who will willingly sacrifice himself and strive for the state?

sentences.zh: 昔宋藝祖欲積縑二百萬易遼人首，太宗移內藏上供物為用兵養士之資。

translations.literal: Formerly Emperor Taizu of Song wished to amass two million bolts of silk to buy a Khitan head; Emperor Taizong diverted tribute goods from the inner treasury to fund war and support troops.
translations.idiomatic: Long ago, Emperor Taizu of Song wished to amass two million bolts of silk to buy the head of a Khitan; Emperor Taizong diverted tribute goods from the inner treasury to fund war and support troops.

sentences.zh: 今戶部歲進二十萬，初非舊額，積成常供。

translations.literal: Today the Ministry of Revenue annually delivers two hundred thousand—originally no part of the old quota, yet it has accumulated into regular tribute.
translations.idiomatic: Today the Ministry of Revenue annually delivers two hundred thousand—originally no part of the old quota, yet it has hardened into regular tribute.

sentences.zh: 陛下富有四海，奈何自營私蓄！

translations.literal: Your Majesty is rich with all within the four seas—why hoard a private fortune!
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty possesses all beneath Heaven—why hoard a private fortune!

sentences.zh: 竊見都城寺觀，丹碧熒煌，梵剎之供奉，齋醮之祈禳，何一不糜內帑。

translations.literal: I have privately seen the temples and monasteries of the capital, brilliant in cinnabar and azure—the offerings to Buddhist shrines, the fasting rites and prayers of supplication—none fail to drain the inner treasury.
translations.idiomatic: I have seen the temples and monasteries of the capital, brilliant in cinnabar and azure—the offerings to Buddhist shrines, the fasting rites and prayers of supplication—none fail to drain the inner treasury.

sentences.zh: 與其要福於冥漠之鬼神，孰若廣施於孑遺之赤子。」

translations.literal: Rather than seeking blessings from ghosts in the dark void, would it not be better to bestow widely upon orphaned children left in the land?
translations.idiomatic: Rather than seeking blessings from ghosts in the dark void, would it not be better to bestow widely upon orphaned children left in the land?

sentences.zh: 帝不能用。

translations.literal: The emperor could not adopt his counsel.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor could not adopt his counsel.

sentences.zh: 廷臣爭建儲，久未得命，帝諭閣臣以明春舉行。

translations.literal: Court ministers struggled over establishing the heir; for long they received no decree. The emperor told the Grand Secretaries that it would be carried out the following spring.
translations.idiomatic: Court ministers struggled over establishing the heir; for long they received no decree. The emperor told the Grand Secretaries that it would be carried out the following spring.

sentences.zh: 大學士王家屏出語禮部，鳳翔與尚書於慎行、左侍郎李長春以冊立儀上。

translations.literal: Grand Secretary Wang Jiaping spoke to the Ministry of Rites outside court; Fengxiang, together with Minister Yu Shenxing and Left Vice Minister Li Changchun, submitted the investiture rites for establishing the heir.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Secretary Wang Jiaping spoke to the Ministry of Rites outside court; Fengxiang, together with Minister Yu Shenxing and Vice Minister Li Changchun, submitted the investiture rites for establishing the heir.

sentences.zh: 帝怒，俱奪俸，意復變。

translations.literal: The emperor grew angry; all had their salaries confiscated, and his intention shifted again.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor grew angry; all had their salaries confiscated, and his intention shifted again.

sentences.zh: 鳳翔又疏爭，不報，遂請告去。

translations.literal: Fengxiang again remonstrated in a memorial; there was no response, and he requested leave and departed.
translations.idiomatic: Fengxiang remonstrated again; there was no response, and he requested leave and departed.

sentences.zh: 二十年，禮部左侍郎韓世能去，張一桂未任而卒，復起鳳翔代之。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year, Left Vice Minister of Rites Han Shineng departed; Zhang Yigui died before assuming his post, and Fengxiang was recalled to replace him.
translations.idiomatic: In the twentieth year, Vice Minister Han Shineng of Rites left office; Zhang Yigui died before assuming his post, and Fengxiang was recalled to replace him.

sentences.zh: 尋改吏部，拜南京禮部尚書。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to the Ministry of Personnel and appointed Minister of Rites at Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was transferred to the Ministry of Personnel and appointed Minister of Rites at Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 以養親歸。

translations.literal: He returned home to care for his parents.
translations.idiomatic: He returned home to care for his parents.

sentences.zh: 再起故官，力以親老辭。

translations.literal: When recalled to his former post, he firmly declined on grounds that his parents were aged.
translations.idiomatic: When recalled to his former post, he firmly declined on grounds that his parents were aged.

sentences.zh: 久之母卒，遂不出，卒於家。

translations.literal: After a long time his mother died; he then did not go out and died at home.
translations.idiomatic: After a time his mother died; he never went out again and died at home.

sentences.zh: 天啟初，謚文簡。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianqi he was given the posthumous title Wen Jian.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Tianqi he was given the posthumous title Wen Jian.

sentences.zh: 世能，字存良，長洲人。

translations.literal: Shineng, courtesy name Cunliang, was a man of Changzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Shineng, courtesy name Cunliang, was a native of Changzhou.

sentences.zh: 鳳翔同年進士。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination in the same year as Fengxiang.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in the same year as Fengxiang.

sentences.zh: 由庶吉士授編修。

translations.literal: From Hanlin Bachelor he was appointed Compiler.
translations.idiomatic: From Hanlin Bachelor he was appointed Compiler.

sentences.zh: 與修世宗、穆宗寶實《錄》，充經筵日講官。

translations.literal: He participated in compiling the Veritable Records of Emperors Shizong and Muzong and served as daily lecturer at the Classics Colloquium.
translations.idiomatic: He participated in compiling the Veritable Records of Emperors Shizong and Muzong and served as daily lecturer at the Classics Colloquium.

sentences.zh: 歷侍讀、祭酒、禮部侍郎、教習庶吉士。

translations.literal: He successively served as Reader, Chancellor, Vice Minister of Rites, and Instructor of Hanlin Bachelors.
translations.idiomatic: He successively served as Reader, Chancellor, Vice Minister of Rites, and Instructor of Hanlin Bachelors.

sentences.zh: 館閣文字，是科為最盛。

translations.literal: Among the literary men of the academies, his cohort was the most distinguished.
translations.idiomatic: Among the literary men of the academies, his cohort was the most distinguished.

sentences.zh: 世能嘗使朝鮮，贈遺一無所受。

translations.literal: Shineng once served as envoy to Korea and accepted none of the gifts offered him.
translations.idiomatic: Shineng once served as envoy to Korea and accepted none of the gifts offered him.

sentences.zh: 余繼登，字世用，交河人。

translations.literal: Yu Jideng, courtesy name Shiyong, was a man of Jiaohe.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Jideng, courtesy name Shiyong, was a native of Jiaohe.

sentences.zh: 萬歷五年進士。

translations.literal: In Wanli 5 he became a jinshi.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Wanli he became a jinshi.

sentences.zh: 改庶吉士，授檢討。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Hanlin Bachelor and appointed Reviser.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Hanlin Bachelor and appointed Reviser.

sentences.zh: 與修《會典》成，進修撰，直講經筵。

translations.literal: When work on the Collected Statutes was completed, he was promoted to Senior Compiler and served lecturing at the Classics Colloquium.
translations.idiomatic: When work on the Collected Statutes was completed, he was promoted to Senior Compiler and served lecturing at the Classics Colloquium.

sentences.zh: 尋進右中允，充日講官。

translations.literal: Soon he was promoted to Right Vice Director and served as daily lecturer.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was promoted to Right Vice Director and served as daily lecturer.

sentences.zh: 時講筵久輟，侍臣無所納忠。

translations.literal: At that time the lecture sessions had long been suspended; attendant ministers had no avenue to offer loyal counsel.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the lecture sessions had long been suspended; attendant ministers had no avenue to offer loyal counsel.

sentences.zh: 繼登與同官馮琦共進《通鑒》講義，傅以時政缺失。

translations.literal: Jideng and his colleague Feng Qi jointly submitted lectures on the Comprehensive Mirror, attaching commentary on lapses in current policy.
translations.idiomatic: Jideng and his colleague Feng Qi jointly submitted lectures on the Comprehensive Mirror, attaching commentary on lapses in current policy.

sentences.zh: 歷少詹事兼侍讀學士，充正史副總裁。

translations.literal: He served successively as Junior Guardian and Concurrent Reader-in-waiting, and as Associate Chief Editor of the official history.
translations.idiomatic: He served successively as Junior Guardian and Concurrent Reader-in-waiting, and as Associate Chief Editor of the official history.

sentences.zh: 已，擢詹事，掌翰林院。

translations.literal: Thereafter he was promoted to Grand Guardian and took charge of the Hanlin Academy.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter he was promoted to Grand Guardian and took charge of the Hanlin Academy.

sentences.zh: 兩宮災，偕諸講官引《洪範五行傳》切諫。

translations.literal: When fire struck both palaces, he joined the other lecturers in citing the treatise on the Five Processes from the Hong Fan to offer pointed remonstrance.
translations.idiomatic: When fire struck both palaces, he joined the other lecturers in citing the treatise on the Five Processes from the Hong Fan to offer pointed remonstrance.

sentences.zh: 不報。

translations.literal: No response was given.
translations.idiomatic: No response was given.

sentences.zh: 進禮部右侍郎。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Vice Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Vice Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 二十六年，以左侍郎攝部事。

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth year he served as acting head of the ministry in his capacity as Left Vice Minister.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-sixth year he served as acting head of the ministry in his capacity as Left Vice Minister.

sentences.zh: 陜西、山西地震，南都雷火，西寧鐘自鳴，紹興地湧血。

translations.literal: Earthquakes struck Shaanxi and Shanxi; lightning fire in the southern capital; a bell in Xining rang of itself; blood welled from the ground in Shaoxing.
translations.idiomatic: Earthquakes struck Shaanxi and Shanxi; lightning fire in the southern capital; a bell in Xining rang of itself; blood welled from the ground in Shaoxing.

sentences.zh: 繼登於歲終類奏，因請罷一切誅求開采之害民者。

translations.literal: In his year-end summary memorial Jideng asked that all levies and mining operations harmful to the people be abolished.
translations.idiomatic: In his year-end summary memorial Jideng asked that all levies and mining operations harmful to the people be abolished.

sentences.zh: 時不能用。

translations.literal: At the time his counsel could not be adopted.
translations.idiomatic: At the time his counsel could not be adopted.

sentences.zh: 雷擊太廟樹，復請帝躬郊祀、廟享，冊立元子，停礦稅，撤中使。

translations.literal: Lightning struck a tree in the Imperial Ancestral Temple. He again asked the emperor to personally perform suburban sacrifice and temple rites, invest the eldest son, halt mining taxes, and withdraw the eunuch commissioners.
translations.idiomatic: Lightning struck a tree in the Imperial Ancestral Temple. He again asked the emperor to personally perform suburban sacrifice and temple rites, invest the eldest son, halt mining taxes, and withdraw the eunuch commissioners.

sentences.zh: 帝優詔報聞而已。

translations.literal: The emperor issued a gracious edict acknowledging receipt—and nothing more.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor issued a gracious edict acknowledging receipt—and nothing more.

sentences.zh: 旋擢本部尚書。

translations.literal: Soon he was promoted to Minister of his own ministry.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was promoted to Minister of his own ministry.

sentences.zh: 時將討播州楊應龍。

translations.literal: At that time they were about to campaign against Yang Yinglong of Bozhou.
translations.idiomatic: At that time they were about to campaign against Yang Yinglong of Bozhou.

sentences.zh: 繼登請罷四川礦稅，以佐兵食。

translations.literal: Jideng asked that Sichuan mining taxes be abolished to help supply the army.
translations.idiomatic: Jideng asked that Sichuan mining taxes be abolished to help supply the army.

sentences.zh: 復上言：「頃者星躔失度，水旱為沴，太白晝見，天不和也。

translations.literal: He submitted again: "Recently the stars have strayed from their courses, flood and drought have brought calamity, and Venus has appeared by day—Heaven is out of harmony.
translations.idiomatic: He submitted again, "Recently the stars have strayed from their courses, flood and drought have brought calamity, and Venus has appeared by day—Heaven is out of harmony.

sentences.zh: 鑿山開礦，裂地求砂，致狄道山崩地震，地不和也。

translations.literal: Mountains are drilled and mines opened, the earth is torn to seek ore, causing landslides and earthquakes at Didao—the earth is out of harmony.
translations.idiomatic: Mountains are drilled and mines opened, the earth is torn to seek ore, causing landslides and earthquakes at Didao—the earth is out of harmony.

sentences.zh: 閭閻窮困，更加誅求，帑藏空虛，復責珠寶，奸民蟻聚，中使鴟張，中外壅隔，上下不交，人不和也。

translations.literal: Lane and ward are exhausted yet levies grow heavier; the treasury is empty yet pearls and gems are demanded; wicked men swarm like ants; eunuch commissioners rage like owls; court and country are blocked off; above and below do not connect—humanity is out of harmony.
translations.idiomatic: Lane and ward are exhausted yet levies grow heavier; the treasury is empty yet pearls and gems are demanded; wicked men swarm like ants; eunuch commissioners rage like owls; court and country are blocked off; above and below do not connect—humanity is out of harmony.

sentences.zh: 戾氣凝而不散，怨毒結而成形，陵谷變遷，高卑易位，是為陰乘陽、邪幹正、下叛上之象。

translations.literal: Malice congeals yet will not disperse; grievous poison knots and takes shape; hills and valleys shift; high and low exchange places—these are signs of yin overwhelming yang, wickedness obstructing the upright, and those below rebelling against those above.
translations.idiomatic: Malice congeals yet will not disperse; grievous poison knots and takes shape; hills and valleys shift; high and low exchange places—these are signs of yin overwhelming yang, wickedness obstructing the upright, and those below rebelling against those above.

sentences.zh: 臣子不能感動君父，言愈數愈厭，故天以非常之變，警悟陛下，尚可恬然不為意乎？」

translations.literal: We subjects cannot move our ruler; the more we speak the more we are despised—so Heaven uses these extraordinary changes to awaken Your Majesty. Can You still remain untroubled and indifferent?
translations.idiomatic: We subjects cannot move our ruler; the more we speak the more we are despised—so Heaven uses these extraordinary changes to awaken Your Majesty. Can You still remain untroubled and indifferent?

sentences.zh: 帝不省。

translations.literal: The emperor took no heed.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor took no heed.

sentences.zh: 繼登自署部事，請元子冊立冠婚。

translations.literal: While signing documents for the ministry himself, Jideng petitioned for the eldest son's investiture, capping, and marriage.
translations.idiomatic: While signing documents for the ministry himself, Jideng petitioned for the eldest son's investiture, capping, and marriage.

sentences.zh: 疏累上，以不得請，郁郁成疾。

translations.literal: He submitted memorial after memorial; denied his request, he sank into illness from gloom.
translations.idiomatic: He submitted memorial after memorial; denied his request, he sank into illness from gloom.

sentences.zh: 每言及，輒流涕曰：「大禮不舉，吾禮官死不瞑目！」

translations.literal: Whenever the matter arose he would weep and say: "If this great rite is not performed, I as Minister of Rites will not close my eyes in death!
translations.idiomatic: Whenever the matter arose he would weep and say, "If this great rite is not performed, I as Minister of Rites will not close my eyes in death!

sentences.zh: 病滿三月，連章乞休，不許。

translations.literal: When his illness had lasted three months, he submitted repeated memorials requesting retirement; permission was denied.
translations.idiomatic: When his illness had lasted three months, he submitted repeated memorials requesting retirement; permission was denied.

sentences.zh: 請停俸，亦不許。

translations.literal: He asked to have his salary suspended; that too was denied.
translations.idiomatic: He asked to have his salary suspended; that too was denied.

sentences.zh: 竟卒於官。

translations.literal: In the end he died in office.
translations.idiomatic: In the end he died in office.

sentences.zh: 贈太子少保，謚文恪。

translations.literal: He was posthumously enfeoffed as Junior Mentor of the Heir Apparent and given the posthumous title Wen Ke.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously enfeoffed as Junior Mentor of the Heir Apparent and given the posthumous title Wen Ke.

sentences.zh: 繼登樸直慎密，寡言笑。

translations.literal: Jideng was plain, upright, cautious, and reserved, seldom given to speech or laughter.
translations.idiomatic: Jideng was plain, upright, cautious, and reserved, seldom given to speech or laughter.

sentences.zh: 當大事，言議侃侃。

translations.literal: When great matters were at stake, his words flowed freely and confidently.
translations.idiomatic: When great matters were at stake, his words flowed freely and confidently.

sentences.zh: 居家廉約。

translations.literal: At home he lived frugally.
translations.idiomatic: At home he lived frugally.

sentences.zh: 學士曾朝節嘗過其裏，蓬蒿滿徑。

translations.literal: Academician Zeng Chaojie once visited his home; wild grass filled the path.
translations.idiomatic: Academician Zeng Chaojie once visited his home; wild grass filled the path.

sentences.zh: 及病革，視之，擁粗布衾，羊毳覆足而已。

translations.literal: When his illness became critical, one looked in on him: he lay under a coarse cloth quilt, with nothing but sheep's wool over his feet.
translations.idiomatic: When his illness became critical, one looked in on him: he lay under a coarse cloth quilt, with nothing but sheep's wool over his feet.

sentences.zh: 幼子應諸生試，夫人請為一言，終不可。

translations.literal: When his youngest son was to take the licentiate examination, his wife asked him to put in a word; he would not.
translations.idiomatic: When his youngest son was to take the licentiate examination, his wife asked him to put in a word; he would not.

sentences.zh: 馮琦，字用韞，臨朐人。

translations.literal: Feng Qi, courtesy name Yongyun, was a man of Linqu.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Qi, courtesy name Yongyun, was a native of Linqu.

sentences.zh: 幼穎敏絕人。

translations.literal: From childhood he was exceptionally quick and perceptive beyond others.
translations.idiomatic: From childhood he was exceptionally quick and perceptive.

sentences.zh: 年十九，舉萬歷五年進士，改庶吉士，授編修。

translations.literal: At nineteen he passed the jinshi examination in Wanli 5, was transferred to Hanlin Bachelor, and was appointed Compiler.
translations.idiomatic: At nineteen he passed the jinshi examination in the fifth year of Wanli, was transferred to Hanlin Bachelor, and was appointed Compiler.

sentences.zh: 預修《會典》成，進侍講，充日講官，歷庶子。

translations.literal: When participation in compiling the Collected Statutes was completed, he was promoted to Lecturer-in-waiting, served as daily lecturer, and served successively as Tutor.
translations.idiomatic: When participation in compiling the Collected Statutes was completed, he was promoted to Lecturer-in-waiting, served as daily lecturer, and served successively as Tutor.

sentences.zh: 三王並封議起，移書王錫爵力爭之。

translations.literal: When debate arose over enfeoffing three princes simultaneously, he wrote to Wang Xizhi and argued against it with all his force.
translations.idiomatic: When debate arose over enfeoffing three princes simultaneously, he wrote to Wang Xizhi and argued against it with all his force.

sentences.zh: 進少詹事，掌翰林院事。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Junior Guardian and took charge of Hanlin Academy affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Junior Guardian and took charge of Hanlin Academy affairs.

sentences.zh: 遷禮部右侍郎，改吏部。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Right Vice Minister of Rites, then reassigned to the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Right Vice Minister of Rites, then transferred to the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 蒞政勤敏，力抑營競，尚書李戴倚重之。

translations.literal: In administering affairs he was diligent and quick, forcefully repressing office-seeking and rivalry; Minister Li Dai relied heavily on him.
translations.idiomatic: He administered affairs with diligence and dispatch, forcefully curbing corrupt competition for office, and Minister Li Dai came to rely on him heavily.

sentences.zh: 二十七年九月，太白、太陰同見於午；

translations.literal: In the ninth month of the twenty-seventh year, Venus and the Moon both appeared at the noon meridian;
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of Wanli 27, Venus and the Moon both appeared together at the southern meridian;

sentences.zh: 又狄道山崩，平地湧大小山五。

translations.literal: Moreover at Didao mountains collapsed, and from level ground five large and small hills welled up.
translations.idiomatic: At Didao, mountains collapsed and five hills of various sizes rose from level ground.

sentences.zh: 琦草疏，偕尚書戴上言：

translations.literal: Qi drafted a memorial and jointly submitted with Minister Dai, stating:
translations.idiomatic: Feng Qi drafted a memorial and, together with Minister Li Dai, submitted it, saying:

sentences.zh: 近見太陰經天，太白晝見，已為極異。

translations.literal: Recently we have seen the Moon cross the heavens and Venus appear by day—these are already extreme anomalies.
translations.idiomatic: Recently the Moon has crossed the heavens and Venus has appeared by day—already signs of the gravest anomaly.

sentences.zh: 至山陷成谷，地湧成山，則自開辟以來，惟唐垂拱中有之，而今再見也。

translations.literal: As for mountains sinking to become valleys and ground surging to become hills, since the creation of the world this has occurred only in the Tang Chuigong era—and now we see it again.
translations.idiomatic: As for mountains sinking into valleys and the earth surging up into hills, such things have occurred only once since antiquity, during the Tang Chuigong reign—and now we see them again.

sentences.zh: 竊惟上天無私，惟民是聽。

translations.literal: I venture to consider that Heaven is without partiality and listens only to the people.
translations.idiomatic: I believe Heaven shows no partiality and heeds only the voice of the people.

sentences.zh: 欲承天意，當順民心。

translations.literal: To receive Heaven's intent, one must follow the people's hearts.
translations.idiomatic: To answer Heaven's will, you must align with the people's hearts.

sentences.zh: 比來天下賦額，視二十年以前，十增其四。

translations.literal: Recently the empire's tax quotas, compared with twenty years ago, have increased by four in every ten.
translations.idiomatic: In recent years the empire's tax quotas have risen forty percent over what they were twenty years ago.

sentences.zh: 而民戶殷足者，則十減其五。

translations.literal: Yet households that were prosperous and well-off have diminished by five in every ten.
