translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile, prosperous households have dwindled by half.

sentences.zh: 東征西討，蕭然苦兵。

translations.literal: Campaigns east and west have left the land desolate and the people worn by war.
translations.idiomatic: Campaigns east and west have left the realm desolate and the people worn down by war.

sentences.zh: 自礦稅使出，而民間之苦更甚。

translations.literal: Since mining-tax commissioners were sent out, the people's suffering has grown worse still.
translations.idiomatic: Since mining-tax commissioners were dispatched, the common people's suffering has grown worse still.

sentences.zh: 加以水旱蝗災，流離載道，畿輔近地，盜賊公行，此非細故也。

translations.literal: Added to this are flood, drought, and locust disasters; the displaced fill the roads; near the capital region bandits roam openly—this is no minor matter.
translations.idiomatic: On top of this come flood, drought, and locust plagues; refugees choke the highways; even near the capital bandits operate openly—this is no small matter.

sentences.zh: 諸中使銜命而出，所隨奸徒，動以千百。

translations.literal: Eunuch commissioners go forth bearing imperial commands, and the wicked followers who accompany them often number in the hundreds and thousands.
translations.idiomatic: Eunuch commissioners issued with imperial authority go forth accompanied by ruffians numbering in the hundreds and thousands.

sentences.zh: 陛下欲通商，而彼專困商；

translations.literal: Your Majesty wishes to promote trade, yet they specialize in oppressing merchants;
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty wishes to promote commerce, yet they devote themselves to harassing merchants;

sentences.zh: 陛下欲愛民，而彼專害民。

translations.literal: Your Majesty wishes to cherish the people, yet they specialize in harming the people.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty wishes to cherish the people, yet they devote themselves to harming them.

sentences.zh: 蓋近日神奸有二：其一工伺上意，具有成奏，假武弁上之；

translations.literal: Generally speaking, there are two kinds of diabolical villains lately: one skilled at watching the sovereign's intentions, who prepares finished memorials and submits them through military officers;
translations.idiomatic: There are two kinds of villainous schemers at work. One watches the throne's inclinations, drafts ready-made memorials, and submits them through military officers;

sentences.zh: 其一務剝小民，畫有成謀，假中官行之。

translations.literal: The other is devoted to stripping the common people, who devises ready-made schemes and carries them out through palace eunuchs.
translations.idiomatic: The other sets out to plunder the common people, lays ready-made plots, and executes them through palace eunuchs.

sentences.zh: 運機如鬼蜮，取財盡錙銖。

translations.literal: Their scheming is like demons; they extract wealth down to the last cash.
translations.idiomatic: They scheme like demons in the dark and extract wealth down to the last penny.

sentences.zh: 遠近同嗟，貧富交困。

translations.literal: Near and far alike sigh in grief; rich and poor alike are trapped in hardship.
translations.idiomatic: Near and far alike cry out in despair; rich and poor alike are mired in hardship.

sentences.zh: 貧者家無儲蓄，惟恃經營。

translations.literal: The poor have no savings at home and rely solely on daily labor.
translations.idiomatic: The poor keep no savings and depend entirely on their daily labor for survival.

sentences.zh: 但奪其數錢之利，已絕其一日之生。

translations.literal: Seize from them profits of a few coins and you already cut off their livelihood for a day.
translations.idiomatic: Strip them of a few coins' profit and you cut off their means to live for a day.

sentences.zh: 至於富民，更蒙毒害。

translations.literal: As for the wealthy, they suffer even greater harm.
translations.idiomatic: The wealthy suffer even worse abuse.

sentences.zh: 或陷以漏稅竊礦，或誣之販鹽盜木。

translations.literal: Some are entrapped on charges of evading taxes or illicit mining; others are accused of peddling salt or stealing timber.
translations.idiomatic: Some are framed for evading taxes or illicit mining; others are accused of illegal salt trade or timber theft.

sentences.zh: 布成詭計，聲勢赫然。

translations.literal: When their schemes are laid, their authority blazes forth.
translations.idiomatic: They lay their traps and thunder in with terrifying authority.

sentences.zh: 及其得財，寂然無事。

translations.literal: Once they obtain the money, all falls silent as if nothing happened.
translations.idiomatic: Once they extract the money, everything falls silent as though nothing had happened.

sentences.zh: 小民累足屏息，無地得容。

translations.literal: Common people walk on tiptoe and hold their breath, with nowhere to find refuge.
translations.idiomatic: Common people tiptoe around in fear, with nowhere to turn.

sentences.zh: 利歸群奸，怨萃朝寧。

translations.literal: Profit goes to the pack of villains; resentment gathers at the imperial court.
translations.idiomatic: The profit falls to a pack of villains; resentment concentrates on the throne.

sentences.zh: 夫以刺骨之窮，抱傷心之痛，一呼則易動，一動則難安。

translations.literal: For people in bone-piercing poverty nursing heart-breaking pain, one call and they are easily stirred; once stirred, they are hard to pacify.
translations.idiomatic: People ground down to the bone and nursing deep grievance are easily roused by a single cry—and once roused, they are hard to pacify.

sentences.zh: 今日猶承平，民已洶洶，脫有風塵之警，天下誰可保信者？

translations.literal: Today we are still at peace yet the people are already in uproar; if alarms of war should arise, who under Heaven can be trusted to remain loyal?
translations.idiomatic: Even now, in a time still called peaceful, the people are already restive; should war break out, who in the empire could be counted on to stay loyal?

sentences.zh: 夫哱拜誅，關白死，此皆募民丁以為兵，用民財以為餉。

translations.literal: When Bo Bai was executed and the Kampaku died—these achievements were won by conscripting commoners as soldiers and spending the people's wealth as provisions.
translations.idiomatic: The defeats of Bo Bai and the Kampaku were won only by conscripting commoners as soldiers and spending the people's wealth on provisions.

sentences.zh: 若一方窮民倡亂，而四面應之，於何征兵，於何取餉哉！

translations.literal: If destitute people in one region rise in rebellion and the four quarters respond, from where will you conscript troops, from where draw provisions?
translations.idiomatic: If the destitute in one corner rise in rebellion and the rest of the empire answers, where will you find soldiers, and where will you find provisions?

sentences.zh: 陛下試遣忠實親信之人，采訪都城內外，閭巷歌謠，令一一聞奏，則民之怨苦，居然可睹。

translations.literal: Your Majesty might try sending loyal and trusted men to inquire within and outside the capital into lane and ward ballads, having each report heard—then the people's resentment and suffering would plainly be visible.
translations.idiomatic: Send loyal and trusted men to gather the street songs of the capital, inside and out, and have each report brought to you—the people's grievous suffering would then stand plain before your eyes.

sentences.zh: 天心仁愛，明示咎徵，誠欲陛下翻然改悟，坐弭禍亂。

translations.literal: Heaven's heart is benevolent; it clearly displays signs of blame, truly wishing Your Majesty to turn about in sudden awakening and quell disaster and rebellion while seated on the throne.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven, in its benevolence, has shown clear signs of warning, wishing only that Your Majesty would turn about in sudden awakening and quell disaster without leaving the throne.

sentences.zh: 乃禮部修省之章未蒙批答，而奸民搜括之奏又見允行。

translations.literal: Yet the Ministry of Rites' memorial on self-examination has not received a written response, while villains' memorials for exactions have again been approved for execution.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the Ministry of Rites' call for self-examination has gone unanswered, while memorials from scoundrels demanding exactions have again been approved.

sentences.zh: 如納何其賢妄說，令遍解天下無礙官銀。

translations.literal: For example, Na Qixian's reckless proposal ordering the seizure throughout the empire of all unencumbered official silver.
translations.idiomatic: Na Qixian's reckless proposal, for example, orders the seizure throughout the empire of all surplus official silver.

sentences.zh: 夫四方錢谷，皆有定額，無礙雲者，意蓋指經費羨余。

translations.literal: Revenue and grain throughout the four directions all have fixed quotas; "unencumbered" presumably refers to surplus from budgeted expenditures.
translations.idiomatic: Revenues throughout the empire all have fixed quotas; "surplus" can only mean funds left over from budgeted expenditures.

sentences.zh: 近者征調頻仍，正額猶逋，何從得羨？

translations.literal: Lately requisitions have been frequent; the regular quotas are still in arrears—from where can surplus come?
translations.idiomatic: Requisitions have lately come one after another; even regular quotas remain unpaid—how can there be any surplus?

sentences.zh: 此令一下，趣督嚴急，必將分公帑以充獻。

translations.literal: Once this order is issued, urgings and supervision will be severe; offices will inevitably raid public treasuries to fill the tribute demanded.
translations.idiomatic: Once this order goes out, enforcement will be pitiless; officials will inevitably strip public treasuries to meet the tribute demanded.

sentences.zh: 經費罔措，還派民間，此事之必不可者也。

translations.literal: When budgetary funds cannot be managed, levies will be reassigned to the common people—this absolutely cannot be done.
translations.idiomatic: When official funds run out, the burden will be shifted onto the people—this simply must not be allowed.

sentences.zh: 又如仇世亨奏徐鼐掘墳一事，以理而論，烏有一墓藏黃金巨萬者？

translations.literal: Again, as in Qiu Shiheng's memorial about Xu Dai's tomb-robbing—as a matter of reason, how could a tomb contain gold in the tens of thousands?
translations.idiomatic: Consider Qiu Shiheng's memorial accusing Xu Dai of tomb-robbing—by any reasonable standard, what tomb holds gold in the tens of thousands?

sentences.zh: 借使有之，亦當下撫按核勘。

translations.literal: Even supposing there were, the provincial surveillance and administration commissioners below should first investigate and verify.
translations.idiomatic: Even if it were true, the provincial officials below should first investigate and verify.

sentences.zh: 先正其盜墓之罪，而後沒墓中之藏。

translations.literal: First establish the crime of tomb-robbing, then only afterward confiscate what lies in the tomb.
translations.idiomatic: First establish the crime of tomb-robbing, then—and only then—confiscate the tomb's contents.

sentences.zh: 未有罪狀未明，而先沒入貲財者也。

translations.literal: There has never been a case where property was confiscated before the charges were established.
translations.idiomatic: Property has never been confiscated before guilt has been established.

sentences.zh: 片紙朝入，嚴命夕傳，縱抱深冤，誰敢辨理？

translations.literal: A slip of paper enters the court in the morning; a stern order is transmitted by evening; even bearing deep injustice, who dares argue the case?
translations.idiomatic: A slip of paper arrives in the morning; a harsh order goes out by evening—even the deeply wronged dare not plead their case.

sentences.zh: 不但破此諸族，又將延禍多人。

translations.literal: This will not only ruin these clans but also spread calamity to many others.
translations.idiomatic: This will not only ruin these families but spread calamity to many others.

sentences.zh: 但有株連，立見敗滅。

translations.literal: Whenever implicated families are drawn in, ruin is immediate.
translations.idiomatic: Wherever guilt by association is invoked, ruin follows at once.

sentences.zh: 輦轂之下，尚須三覆，萬里之外，止據單詞，遂令狡猾之流，操生殺之柄。

translations.literal: Under the imperial chariot-wheels, threefold review is still required; ten thousand li away, on the strength of a single report, cunning characters are made to wield the power of life and death.
translations.idiomatic: Even at the emperor's doorstep, cases require triple review—yet ten thousand li away, a single accusation is enough to put the power of life and death in the hands of scheming thugs.

sentences.zh: 此風一倡，孰不效尤？

translations.literal: Once this practice is inaugurated, who will not imitate it?
translations.idiomatic: Once this practice is set in motion, who will not follow suit?

sentences.zh: 已同告緡之令，又開告密之端。

translations.literal: We already have an order like the Warring States "denunciation of hidden wealth," and now the door to secret denunciation is opened as well.
translations.idiomatic: We already have something like Emperor Wu's denunciation edicts, and now the door to secret denunciation has been opened as well.

sentences.zh: 臣等方欲陳訴，而奸人之奏又得旨矣。

translations.literal: We ministers were just about to state our grievances when villains' memorials again received imperial assent.
translations.idiomatic: We ministers were about to lodge our protests when another memorial from villains received imperial approval.

sentences.zh: 五日之內，搜取天下公私金銀已二百萬。

translations.literal: Within five days, public and private gold and silver seized throughout the empire already amounted to two million.
translations.idiomatic: Within five days, two million in public and private gold and silver had already been seized across the empire.

sentences.zh: 奸內生奸，例外創例。

translations.literal: Villainy breeds villainy within villainy; exceptions become new precedents.
translations.idiomatic: One abuse breeds the next; each exception becomes a new precedent.

sentences.zh: 臣等前猶望其日減，今更患其日增，不至民困財殫激大亂不止。

translations.literal: We ministers had earlier hoped this would diminish day by day; now we fear only that it will increase day by day, until the people are exhausted, resources depleted, and great rebellion is provoked without end.
translations.idiomatic: We had hoped these abuses would dwindle; now we fear only that they will grow, until the people are ruined, the treasury empty, and a great rebellion is provoked that will not stop.

sentences.zh: 伏望陛下穆然遠覽，亟與廷臣共圖修弭，無令海內赤子，結怨熙朝，千秋青史，貽譏聖德。

translations.literal: We bow and hope Your Majesty will contemplatively take a distant view, urgently join with court ministers to plan remedy and mitigation, and not allow the empire's common people to accumulate resentment against this glorious dynasty, or posterity's histories to record slurs upon sacred virtue.
translations.idiomatic: We beg Your Majesty to step back and take the long view, urgently join with your ministers to plan remedy, and not allow the common people to turn against this glorious dynasty—or allow history to record a stain upon your sacred virtue.

sentences.zh: 不報。

translations.literal: No response was given.
translations.idiomatic: No response was given.

sentences.zh: 尋轉左侍郎，拜禮部尚書。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to Left Vice Minister and appointed Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made Left Vice Minister and appointed Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 帝將冊立東宮，詔下期迫，中官掌司設監者以供費不給為詞。

translations.literal: The emperor was about to invest the heir apparent; the deadline for the edict was pressing; eunuchs in charge of the Directorate of Palace Accoutrements pleaded insufficient funds for the ceremony as their pretext.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor was about to invest the heir apparent, the edict's deadline pressed near; eunuchs of the Directorate of Palace Accoutrements claimed they lacked funds for the ceremony.

sentences.zh: 琦曰：「今日禮為重，不可與爭。」

translations.literal: Qi said: "Today ritual is paramount; we cannot contest this."
translations.idiomatic: Feng Qi said, "Today ritual takes priority; we must not quarrel over this."

sentences.zh: 其弟戶部主事瑗適輦餉銀四萬出都，琦立追還，給費，事乃克濟。

translations.literal: His younger brother Yuan, a Secretary in the Ministry of Revenue, happened to be escorting forty thousand taels of army pay out of the capital; Qi immediately had it recalled and provided the funds, and the affair was successfully accomplished.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Yuan, a secretary in the Ministry of Revenue, happened to be escorting forty thousand taels of silver out of the capital; Feng Qi immediately had it recalled and supplied the funds, and the ceremony was successfully carried out.

sentences.zh: 三十年，帝有疾，諭停礦稅，既而悔之。

translations.literal: In the thirtieth year the emperor fell ill and ordered a halt to mining taxes, but afterward regretted it.
translations.idiomatic: In Wanli 30 the emperor fell ill and ordered mining taxes halted, but later changed his mind.

sentences.zh: 琦與同列合疏爭，且請躬郊廟祭享，禦殿受朝，不納。

translations.literal: Qi joined colleagues in a joint memorial protesting, also asking that the emperor personally perform suburban and temple sacrifices and receive audiences in the hall—these were not accepted.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Qi and his colleagues submitted a joint memorial in protest, also asking the emperor to perform suburban and temple sacrifices in person and hold court audiences—these requests were rejected.

sentences.zh: 湖廣稅監陳奉以虐民撤還，會陜西黃河竭，琦言遼東高淮、山東陳增、廣東李鳳、陜西梁永、雲南楊榮，肆虐不減於奉，並乞征還，皆不報。

translations.literal: When Hubei tax commissioner Chen Feng was recalled for abusing the people, the Yellow River in Shaanxi ran dry at the same time. Qi stated that Gao Huai in Liaodong, Chen Zeng in Shandong, Li Feng in Guangdong, Liang Yong in Shaanxi, and Yang Rong in Yunnan were no less tyrannical than Chen Feng, and jointly asked that they all be recalled—not one request was answered.
translations.idiomatic: When Hubei tax commissioner Chen Feng was recalled for abusing the people, the Yellow River in Shaanxi ran dry at the same time. Feng Qi argued that Gao Huai in Liaodong, Chen Zeng in Shandong, Li Feng in Guangdong, Liang Yong in Shaanxi, and Yang Rong in Yunnan were no less tyrannical than Chen Feng, and asked that they all be recalled—none of these requests received a response.

sentences.zh: 南京守備中官邢隆請別給關防征稅，琦不可，乃以御前牙關防給之。

translations.literal: Nanjing garrison eunuch Xing Long asked for a separate seal to levy taxes; Qi refused, but an imperial-front teeth seal was given him instead.
translations.idiomatic: Nanjing garrison eunuch Xing Long requested a separate official seal to levy taxes; Feng Qi objected, but an imperial seal was granted instead.

sentences.zh: 時士大夫多崇釋氏教，士子作文，每竊其緒言，鄙棄傳註。

translations.literal: At the time scholar-officials mostly venerated Buddhism; students composing essays often pilfered its language and scorned classical commentaries.
translations.idiomatic: Scholar-officials at the time mostly venerated Buddhism; students composing essays pilfered Buddhist phrasing and scorned classical commentaries.

sentences.zh: 前尚書余繼登奏請約禁，然習尚如故。

translations.literal: Former Minister Yu Jideng submitted a memorial requesting restrictive prohibition, but the custom remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: Former Minister Yu Jideng had memorialized asking for restrictions, but the fashion persisted unchanged.

sentences.zh: 琦乃復極陳其弊，帝為下詔戒厲。

translations.literal: Qi then again fully stated its evils, and the emperor issued an edict of admonition and restraint on that account.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Qi again laid out the harm at length, and the emperor issued an edict of admonition in response.

sentences.zh: 琦明習典故，學有根柢。

translations.literal: Qi was clearly versed in institutional precedents and his learning had deep roots.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Qi was thoroughly versed in institutional precedent, and his learning ran deep.

sentences.zh: 數陳讜論，中外想望豐采，帝亦深眷倚。

translations.literal: He repeatedly submitted upright counsel; within and outside the court people looked up to his bearing; the emperor also deeply favored and relied on him.
translations.idiomatic: He repeatedly submitted forthright counsel; court and country alike looked up to him; the emperor deeply favored and relied on him.

sentences.zh: 內閣缺人，帝已簡用朱國祚及琦。

translations.literal: The Grand Secretariat lacked men; the emperor had already selected Zhu Guozuo and Qi.
translations.idiomatic: With vacancies in the Grand Secretariat, the emperor had already chosen Zhu Guozuo and Feng Qi.

sentences.zh: 而沈一貫密揭，言二人年未及艾，蓋少需之，先用老成者。

translations.literal: But Shen Yiguan submitted a secret memorial saying both men had not yet reached mature years—one should wait a little and first appoint those of seasoned experience.
translations.idiomatic: But Shen Yiguan submitted a secret memorial saying both men were still too young—better to wait and appoint more seasoned men first.

sentences.zh: 乃改命沈鯉、朱賡。

translations.literal: Thereupon the appointment was changed to Shen Li and Zhu Geng.
translations.idiomatic: The appointments went instead to Shen Li and Zhu Geng.

sentences.zh: 琦素善病，至是篤。

translations.literal: Qi had always been prone to illness; by now it was severe.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Qi had always been frail; by now his illness was grave.

sentences.zh: 十六疏乞休，不允。

translations.literal: Sixteen times he memorialized requesting retirement; not granted.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized sixteen times asking to retire; each request was denied.

sentences.zh: 卒於官，年僅四十六。

translations.literal: He died in office, aged only forty-six.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office at the age of only forty-six.

sentences.zh: 遺疏請厲明作，發章奏，補缺官，推誠接下，收拾人心。

translations.literal: His final memorial asked that imperial governance be made strict and clear, memorials be answered, vacant posts be filled, sincerity be extended toward subordinates, and popular hearts be gathered in.
translations.idiomatic: His final memorial asked the emperor to govern with clarity and vigor, respond to memorials, fill vacant posts, treat subordinates with sincerity, and win back the people's hearts.

sentences.zh: 語極懇摯。

translations.literal: The language was extremely earnest and sincere.
translations.idiomatic: His words were deeply earnest.

sentences.zh: 帝悼惜之。

translations.literal: The emperor mourned and cherished his memory.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor mourned him deeply.

sentences.zh: 贈太子少保。

translations.literal: He was posthumously given the title Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously honored as Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 天啟初，謚文敏。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Tianqi reign he was given the posthumous name Wenmin.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Tianqi reign he was given the posthumous name Wenmin, "Cultured and Quick."

sentences.zh: 自琦曾祖裕以下，累世皆進士。

translations.literal: From Qi's great-grandfather Yu downward, generation after generation produced jinshi.
translations.idiomatic: From Feng Qi's great-grandfather Yu onward, every generation of the family produced a jinshi.

sentences.zh: 裕，字伯順，以戍籍生於遼東。

translations.literal: Yu, courtesy name Boshun, was born in Liaodong while registered as a garrison soldier.
translations.idiomatic: Yu, courtesy name Boshun, was born in Liaodong while his family served under garrison registration.

sentences.zh: 師事賀欽，有學行。

translations.literal: He studied under He Qin and possessed both learning and conduct.
translations.idiomatic: He studied under He Qin and was known for both learning and integrity.

sentences.zh: 終雲南副使。

translations.literal: He ended as Vice Commissioner of Yunnan.
translations.idiomatic: He ended his career as Vice Commissioner of Yunnan.

sentences.zh: 祖惟重，行人。

translations.literal: His grandfather Weizhong was an Erudite Litigator.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Weizhong served as a palace messenger.

sentences.zh: 父子履，河南參政。

translations.literal: His father Zilu was Administration Vice Commissioner of Henan.
translations.idiomatic: His father Zilu served as Administration Vice Commissioner of Henan.

sentences.zh: 從祖惟健，舉人；

translations.literal: His collateral ancestor Weijian was a provincial graduate;
translations.idiomatic: His kinsman Weijian passed the provincial examination;

sentences.zh: 惟訥，字汝言，江西左布政使，加光祿卿致仕。

translations.literal: Weine, courtesy name Ruyan, was Left Provincial Administration Commissioner of Jiangxi; he was given the additional title of Director of Ceremonial and retired.
translations.idiomatic: Weine, courtesy name Ruyan, served as Left Provincial Administration Commissioner of Jiangxi; he received the additional title of Director of Ceremonial before retiring.

sentences.zh: 惟重、惟健、惟訥皆有文名，惟訥最著。

translations.literal: Weizhong, Weijian, and Weine all had literary reputations; Weine was the most renowned.
translations.idiomatic: Weizhong, Weijian, and Weine all had literary reputations; Weine was the most celebrated.

sentences.zh: 惟健子子咸，字受甫。

translations.literal: Weijian's son Zixian, courtesy name Shoufu.
translations.idiomatic: Weijian's son Zixian, courtesy name Shoufu.

sentences.zh: 少孤，事母孝。

translations.literal: Orphaned young, he served his mother with filial devotion.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned young, he devoted himself to his mother with exemplary filial piety.

sentences.zh: 母疾，不解衣者逾年。

translations.literal: When his mother fell ill, for more than a year he did not undress.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother fell ill, he did not undress for more than a year.

sentences.zh: 母歿，哀毀骨立。

translations.literal: When his mother died, his grief was so devastating that only bones remained standing.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother died, his grief reduced him to skin and bone.

sentences.zh: 萬歷元年舉於鄉。

translations.literal: In Wanli 1 he was selected in the provincial examination.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Wanli he passed the provincial examination.

sentences.zh: 再會試不第，遂不復赴。

translations.literal: He twice failed the metropolitan examination and thereafter never went again.
translations.idiomatic: He failed the metropolitan examination twice and never attempted it again.

sentences.zh: 講求濂、洛之學，嘗曰：「為學須剛與恒。

translations.literal: He pursued the learning of Zhou Dunyi and the Cheng brothers, and once said: "In study one must have firmness and perseverance.
translations.idiomatic: He pursued the Neo-Confucian learning of the Zhou and Cheng masters, and once said, "Study requires firmness and perseverance.

sentences.zh: 不剛則隳，不恒則退。」

translations.literal: Without firmness one collapses; without perseverance one retreats."
translations.idiomatic: Without firmness you collapse; without perseverance you fall back."

sentences.zh: 治家宗《顏氏家訓》。

translations.literal: In managing the household he took the Yan Family Instructions as his model.
translations.idiomatic: In managing his household he took the Yan Family Instructions as his guide.

sentences.zh: 鐘羽正稱「子咸信道忘仕則漆雕子，循經蹈古則高子羔」雲。

translations.literal: Zhong Yuzheng praised him, saying: "If in holding to the Way and forgetting office Zixian is like Qidiaozi, in following the classics and treading antiquity he is like Gaozigao."
translations.idiomatic: Zhong Yuzheng praised him, saying, "In holding to the Way and forsaking official ambition he is like Qidiaozi; in following the classics and treading the path of antiquity he is like Gaozigao."

sentences.zh: 王圖，字則之，耀州人。

translations.literal: Wang Tu, styled Zezhi, was a native of Yaozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Tu, courtesy name Zezhi, was from Yaozhou.

sentences.zh: 萬歷十一年進士。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year of Wanli he passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: He became a jinshi in the eleventh year of the Wanli reign.

sentences.zh: 改庶吉士，授檢討，以右中允掌南京翰林院事。

translations.literal: He was transferred to be a bachelors, appointed examining editor, and as right assistant director managed the affairs of the Nanking Hanlin Academy.
translations.idiomatic: He entered the Hanlin Academy as a bachelors, was appointed examining editor, and as Right Assistant Director took charge of the Nanjing Hanlin Academy.

sentences.zh: 召充東宮講官。

translations.literal: He was summoned to serve as a lecturer to the Eastern Palace.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned to serve as lecturer to the crown prince.

sentences.zh: 「妖書」事起，沈一貫欲有所羅織，圖其教習門生也，盡言規之。

translations.literal: When the "sorcery book" affair arose, Shen Yiguan wished to frame someone; Tu had been instructing his disciples, and spoke out fully to admonish him.
translations.idiomatic: When the "sorcery pamphlet" scandal broke out, Shen Yiguan sought to entangle someone in it. Tu, who had been instructing his disciples, spoke out strongly to warn him.

sentences.zh: 累遷詹事，充日講官，教習庶吉士。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Grand Mentor, served as daily lecturer, and instructed bachelors.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through successive promotions to Grand Mentor, served as daily court lecturer, and supervised the Hanlin bachelors.

sentences.zh: 進吏部右侍郎，掌翰林院。

translations.literal: He advanced to right vice minister of the Ministry of Personnel and managed the Hanlin Academy.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Vice Minister of the Right in the Ministry of Personnel and put in charge of the Hanlin Academy.

sentences.zh: 兄國方巡撫保定，廷臣附東林及李三才者，往往推轂圖兄弟。

translations.literal: His elder brother Guo was then grand coordinator of Baoding; court ministers affiliated with the Donglin faction and Li Sancai often pushed the Tu brothers forward.
translations.idiomatic: His elder brother Guo was serving as grand coordinator of Baoding, and ministers aligned with the Donglin faction and Li Sancai frequently promoted the Tu brothers.

sentences.zh: 會孫丕揚起掌吏部，孫瑋以尚書督倉場，皆陜西人，諸不悅圖者，目為秦黨。

translations.literal: As it happened Sun Piyang was raised to manage the Ministry of Personnel, and Sun Wei as minister supervised the grain depots — both were Shaanxi men; those displeased with Tu labeled them the Qin Clique.
translations.idiomatic: Around this time Sun Piyang was recalled to head the Ministry of Personnel, and Sun Wei, as minister, supervised the granaries. Both were Shaanxi natives, and those hostile to Tu denounced them as the Qin faction.

sentences.zh: 而是時郭正域、劉曰寧及圖並有相望。

translations.literal: At this time Guo Zhengyu, Liu Yuening, and Tu all had prospects of advancement.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Guo Zhengyu, Liu Yuening, and Tu were all widely regarded as candidates for high office.

sentences.zh: 正域逐去，曰寧卒，時論益歸圖。

translations.literal: Zhengyu was driven away, Yuening died, and public opinion increasingly favored Tu.
translations.idiomatic: After Zhengyu was driven from office and Yuening died, public sentiment increasingly rallied behind Tu.

sentences.zh: 葉向高獨相久，圖旦夕且入閣，忌者益眾。

translations.literal: Ye Xianggao had long served as sole chief grand secretary; Tu was expected to enter the Grand Secretariat at any moment, and those who envied him grew ever more numerous.
translations.idiomatic: Ye Xianggao had served as sole chief grand secretary for a long time, and Tu seemed on the verge of joining the Grand Secretariat at any day — his enemies grew ever more numerous.

sentences.zh: 適將京察，惡東林及李三才、王元翰者，設詞惑丕揚，令發單咨是非，將陰為鉤黨計。

translations.literal: Just as the capital evaluation was about to take place, those who hated the Donglin faction as well as Li Sancai and Wang Yuanhan devised words to mislead Piyang, asking him to issue a directive soliciting judgments on right and wrong, intending secretly to compile a list of factional associates.
translations.idiomatic: Just before the capital officials' evaluation, enemies of the Donglin faction, Li Sancai, and Wang Yuanhan maneuvered to mislead Sun Piyang into issuing a circular soliciting moral judgments — a covert scheme to compile a blacklist of factional allies.

sentences.zh: 圖急言於丕揚，止之，群小大恨。

translations.literal: Tu urgently spoke to Piyang and stopped it; the petty men greatly resented this.
translations.idiomatic: Tu urgently pleaded with Sun Piyang to halt the plan, and the petty schemers deeply resented him for it.

sentences.zh: 初，圖典庚戌會試。

translations.literal: Earlier, Tu had presided over the gengxu metropolitan examination.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Tu had served as chief examiner for the gengxu-year metropolitan examination.

sentences.zh: 分校官湯賓尹欲私韓敬，與知貢舉吳道南盛氣相詬誶。

translations.literal: The sub-examiner Tang Binyin wished to favor Han Jing privately and exchanged heated curses with the examination supervisor Wu Daonan.
translations.idiomatic: Sub-examiner Tang Binyin sought to favor Han Jing improperly and came to heated blows with examination supervisor Wu Daonan.

sentences.zh: 比出闈，道南欲劾，以圖沮而止。

translations.literal: When the examination ended, Daonan wished to impeach him, but Tu dissuaded him and he desisted.
translations.idiomatic: After the examination gates closed, Daonan wanted to bring charges, but Tu dissuaded him and the matter stopped there.

sentences.zh: 王紹徽者，圖同郡人，賓尹門生也，極譽賓尹於圖，而言道南黨欲傾賓尹並及圖，宜善為計。

translations.literal: Wang Shaohui was a man from the same commandery as Tu and a disciple of Binyin; he lavishly praised Binyin to Tu and said that Daonan's faction wished to topple Binyin and implicate Tu as well — Tu ought to plan accordingly.
translations.idiomatic: One Wang Shaohui, a fellow native of Tu's prefecture and a disciple of Tang Binyin, lavishly praised Binyin to Tu and warned that Wu Daonan's faction meant to bring down Binyin and ruin Tu along with him — Tu ought to take precautions.

sentences.zh: 圖正色卻之，紹徽怫然去。

translations.literal: Tu sternly rejected him, and Shaohui departed in displeasure.
translations.idiomatic: Tu rebuffed him with a stern face, and Shaohui left in a sulk.

sentences.zh: 時賓尹已為祭酒，其先歷翰林京察，當圖註考，思先發傾之。

translations.literal: By then Binyin had already become chancellor of the National University; earlier he had undergone the Hanlin capital evaluation and was to receive Tu's performance rating — he thought to strike first and bring Tu down.
translations.idiomatic: By then Tang Binyin had become chancellor of the Imperial University. An earlier round of Hanlin evaluations had put him under Tu's rating, and he resolved to strike first and bring Tu down.

sentences.zh: 乃與紹徽計。

translations.literal: Thereupon he plotted with Shaohui.
translations.idiomatic: He then conspired with Shaohui.

sentences.zh: 令御史金明時劾圖子寶坻知縣淑抃贓私巨萬。

translations.literal: He had censor Jin Mingshi impeach Tu's son Shubian, magistrate of Baodi, for embezzling tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: They had censor Jin Mingshi impeach Tu's son Shubian, magistrate of Baodi, for corruption involving vast sums.

sentences.zh: 且謂國素疾李三才，圖為求解，國怒詈之，圖遂欲以拾遺去國。

translations.literal: Moreover they claimed that Guo had always hated Li Sancai, that Tu sought to intercede on his behalf, that Guo angrily berated him, and that Tu thus wished to use a remonstrance memorial to remove Guo.
translations.idiomatic: They further claimed that Guo had long despised Li Sancai, that Tu interceded on Li's behalf, that Guo furiously rebuked him, and that Tu then tried to have Guo removed through a memorial of remonstrance.

sentences.zh: 國兄弟抗章力辯，忌者復偽為淑抃劾國疏，播之邸抄。

translations.literal: The Guo brothers submitted successive memorials forcefully rebutting the charges; their enemies further forged an impeachment memorial by Shubian against Guo and circulated it in the court gazette.
translations.idiomatic: The Guo brothers filed memorial after memorial in stout defense; their enemies then forged an impeachment memorial purportedly from Shubian against Guo and spread it through the court gazette.

sentences.zh: 圖上疏言狀，帝為下詔購捕，乃已。

translations.literal: Tu submitted a memorial stating the facts; the emperor issued an edict offering a reward for the capture of the forgers, and only then did it stop.
translations.idiomatic: Tu memorialized the emperor with a full account of events; the emperor issued an edict offering a reward for the forgers' arrest, and the affair finally quieted.

sentences.zh: 及考察，卒註賓尹不謹，褫其官，明時亦被黜。

translations.literal: At the evaluation, Binyin was ultimately rated as "not careful" and stripped of his office; Mingshi was also dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: When the evaluation came, Tang Binyin was ultimately rated "negligent" and stripped of office, and Jin Mingshi was dismissed as well.

sentences.zh: 由是其黨大噪。

translations.literal: Thereupon his faction raised a great outcry.
translations.idiomatic: His faction erupted in outrage.

sentences.zh: 秦聚、奎朱一桂、鄭繼芳、徐兆魁、高節、王萬祚、曾陳易輩，連章力攻圖。

translations.literal: Qin Jukui, Zhu Yigui, Zheng Jifang, Xu Zhaokui, Gao Jie, Wang Wanzuo, Zeng Chenyi, and their ilk submitted successive memorials forcefully attacking Tu.
translations.idiomatic: Qin Jukui, Zhu Yigui, Zheng Jifang, Xu Zhaokui, Gao Jie, Wang Wanzuo, Zeng Chenyi, and others filed memorial after memorial denouncing Tu.

sentences.zh: 圖亦連章求去，出郊待命。

translations.literal: Tu also submitted successive memorials requesting dismissal and went to the suburbs to await orders.
translations.idiomatic: Tu too submitted repeated memorials asking to resign and withdrew to the countryside to await the emperor's decision.

sentences.zh: 溫詔屢慰留，堅臥不起，九閱月始予告歸。

translations.literal: Warm edicts repeatedly urged him to stay, but he steadfastly remained abed and would not rise; only after nine months was he granted leave to return home.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's kind edicts urged him repeatedly to stay, but he refused to rise from his bed; only after nine months was he granted leave to retire home.

sentences.zh: 國亦乞休去，未幾卒。

translations.literal: Guo also requested retirement and left; before long he died.
translations.idiomatic: Guo likewise petitioned to retire and withdrew; he died not long after.

sentences.zh: 四十五年京察，當事者多賓尹、紹徽黨，以拾遺落圖職。

translations.literal: In the forty-fifth year at the capital evaluation, most of those in power were of Binyin and Shaohui's faction; Tu was demoted to remonstrance official through the evaluation.
translations.idiomatic: At the forty-fifth year's capital evaluation, those in power were largely allies of Tang Binyin and Wang Shaohui, and Tu was downgraded to a remonstrance post.

sentences.zh: 天啟三年，召起故官。

translations.literal: In the third year of Tianqi he was summoned back to his former office.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of the Tianqi reign he was recalled to his former post.

sentences.zh: 進禮部尚書，協理詹事府。

translations.literal: He was promoted to minister of rites and assisted in managing the Grand Mentor's office.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Minister of Rites and appointed to assist in managing the Grand Mentor's office.

sentences.zh: 明年，魏忠賢黨劉弘先劾圖，遂削籍。

translations.literal: The next year Liu Hongxian, a member of Wei Zhongxian's faction, impeached Tu, and Tu was stricken from the rolls.
translations.idiomatic: The following year Liu Hongxian, an ally of Wei Zhongxian, impeached Tu, and he was stripped from the official register.

sentences.zh: 尋卒。

translations.literal: Before long he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died soon after.

sentences.zh: 崇禎初，贈太子太保，謚文肅。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Chongzhen he was posthumously awarded Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent with the posthumous title Wensu.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Chongzhen reign he was posthumously ennobled as Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent and given the posthumous name Wensu.

sentences.zh: 淑抃終戶部郎中。

translations.literal: Shubian ended his career as director in the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: Shubian eventually served out his career as a director in the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 劉曰寧，字幼安，南昌人。

translations.literal: Liu Yuening, styled You'an, was a native of Nanchang.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yuening, courtesy name You'an, was from Nanchang.

sentences.zh: 萬歷十七年進士。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year of Wanli he passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: He became a jinshi in the seventeenth year of the Wanli reign.

sentences.zh: 改庶吉士，授編修。

translations.literal: He was transferred to be a bachelors and appointed compiling editor.
translations.idiomatic: He entered the Hanlin Academy as a bachelors and was appointed compiling editor.

sentences.zh: 進右中允，直皇長子講幄。

translations.literal: He was promoted to right assistant director and attended upon the eldest imperial son in the lecture hall.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Right Assistant Director and served in the crown prince's lecture hall.

sentences.zh: 時冊立未舉，外議紛紜。

translations.literal: At the time the investiture as heir had not been conducted and outside opinion was in turmoil.
translations.idiomatic: The formal investiture of the heir apparent had not yet taken place, and public debate raged outside the palace.

sentences.zh: 曰寧旁慰曲喻，依於仁孝，光宗心識之。

translations.literal: Yuening offered indirect comfort and gentle persuasion, keeping to benevolence and filial piety; Emperor Guangzong took note of this in his heart.
translations.idiomatic: Yuening offered subtle comfort and gentle counsel, appealing to the virtues of benevolence and filial piety — the future Emperor Guangzong noted this and held him in regard.

sentences.zh: 礦使四出，曰寧發憤上疏，陳六疑四患，極言稅監李道、王朝諸不法狀。

translations.literal: Mining envoys were dispatched in all directions; Yuening in indignation submitted a memorial setting forth six doubts and four evils, speaking in the strongest terms of the illegal conduct of tax supervisors Li Dao, Wang Chao, and others.
translations.idiomatic: Mining commissioners were sent out in all directions; Yuening, in outrage, memorialized the throne with six doubts and four calamities, denouncing in detail the illegal conduct of tax supervisors Li Dao, Wang Chao, and others.

sentences.zh: 疏入，留中。

translations.literal: The memorial was submitted and kept at court.
translations.idiomatic: His memorial was submitted but shelved by the emperor.

sentences.zh: 以母病歸。

translations.literal: He returned home because his mother was ill.
translations.idiomatic: He retired home when his mother fell ill.

sentences.zh: 起右諭德，掌南京翰林院，就遷國子祭酒。

translations.literal: He was raised to right preceptor, managed the Nanking Hanlin Academy, and was promptly transferred to chancellor of the National University.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled as Right Preceptor, put in charge of the Nanjing Hanlin Academy, and soon promoted to chancellor of the Imperial University.

sentences.zh: 奉母歸，吏進贏金數千，曰「例也」，曰寧峻卻之。

translations.literal: When escorting his mother home, an official presented several thousand in surplus gold, saying "It is customary"; Yuening sternly refused.
translations.idiomatic: While escorting his mother home, an official offered him several thousand taels in surplus funds, saying it was standard practice — Yuening flatly refused.

sentences.zh: 尋起少詹事，母喪不赴。

translations.literal: Before long he was raised to junior grand mentor, but upon his mother's death he did not take up the post.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon recalled as Junior Grand Mentor but did not report for duty when his mother died.

sentences.zh: 服闋，召為禮部右侍郎，協理詹事府。

translations.literal: When mourning ended he was summoned as right vice minister of rites and assisted in managing the Grand Mentor's office.
translations.idiomatic: After the mourning period he was summoned as Vice Minister of the Right in the Ministry of Rites to assist in managing the Grand Mentor's office.

sentences.zh: 道卒。

translations.literal: On the way he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died en route.

sentences.zh: 贈禮部尚書。

translations.literal: He was posthumously awarded minister of rites.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously honored as Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 天啟初，追謚文簡。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianqi he was posthumously given the title Wenjian.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Tianqi reign he was granted the posthumous name Wenjian.

sentences.zh: 翁正春，字兆震，侯官人。

translations.literal: Weng Zhengchun, styled Zhaozhen, was a native of Houguan.
translations.idiomatic: Weng Zhengchun, courtesy name Zhaozhen, was from Houguan.

sentences.zh: 萬歷中，為龍溪教諭。

translations.literal: During Wanli he served as instructor of Longxi.
translations.idiomatic: During the Wanli reign he served as county school instructor in Longxi.

sentences.zh: 二十年，擢進士第一，授修撰，累遷少詹事。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year he was selected first in the jinshi examination, appointed revising editor, and repeatedly promoted to junior grand mentor.
translations.idiomatic: In the twentieth year he topped the jinshi examination, was appointed revising editor, and rose through successive promotions to Junior Grand Mentor.

sentences.zh: 三十八年九月，拜禮部左侍郎，代吳道南署部事。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of the thirty-eighth year he was appointed left vice minister of rites, acting for Wu Daonan in managing the ministry.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of the thirty-eighth year he was appointed Vice Minister of the Left in the Ministry of Rites, standing in for Wu Daonan as acting head of the ministry.

sentences.zh: 十一月，日有食之，正春極言闕失，不報。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month there was a solar eclipse; Zhengchun spoke at length of failings and omissions, but received no response.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month a solar eclipse occurred; Zhengchun memorialized at length about the court's failings, but the emperor gave no reply.

sentences.zh: 明年秋，萬壽節，正春獻八箴：曰清君心，遵祖制，振國紀，信臣僚，寶賢才，謹財用，恤民命，重邊防。

translations.literal: The next autumn, on the emperor's longevity festival, Zhengchun presented eight admonitions: namely, purify the ruler's mind, follow ancestral institutions, restore national discipline, trust ministers and officials, cherish worthy talent, be careful with finances, show compassion for the people's lives, and take border defense seriously.
translations.idiomatic: The following autumn, on the emperor's birthday celebration, Zhengchun presented eight admonitions: purify the sovereign's heart, uphold ancestral institutions, restore national discipline, trust his ministers, cherish worthy talent, husband the treasury, show compassion for the people's lives, and strengthen frontier defense.

sentences.zh: 帝不省。

translations.literal: The emperor took no notice.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor paid no heed.

sentences.zh: 吉王翊鑾請封支子常源為郡王。

translations.literal: Prince Ji Yiquan requested that his branch son Changyuan be enfeoffed as a commandery prince.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Ji Yiquan petitioned to have his younger son Changyuan enfeoffed as a commandery prince.

sentences.zh: 正春言翊鑾之封在《宗藩條例》已定之後，其支庶宜止本爵。

translations.literal: Zhengchun said that Yiquan's enfeoffment came after the Regulations on Imperial Clansmen had been fixed, and that his branch descendants should stop at their original rank.
translations.idiomatic: Zhengchun argued that Yiquan's enfeoffment had come after the Regulations on Imperial Clansmen were established, and that collateral descendants should retain only their original titles.

sentences.zh: 乃授鎮國將軍。

translations.literal: Thereupon he was granted the title Suppressing-State General.
translations.idiomatic: Changyuan was accordingly granted only the title of State-pacifying General.

sentences.zh: 王貴妃薨，久不卜葬，正春以為言。

translations.literal: Consort Wang died, but for a long time no auspicious burial site was chosen; Zhengchun spoke out on this.
translations.idiomatic: When Consort Wang died, no burial site was chosen for a long time; Zhengchun raised the matter.

sentences.zh: 命偕中官往擇地，得吉。

translations.literal: He was ordered to go together with eunuchs to select a site, and an auspicious one was found.
translations.idiomatic: He was ordered to go with court eunuchs to select a site, and they found an auspicious location.

sentences.zh: 中官難以煩費，正春勃然曰：「貴妃誕育元良，他日國母也，奈何以天下儉乎？」

translations.literal: The eunuchs objected on grounds of trouble and expense; Zhengchun flushed with anger and said: "The consort bore the primary son — she will one day be empress dowager — how can we be sparing with the empire's resources?
translations.idiomatic: The eunuchs balked at the cost and trouble, whereupon Zhengchun flushed with anger and said: "The consort gave birth to the heir apparent — one day she will be empress dowager. How can we stint on the empire's behalf?

sentences.zh: 奏上，報可。

translations.literal: The memorial was submitted and approved.
translations.idiomatic: His memorial was submitted and approved.

sentences.zh: 代王欲廢長子鼎渭，立次子鼎莎，朝議持二十余年。

translations.literal: The Prince of Dai wished to depose his eldest son Dingwei and establish his second son Dingsha; court debate continued for more than twenty years.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Dai sought to disinherit his eldest son Dingwei and install his second son Dingsha instead — court debate dragged on for more than twenty years.

sentences.zh: 正春集眾議上疏，鼎渭卒得立。

translations.literal: Zhengchun gathered collective opinion and submitted a memorial; Dingwei ultimately was established as heir.
translations.idiomatic: Zhengchun collected consensus and memorialized the throne; Dingwei was ultimately confirmed as heir.

sentences.zh: 琉球中山王遣使入貢，正春言：「中山已入於倭，今使臣多倭人，貢物多倭器，絕之便；

translations.literal: The King of Chungshan in Ryukyu sent envoys to pay tribute; Zhengchun said: "Chungshan has already fallen under Japan; now most of the envoys are Japanese and most of the tribute goods are Japanese articles — it would be best to cut off relations;
translations.idiomatic: The King of Chungshan in Ryukyu sent envoys to pay tribute; Zhengchun argued: "Chungshan has already fallen under Japan; most of the envoys are now Japanese and most of the tribute goods are Japanese wares — it would be best to cut off relations altogether;

sentences.zh: 否亦宜詔福建撫臣量留土物，毋俾入朝。」

translations.literal: if not, Fujian's grand coordinator should at least be instructed to retain only local products in measured amounts and not allow them to enter court.
translations.idiomatic: failing that, the Fujian governor should be ordered to retain only a measured portion of local tribute goods and bar the envoys from entering the capital.

sentences.zh: 帝是之。

translations.literal: The emperor approved of this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 四十年，進士鄒之麟分校鄉試，私舉子童學賢，為御史馬孟禎等所發。

translations.literal: In the fortieth year jinshi Zou Zhilin served as sub-examiner in the provincial examination and privately favored the candidate Tong Xuexian; this was exposed by censor Ma Mengzhen and others.
translations.idiomatic: In the fortieth year, jinshi Zou Zhilin served as sub-examiner for the provincial examinations and improperly favored candidate Tong Xuexian; censor Ma Mengzhen and others exposed the affair.

sentences.zh: 正春議黜學賢，謫之麟，而不及主考官。

translations.literal: Zhengchun proposed to disqualify Xuexian and demote Zhilin, but did not implicate the chief examiner.
translations.idiomatic: Zhengchun ruled to disqualify Xuexian and demote Zhilin but did not punish the chief examiner.

sentences.zh: 給事中趙興邦、亓詩教因劾正春徇私。

translations.literal: Supervising secretaries Zhao Xingbang and Qi Shijiao therefore impeached Zhengchun for favoritism.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising secretaries Zhao Xingbang and Qi Shijiao then impeached Zhengchun for showing favoritism.

sentences.zh: 正春求去，不許。

translations.literal: Zhengchun requested dismissal; it was not granted.
translations.idiomatic: Zhengchun asked to resign, but the request was denied.

sentences.zh: 頃之，言官發湯賓尹、韓敬科場事。

translations.literal: Before long, remonstrance officials exposed the examination hall affair of Tang Binyin and Han Jing.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward, memorialists exposed the examination scandal involving Tang Binyin and Han Jing.

sentences.zh: 正春坐敬不謹，敬黨大恨。

translations.literal: Zhengchun was judged responsible for Han Jing's rating of "not careful"; Jing's faction greatly resented this.
translations.idiomatic: Zhengchun was held accountable for rating Han Jing "negligent," and Han's faction deeply resented him.

sentences.zh: 詩教復劾正春，正春疏辯，益求去。

translations.literal: Shijiao again impeached Zhengchun; Zhengchun memorialized in defense and all the more sought dismissal.
translations.idiomatic: Qi Shijiao impeached Zhengchun again; Zhengchun memorialized in his own defense and pressed all the harder to resign.

sentences.zh: 帝雖慰留，然自是不安其位。

translations.literal: Although the emperor urged him to stay, from then on he was ill at ease in his position.
translations.idiomatic: Though the emperor urged him to remain, from that point on he no longer felt secure in office.

sentences.zh: 尋改吏部，掌詹事府，以侍養歸。

translations.literal: Before long he was transferred to the Ministry of Personnel and managed the Grand Mentor's office, then returned home to care for his parents.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon transferred to the Ministry of Personnel and put in charge of the Grand Mentor's office, then retired home to tend his parents.

sentences.zh: 天啟元年，起禮部尚書，協理詹事府事。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tianqi he was raised to minister of rites and assisted in managing the Grand Mentor's office.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of the Tianqi reign he was recalled as Minister of Rites to assist in managing the Grand Mentor's office.

sentences.zh: 抗論忤魏忠賢，被旨譙責。

translations.literal: His forthright arguments offended Wei Zhongxian, and he received an edict of censure and rebuke.
translations.idiomatic: His outspoken remonstrance offended Wei Zhongxian, and he received an imperial edict of rebuke.

sentences.zh: 明年，御史趙胤昌希指劾之，正春再疏乞歸。

translations.literal: The next year censor Zhao Yinchang, seeking to please his superiors, impeached him; Zhengchun again memorialized begging to return home.
translations.idiomatic: The following year censor Zhao Yinchang, reading the prevailing winds, impeached him, and Zhengchun memorialized once more begging leave to retire.

sentences.zh: 帝以正春嘗為皇祖講官，特加太子少保，賜敕馳傳，異數也。

translations.literal: Because Zhengchun had once been lecturer to the imperial grandfather, the emperor specially added the title Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent, granted an edict and post horses for swift travel — an extraordinary honor.
translations.idiomatic: Because Zhengchun had once served as lecturer to the emperor's grandfather, the throne specially added the title of Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent and granted him an imperial edict with post horses for the journey home — a rare distinction.

sentences.zh: 時正春年逾七十，母百歲，率子孫奉觴上壽，鄉閭艷之。

translations.literal: At the time Zhengchun was over seventy and his mother was one hundred; leading his sons and grandsons he offered cups to celebrate her longevity, and the villagers admired this.
translations.idiomatic: By then Zhengchun was past seventy and his mother had reached one hundred; he led his sons and grandsons in raising cups to celebrate her birthday, to the admiration of the whole neighborhood.

sentences.zh: 未幾，卒。

translations.literal: Before long he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died not long after.

sentences.zh: 崇禎初，謚文簡。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Chongzhen he was given the posthumous title Wenjian.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Chongzhen reign he was granted the posthumous name Wenjian.

sentences.zh: 正春風度峻整，終日無狎語。

translations.literal: Zhengchun's bearing was stern and dignified; all day long there was no familiar banter.
translations.idiomatic: Zhengchun's bearing was austere and dignified; never a day passed with careless or familiar talk.

sentences.zh: 倦不傾倚，暑不裸裎，目無流視。

translations.literal: When weary he did not lean askew; in heat he did not expose his body; his eyes did not wander.
translations.idiomatic: When tired he would not slump or lean; in summer heat he would not strip bare; his gaze never wandered idly.

sentences.zh: 見者肅然。

translations.literal: Those who saw him were struck with reverence.
translations.idiomatic: All who saw him were moved to solemn respect.

sentences.zh: 明一代，科目職官冠廷對者二人；

translations.literal: Throughout the Ming dynasty, only two men holding official posts through the examination system topped the palace examination;
translations.idiomatic: In the entire Ming dynasty, only two sitting officials who had risen through the examinations ranked first in the palace examination:

sentences.zh: 曹鼐以典史，正春以教諭雲。

translations.literal: Cao Tai as a county recorder, and Zhengchun as an instructor — such were they.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Tai, when a county recorder, and Zhengchun, when a county instructor.

sentences.zh: 劉應秋，字士和，吉水人。

translations.literal: Liu Yingqiu, styled Shihe, was a native of Jishui.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yingqiu, courtesy name Shihe, was from Jishui.

sentences.zh: 萬歷十一年進士及第，授編修，遷南京司業。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year of Wanli he passed the jinshi examination with highest honors, was appointed compiling editor, and transferred to vice director of studies in Nanking.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination with highest honors in the eleventh year of the Wanli reign, was appointed compiling editor, and was transferred to Vice Director of Studies in Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 十八年冬，疏論首輔申時行言：「陛下召對輔臣，諮以邊事，時行不能抒誠謀國，專事蒙蔽。

translations.literal: In the winter of the eighteenth year he submitted a memorial discussing Chief Grand Secretary Shen Shixing, saying: "Your Majesty summoned the grand secretaries for audience and consulted them on border affairs, but Shixing could not speak sincerely for the state's benefit and devoted himself to concealment.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of the eighteenth year he memorialized the throne regarding Chief Grand Secretary Shen Shixing, saying: "Your Majesty summoned the grand secretaries for audience and consulted them on border affairs, yet Shixing could not speak sincerely in the state's interest and devoted himself instead to concealment.

sentences.zh: 賊大舉入犯，既掠洮、岷，直迫臨、鞏，覆軍殺將，頻至喪敗，而時行猶曰『掠番』，曰『聲言入寇』，豈洮、河以內，盡皆番地乎？

translations.literal: The bandits launched a major invasion, having already plundered Tao and Min and pressing straight toward Lin and Gong; they wiped out armies and killed generals, repeatedly bringing defeat — yet Shixing still said "raiding the fan tribes" and "merely making a show of invasion." Are all lands within Tao and the Yellow River fan territory?
translations.idiomatic: The enemy launched a major invasion, plundering Tao and Min and pressing straight toward Lin and Gong; they wiped out armies and killed generals, bringing defeat after defeat — yet Shixing still called it "raiding the tribal frontier" and "merely threatening invasion." Are all lands within Tao and the Yellow River merely tribal territory?

sentences.zh: 輔臣者，天子所與托腹心者也。

translations.literal: A grand secretary is one in whom the Son of Heaven entrusts his innermost heart.
translations.idiomatic: A chief grand secretary is one in whom the Son of Heaven entrusts his innermost thoughts.

sentences.zh: 輔臣先蒙蔽，何責庶僚？

translations.literal: If the grand secretary first conceals the truth, how can ordinary officials be held accountable?
translations.idiomatic: When the chief minister himself conceals the truth, how can lesser officials be blamed?

sentences.zh: 故近日敵情有按臣疏而督撫不以聞者，有督撫聞而樞臣不以奏者。

translations.literal: Therefore of late regarding enemy intelligence, there are cases where investigating censors submit memorials yet governors and grand coordinators do not report upward; there are cases where governors and grand coordinators learn of it yet ministers of the military establishment do not memorialize the throne.
translations.idiomatic: Hence of late, when it comes to enemy intelligence, there are cases where investigating censors submit memorials yet governors and grand coordinators fail to report upward, and cases where governors and grand coordinators learn of matters yet central military ministers fail to memorialize the throne.

sentences.zh: 彼習見執政大臣喜聞捷而惡言敗，故內外相蒙，恬不為怪。

translations.literal: They are accustomed to seeing executing ministers delight in hearing of victory and loathe to speak of defeat, therefore inside and outside deceive one another, taking it calmly as nothing strange.
translations.idiomatic: They had long grown used to seeing those in power delight in news of victory and shrink from reporting defeat, so officials at every level deceived one another and thought nothing of it.

sentences.zh: 欺蔽之端，自輔臣始。

translations.literal: The origin of deception and concealment begins with the grand secretary.
translations.idiomatic: The practice of deception and concealment begins with the chief minister himself.

sentences.zh: 夫士風高下，關乎氣運，說者謂嘉靖至今，士風三變。

translations.literal: Now the rise and fall of scholarly morals relates to the turnings of fortune; commentators say that from the Jiajing reign to the present, scholarly morals have changed thrice.
translations.idiomatic: The moral character of the scholarly class rises and falls with the times; some say that from the Jiajing reign to the present it has shifted three times.

sentences.zh: 一變環境嚴嵩之黷賄，而士化為貪。

translations.literal: The first change came amid Yan Song's corrupt bribery, and scholars were transformed into greed.
translations.idiomatic: The first shift came in the era of Yan Song's corrupt venality, when scholars turned grasping.

sentences.zh: 再變於張居正之專擅，而士競於險。

translations.literal: The second change came with Zhang Juzheng's monopolization of power, and scholars competed in craftiness.
translations.idiomatic: The second came under Zhang Juzheng's autocratic rule, when scholars competed in ruthless scheming.

sentences.zh: 至於今，外逃貪黷之名，而頑夫債帥多出門下；

translations.literal: As for today, outwardly they flee the name of greedy corruption, yet obstinate men and debt-ridden commanders mostly issue from their gates;
translations.idiomatic: As for the present day, they outwardly shun the label of greedy corruption, yet obstinate schemers and incompetent generals mostly come from their own followers;

sentences.zh: 陽避專擅之跡，而芒刃斧斤倒持手中。

translations.literal: Outwardly they avoid the traces of monopolizing power, yet sharp blades and axes they hold inverted in their hands.
translations.idiomatic: They openly avoid any appearance of tyrannical power, yet hold sharp blades and axes reversed in their hands — wielding deadly authority while pretending not to.

sentences.zh: 威福之權，潛移其向；

translations.literal: The authority of power and favor quietly shifts its direction;
translations.idiomatic: The power to grant favor and inflict punishment quietly shifts course;

sentences.zh: 愛憎之的，明示之趨。

translations.literal: The objects of love and hatred are openly shown in where trends lean;
translations.idiomatic: Whom they favor and whom they hate is made plain, and all can see which way the wind blows.

sentences.zh: 欲天下無靡，不可得也。」

translations.literal: To wish the realm free of deference and compliance — it cannot be attained."
translations.idiomatic: To expect the empire to free itself of sycophancy is impossible.

sentences.zh: 語並侵次輔王錫爵。

translations.literal: ] The words also impugned Secondary Grand Secretary Wang Xijue.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial also impugned Secondary Grand Secretary Wang Xijue.

sentences.zh: 時主事蔡時鼎、南京御史章守誠亦疏論時行。

translations.literal: At the time Principal Secretary Cai Shiding and Nanjing Censor Zhang Shoucheng also submitted memorials criticizing Shixing.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Principal Secretary Cai Shiding and Nanjing Censor Zhang Shoucheng also submitted memorials criticizing Shixing.

sentences.zh: 並留中。

translations.literal: All were kept at court without action.
translations.idiomatic: All were kept at court without action.

sentences.zh: 應秋尋召為中允，充日講官。

translations.literal: Yingqiu was soon summoned as Middle Attendant and appointed Daily Lecture Official.
translations.idiomatic: Yingqiu was soon summoned as Middle Attendant and appointed Daily Lecture Official.

sentences.zh: 歷右庶子、祭酒。

translations.literal: He served as Right Vice Director of the Secretariat and Grand Master of the Imperial Academy.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Right Vice Director of the Secretariat and Grand Master of the Imperial Academy.

sentences.zh: 二十六年，有撰《憂危竑議》者，御史趙之翰以指大學士張位，並及應秋。

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth year, someone composed the "Youwei Jidong Discussion"; Censor Zhao Zihan held that it targeted Grand Secretary Zhang Wei and also implicated Yingqiu.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-sixth year, someone composed the Youwei Jidong Discussion; Censor Zhao Zihan held that it targeted Grand Secretary Zhang Wei and also implicated Yingqiu.

sentences.zh: 所司言應秋非位黨，宜留。

translations.literal: The investigating office said Yingqiu was not a member of Wei's faction and should be retained.
translations.idiomatic: The investigating office reported that Yingqiu was not a member of Wei's faction and should be retained.

sentences.zh: 帝命調外，應秋遂辭疾歸。

translations.literal: The Emperor ordered him transferred outside the capital; Yingqiu thereupon pleaded illness and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor ordered him transferred outside the capital; Yingqiu thereupon pleaded illness and returned home.

sentences.zh: 初，御史黃卷索珠商徐性善賕，不盡應，上章籍沒之。

translations.literal: Earlier, Censor Huang Juan had demanded bribes from pearl merchant Xu Xingshan; when Xu did not fully comply, Huang submitted a memorial requesting confiscation of his property.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Censor Huang Juan had extorted bribes from the pearl merchant Xu Xingshan; when Xu did not fully comply, Huang submitted a memorial requesting that his property be confiscated.

sentences.zh: 應秋詈卷啟天子好利之端。

translations.literal: Yingqiu denounced Juan for opening the door to the Son of Heaven's covetousness.
translations.idiomatic: Yingqiu denounced Huang Juan for opening the door to imperial covetousness.

sentences.zh: 男子諸龍光奏訐李如松，至荷枷大暑中。

translations.literal: A commoner named Zhu Longguang submitted an accusation against Li Rushi, and was made to wear the cangue in the height of summer heat.
translations.idiomatic: A commoner named Zhu Longguang submitted an accusation against Li Rushi and was made to wear the cangue in the sweltering midsummer heat.

sentences.zh: 應秋言一妄人上書，何必置死地。

translations.literal: Yingqiu said: "One madman submits a letter — why must he be driven to death?"
translations.idiomatic: Yingqiu said, "One madman submits a letter — why must he be driven to his death?"

sentences.zh: 時詞臣率優遊養望，應秋獨好議評時事，以此取忌，竟被黜。

translations.literal: At the time literary officials generally cultivated their reputations in leisurely ease; Yingqiu alone loved to discuss and critique current affairs, and for this incurred enmity and was ultimately dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: At the time literary officials generally cultivated their reputations in leisurely ease; Yingqiu alone loved to discuss and critique current affairs, and for this he incurred enmity and was ultimately dismissed.

sentences.zh: 歸數年，卒。

translations.literal: Several years after returning home, he died.
translations.idiomatic: Several years after returning home, he died.

sentences.zh: 崇禎時，贈禮部侍郎，謚文節。

translations.literal: During the Chongzhen reign he was posthumously made Vice Minister of Rites and given the posthumous name Wenjie.
translations.idiomatic: During the Chongzhen reign he was posthumously made Vice Minister of Rites and given the posthumous name Wenjie.

sentences.zh: 子同升，字晉卿。

translations.literal: His son Tongsheng, courtesy name Jin Qing.
translations.idiomatic: His son Tongsheng, courtesy name Jin Qing.

sentences.zh: 師同里鄒元標。

translations.literal: He studied under Zou Yuanbiao of his home district.
translations.idiomatic: He studied under Zou Yuanbiao of his home district.

sentences.zh: 崇禎十年，殿試第一。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Chongzhen he ranked first in the palace examination.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year of the Chongzhen reign he ranked first in the palace examination.

sentences.zh: 莊烈帝問年幾何，對曰：「五十有一。」

translations.literal: Emperor Zhuanglie asked how old he was; he answered: "Fifty-one.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Zhuanglie asked how old he was, and he answered, "Fifty-one.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「若尚如少年，勉之。」

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "You still look like a young man — apply yourself."
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said, "You still look like a young man — apply yourself."

sentences.zh: 授翰林修撰。

translations.literal: He was appointed Hanlin Compiler.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Hanlin Compiler.

sentences.zh: 楊嗣昌奪情入閣，何楷、林蘭友、黃道周言之俱獲罪，同升抗疏言：「日者策試諸臣，簡用嗣昌，良以中外交訌，冀得一效，拯我蒼生。

translations.literal: Yang Sichang took leave from mourning to enter the Grand Secretariat; He Kai, Lin Lanyou, and Huang Daozhou spoke of it and all were punished. Tongsheng submitted a bold memorial saying: "Recently Your Majesty tested the officials by edict and selected Sichang for appointment, truly because affairs at home and abroad are in turmoil, hoping he might prove effective and deliver our people.
translations.idiomatic: When Yang Sichang took leave from mourning to enter the Grand Secretariat, He Kai, Lin Lanyou, and Huang Daozhou spoke against it and all were punished. Tongsheng submitted a bold memorial saying, "Recently Your Majesty tested the officials by edict and selected Sichang for appointment, truly because affairs at home and abroad are in turmoil, hoping he might prove effective and deliver our people.

sentences.zh: 聖明用心，亦甚苦矣。

translations.literal: The sagely mind's exertion is also very arduous indeed.
translations.idiomatic: Your sagely exertions have been arduous indeed.

sentences.zh: 都人籍籍，謂嗣昌缞绖在身，且入閣非金革比。

translations.literal: People in the capital murmured everywhere that Sichang still wore mourning garments upon his body, and moreover entering the Grand Secretariat is not comparable to the exigencies of war.
translations.idiomatic: People throughout the capital murmured that Sichang still wore mourning garments upon his body, and that entering the Grand Secretariat is not comparable to the exigencies of war.

sentences.zh: 臣以嗣昌必且哀痛惻怛，上告君父，辭免綸扉；

translations.literal: Your subject expected Sichang would surely grieve in anguish, appeal above to his sovereign lord and father, and decline the Grand Secretariat;
translations.idiomatic: Your subject expected that Sichang would surely grieve in anguish, appeal to his sovereign lord and father, and decline appointment to the Grand Secretariat;

sentences.zh: 乃循例再疏，遽入辦事。

translations.literal: Yet he followed routine with a second memorial and hastened to take up duties.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he followed routine with a perfunctory second memorial and hastened to take up his duties.

sentences.zh: 夫人有所不忍，而後能及其所忍；

translations.literal: A person has things he cannot bear — only then can he extend to what he can bear;
translations.idiomatic: A man must have things he cannot bear before he can extend himself to what he can bear;

sentences.zh: 有所不為，而後可以有為。

translations.literal: Has things he will not do — only then can he accomplish something.
translations.idiomatic: he must have things he will not do before he can accomplish anything worth doing.

sentences.zh: 臣以嗣昌所忍，覘其所為，知嗣昌心失智短，必不能為國建功，何也？

translations.literal: Your subject observes what Sichang is willing to tolerate and watches what he does; I know his heart has lost its footing and his wisdom is short — he surely cannot achieve merit for the state. Why?
translations.idiomatic: Your subject observes what Sichang is willing to tolerate and watches what he does; I know his heart has lost its footing and his judgment is impaired — he surely cannot achieve merit for the state. Why?

sentences.zh: 成天下之事在乎誌，勝天下之任在乎氣；

translations.literal: Accomplishing the affairs under heaven depends on resolve; bearing up under heaven's burden depends on spirit;
translations.idiomatic: Accomplishing the affairs of the realm depends on resolve; bearing the empire's burden depends on spirit;

sentences.zh: 誌敗氣餒，而能任天下事，必無是理。

translations.literal: Resolve defeated and spirit exhausted — yet able to shoulder the empire's affairs? There is surely no such principle.
translations.idiomatic: With resolve broken and spirit exhausted, yet able to shoulder the empire's affairs? There is surely no such principle.

sentences.zh: 伎倆已窮，茍且富貴。

translations.literal: His tricks are exhausted; he clings to rank and fortune.
translations.idiomatic: His tricks are exhausted; he clings to rank and fortune.

sentences.zh: 兼樞部以重綸扉之權，借綸扉為解樞部之漸。

translations.literal: He combined the Military Board to augment Grand Secretariat power, and used the Grand Secretariat as a gradual means to shift blame from the Military Board.
translations.idiomatic: He combined the Military Board with the Grand Secretariat to augment his authority at court, and used the Secretariat as a gradual means to deflect blame from the military establishment.

sentences.zh: 和議自專，票擬由己。

translations.literal: He monopolized peace negotiations; draft memorials for imperial approval were his alone.
translations.idiomatic: He monopolized peace negotiations and reserved draft memorials for imperial approval to himself alone.

sentences.zh: 與方一藻、高起潛輩扶同罔功，掩敗為勝。

translations.literal: With Fang Yizao, Gao Qiqian, and the like he colluded to fake achievements and disguised defeat as victory.
translations.idiomatic: With Fang Yizao, Gao Qiqian, and their ilk he colluded to fake achievements and disguised defeat as victory.

sentences.zh: 歲糜金繒，養患邊圉。

translations.literal: Year after year he squandered gold and silk, nurturing danger on the borders.
translations.idiomatic: Year after year he squandered gold and silk, nurturing danger on the frontier.

sentences.zh: 立心如此，獨不畏堯、舜在上乎？

translations.literal: With a heart set like this, is he alone unafraid that Yao and Shun sit above?
translations.idiomatic: With a heart set like this, is he alone unafraid that Yao and Shun sit above?

sentences.zh: 曩自陛下切責議和，而嗣昌不可以為臣。

translations.literal: Formerly, when Your Majesty sternly rebuked the talk of peace, Sichang was already unfit to serve as minister.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly, when Your Majesty sternly rebuked the talk of peace, Sichang was already unfit to serve as minister.

sentences.zh: 今一旦忽易墨缞，而嗣昌不可以為子。

translations.literal: Now, suddenly casting off black mourning hemp, Sichang is unfit to serve as a son.
translations.idiomatic: Now, suddenly casting off black mourning hemp, Sichang is unfit to serve as a son.

sentences.zh: 若附和黨比，緘口全軀，嗣昌得罪名教，臣亦得罪名教矣。」

translations.literal: If I joined factions and kept silent to preserve my body, Sichang would offend the moral teachings — and your subject would offend the moral teachings as well.
translations.idiomatic: If I joined factions and kept silent to preserve my own safety, Sichang would offend the moral teachings — and your subject would offend them as well.

sentences.zh: 疏入，帝大怒，謫福建按察司知事。

translations.literal: When the memorial arrived, the Emperor was greatly angered and demoted him to Administrative Vice Commissioner of the Fujian Surveillance Commission.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial arrived, the Emperor was greatly angered and demoted him to Administrative Vice Commissioner of the Fujian Surveillance Commission.

sentences.zh: 移疾歸。

translations.literal: He pleaded illness and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: He pleaded illness and returned home.

sentences.zh: 廷臣屢薦，將召用，而京師陷。

translations.literal: Court officials repeatedly recommended him; he was about to be recalled when the capital fell.
translations.idiomatic: Court officials repeatedly recommended him, and he was about to be recalled when the capital fell.

sentences.zh: 福王立，召起故官，不赴。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Fu was enthroned, he was summoned to his former post but did not go.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Fu was enthroned, he was summoned to his former post but did not go.

sentences.zh: 明年五月，南都不守，江西郡縣多失。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the following year, the Southern Capital was lost and many counties and prefectures in Jiangxi fell.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of the following year, the Southern Capital was lost and many counties and prefectures in Jiangxi fell.

sentences.zh: 同升攜家將入福建，止雩都，與楊廷麟謀興復。

translations.literal: Tongsheng took his family intending to enter Fujian, stopped at Yudu, and plotted restoration with Yang Tinglin.
translations.idiomatic: Tongsheng took his family intending to enter Fujian, stopped at Yudu, and plotted restoration with Yang Tinglin.

sentences.zh: 唐王加同升祭酒。

translations.literal: The Tang Prince promoted Tongsheng to Grand Master of the Imperial Academy.
translations.idiomatic: The Tang Prince promoted Tongsheng to Grand Master of the Imperial Academy.

sentences.zh: 同升乃入贛州，偕廷麟籌兵食。

translations.literal: Tongsheng then entered Ganzhou and together with Tinglin gathered troops and provisions.
translations.idiomatic: Tongsheng then entered Ganzhou and together with Tinglin gathered troops and provisions.

sentences.zh: 取吉安、臨江，加詹事兼兵部左侍郎。

translations.literal: After recovering Ji'an and Linjiang, he was promoted to Junior Mentor concurrently as Vice Minister of the Left in the Ministry of War.
translations.idiomatic: After recovering Ji'an and Linjiang, he was promoted to Junior Mentor concurrently serving as Vice Minister of the Left in the Ministry of War.

sentences.zh: 同升已羸疾，日與士大夫講忠孝大節，聞者咸奮，以廷麟請，撫南、贛，十二，月卒於贛州。

translations.literal: Tongsheng was already frail and ill; daily he discussed with scholar-officials the great principles of loyalty and filial piety, and all who heard him were stirred. At Tinglin's request he was appointed Grand Coordinator of Southern Gan; in the twelfth month he died at Ganzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Tongsheng was already frail and ill; daily he discussed with scholar-officials the great principles of loyalty and filial piety, and all who heard him were stirred. At Tinglin's request he was appointed Grand Coordinator of Southern Gan; in the twelfth month he died at Ganzhou.

sentences.zh: 唐文獻，字元徵，華亭人。

translations.literal: Tang Wenxian, courtesy name Yuanzheng, a native of Huating.
translations.idiomatic: Tang Wenxian, courtesy name Yuanzheng, was a native of Huating.

sentences.zh: 萬歷十四年進士第一。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year of Wanli he ranked first among jinshi.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year of the Wanli reign he ranked first among jinshi.

sentences.zh: 授修撰，歷詹事。

translations.literal: Appointed Compiler; he rose to Junior Mentor.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Compiler and rose to Junior Mentor.

sentences.zh: 沈一貫以「妖書」事傾尚書郭正域，持之急。

translations.literal: Shen Yiguan used the "Demonic Book" affair to bring down Minister Guo Zhengyu and pressed the case urgently.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Yiguan used the Demonic Book affair to bring down Minister Guo Zhengyu and pressed the case urgently.

sentences.zh: 文獻偕其僚楊道賓、周如砥、陶望齡往見一貫曰：「郭公將不免，人謂公實有意殺之。」

translations.literal: Wenxian together with his colleagues Yang Daobin, Zhou Rudi, and Tao Wangling went to see Yiguan and said: "Minister Guo will not escape harm; people say you truly intend to kill him.
translations.idiomatic: Wenxian together with his colleagues Yang Daobin, Zhou Rudi, and Tao Wangling went to see Yiguan and said, "Minister Guo will not escape harm; people say you truly intend to kill him.

sentences.zh: 一貫踞蹐，酹地若為誓者。

translations.literal: Yiguan fidgeted uneasily and poured a libation on the ground as if swearing an oath.
translations.idiomatic: Yiguan fidgeted uneasily and poured a libation on the ground as if swearing an oath.

sentences.zh: 文獻曰：「亦知公無意殺之也，第臺省承風下石，而公不早訖此獄，何辭以謝天下。」

translations.literal: Wenxian said: "We also know you have no intent to kill him, but the censorate and ministries follow the wind to cast stones, and if you do not conclude this case early, with what words will you answer the world?
translations.idiomatic: Wenxian said, "We also know you have no intent to kill him, but the censorate and ministries follow the wind to cast stones, and if you do not conclude this case early, with what words will you answer the world?

sentences.zh: 一貫斂容謝之。

translations.literal: Yiguan composed his expression and apologized to them.
translations.idiomatic: Yiguan composed his expression and apologized to them.

sentences.zh: 望齡見朱賡不為救，亦正色責以大義，願棄官與正域同死。
