translations.literal: Wangling saw Zhu Geng fail to rescue him and likewise sternly rebuked him with the greater principle, declaring he would abandon office and die with Zhengyu.
translations.idiomatic: Wangling saw Zhu Geng fail to rescue Guo and likewise sternly rebuked him on principle, declaring he would abandon office and die with Zhengyu.

sentences.zh: 獄得稍解。

translations.literal: The case was somewhat eased.
translations.idiomatic: The case was somewhat eased.

sentences.zh: 然文獻等以是失政府意。

translations.literal: Yet Wenxian and the others for this lost favor with the government.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Wenxian and the others lost favor with the government for this.

sentences.zh: 久之，拜禮部右侍郎，掌翰林院事。

translations.literal: After some time he was appointed Vice Minister of the Right in the Ministry of Rites, directing Hanlin Academy affairs.
translations.idiomatic: After some time he was appointed Vice Minister of the Right in the Ministry of Rites and put in charge of Hanlin Academy affairs.

sentences.zh: 初，文獻出趙用賢門，以名節相矜許。

translations.literal: Earlier, Wenxian had been a follower of Zhao Yongxian's school and prided himself on reputation and integrity among peers.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Wenxian had been a follower of Zhao Yongxian's school and prided himself on reputation and integrity among his peers.

sentences.zh: 同年生給事中李沂劾張鯨被廷杖，文獻掖之出，資給其湯藥。

translations.literal: A fellow graduate, Supervising Secretary Li Yi, was beaten at court for impeaching Zhang Jing; Wenxian supported him out and supplied him with medicines.
translations.idiomatic: A fellow graduate, Supervising Secretary Li Yi, was beaten at court for impeaching Zhang Jing; Wenxian supported him out and supplied him with medicines.

sentences.zh: 荊州推官華鈺忤稅監逮下詔獄，文獻力周旋，得無死。

translations.literal: Hua Yu, magistrate's assistant at Jingzhou, offended a tax eunuch supervisor and was arrested into the imperial prison; Wenxian exerted himself to intercede, and Hua escaped death.
translations.idiomatic: Hua Yu, magistrate's assistant at Jingzhou, offended a tax eunuch supervisor and was arrested into the imperial prison; Wenxian exerted himself to intercede, and Hua escaped death.

sentences.zh: 掌翰林日，當考察，執政欲庇一人，執不許。

translations.literal: When directing the Hanlin Academy, during the evaluation period the chief ministers wished to shield someone; he firmly refused to allow it.
translations.idiomatic: While directing the Hanlin Academy, during the evaluation period the chief ministers wished to shield someone; he firmly refused.

sentences.zh: 卒官。

translations.literal: He died in office.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office.

sentences.zh: 贈禮部尚書，謚文恪。

translations.literal: Posthumously made Minister of Rites; posthumous name Wenkè.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made Minister of Rites and given the posthumous name Wenkè.

sentences.zh: 楊道賓，字惟彥，晉江人。

translations.literal: Yang Daobin, courtesy name Weiyan, a native of Jinjiang.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Daobin, courtesy name Weiyan, was a native of Jinjiang.

sentences.zh: 萬歷十四年進士第二，授編修。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year of Wanli he ranked second among jinshi and was appointed Compiler.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year of the Wanli reign he ranked second among jinshi and was appointed Compiler.

sentences.zh: 累遷國子祭酒，少詹事，禮部右侍郎，掌翰林院事。

translations.literal: He was promoted in succession to Grand Master of the Imperial Academy, Junior Mentor, Vice Minister of the Right in the Ministry of Rites, directing Hanlin Academy affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He rose in succession to Grand Master of the Imperial Academy, Junior Mentor, and Vice Minister of the Right in the Ministry of Rites, directing Hanlin Academy affairs.

sentences.zh: 轉左，改掌部事。

translations.literal: He was transferred to the left and changed to directing the ministry's affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to the left vice ministership and put in charge of the ministry's affairs.

sentences.zh: 嘗因星變，請釋逮系知縣滿朝薦等，又請亟舉朝講大典，皆不報。

translations.literal: Once, on account of a celestial anomaly, he requested release of the detained county magistrate Man Chaojian and others, and also urgently requested the great ceremony of morning lectures — all went unanswered.
translations.idiomatic: Once, on account of a celestial anomaly, he requested the release of the detained county magistrate Man Chaojian and others, and also urgently requested restoration of the great ceremony of morning lectures — all went unanswered.

sentences.zh: 南京大水，疏陳時政，略言：「宮中夜分方寢，日旰未起，致萬幾怠曠。

translations.literal: When Nanjing suffered great flooding, he submitted a memorial on current affairs, stating in summary: "Within the palace one sleeps only after midnight and does not rise until the sun is high, causing the myriad affairs of state to be neglected and delayed.
translations.idiomatic: When Nanjing suffered great flooding, he submitted a memorial on current affairs, stating in summary, "Within the palace Your Majesty sleeps only after midnight and does not rise until the sun is high, causing the myriad affairs of state to be neglected and delayed.

sentences.zh: 請夙興夜寐，以圖治功。

translations.literal: I request rising early and retiring late, to seek the achievements of good governance.
translations.idiomatic: I urge Your Majesty to rise early and retire late, to seek the achievements of good governance.

sentences.zh: 時禦便殿，與大臣面決大政。

translations.literal: At times hold audience in the informal hall and decide great affairs face to face with ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Hold audience at times in the informal hall and decide great affairs face to face with your ministers.

sentences.zh: 章疏及時批答，毋輒留中及從內降。」

translations.literal: Memorials should be promptly answered with rescripts; do not casually keep them at court or issue decisions from within the palace.
translations.idiomatic: Memorials should be promptly answered with rescripts; do not casually keep them at court or issue decisions from within the palace.

sentences.zh: 帝優旨報聞。

translations.literal: The Emperor responded with a gracious edict acknowledging receipt.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor responded with a gracious edict acknowledging receipt.

sentences.zh: 皇太子輟講已四年，道賓極諫，引唐宦官仇士良語為戒。

translations.literal: The Crown Prince had ceased lectures for four years; Daobin remonstrated urgently, citing the words of the Tang eunuch Qiu Shiliang as a warning.
translations.idiomatic: The Crown Prince had ceased lectures for four years; Daobin remonstrated urgently, citing the words of the Tang eunuch Qiu Shiliang as a warning.

sentences.zh: 其冬，天鼓鳴，道賓言：「天之視聽在民。

translations.literal: That winter the sky drum sounded; Daobin said: "Heaven's eyes and ears are in the people.
translations.idiomatic: That winter the sky drum sounded; Daobin said, "Heaven's eyes and ears are in the people.

sentences.zh: 今民生顛躓，無所赴訴，天若代為之鳴。

translations.literal: Now the people's livelihood is overturned and stumbling; they have nowhere to appeal — heaven seems to sound on their behalf.
translations.idiomatic: Now the people's livelihood is in turmoil and they have nowhere to appeal — heaven seems to sound on their behalf.

sentences.zh: 宜急罷礦使，更張闕政，以和民心。」

translations.literal: It is fitting urgently to abolish mine tax eunuchs, reform deficient policies, and harmonize the people's hearts.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty should urgently abolish the mine tax eunuchs, reform deficient policies, and harmonize the people's hearts.

sentences.zh: 帝不聽。

translations.literal: The Emperor did not heed it.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor did not heed it.

sentences.zh: 逾年卒官。

translations.literal: After more than a year he died in office.
translations.idiomatic: After more than a year he died in office.

sentences.zh: 贈禮部尚書，謚文恪。

translations.literal: Posthumously made Minister of Rites; posthumous name Wenkè.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made Minister of Rites and given the posthumous name Wenkè.

sentences.zh: 陶望齡，字周望，會稽人。

translations.literal: Tao Wangling, courtesy name Zhouwang, a native of Kuaiji.
translations.idiomatic: Tao Wangling, courtesy name Zhouwang, was a native of Kuaiji.

sentences.zh: 父承學，南京禮部尚書。

translations.literal: His father Chengxue was Minister of Rites at Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: His father Chengxue was Minister of Rites at Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 望齡少有文名。

translations.literal: Wangling from youth had a literary reputation.
translations.idiomatic: Wangling had a literary reputation from youth.

sentences.zh: 舉萬歷十七年會試第一，殿試一甲第三，授編修，歷官國子祭酒。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year of Wanli he ranked first in the metropolitan examination; in the palace examination he placed third in the first class and was appointed Compiler; he served in succession as Grand Master of the Imperial Academy.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year of the Wanli reign he ranked first in the metropolitan examination; in the palace examination he placed third in the first class and was appointed Compiler; he rose in succession to Grand Master of the Imperial Academy.

sentences.zh: 篤嗜王守仁說，所宗者周汝登。

translations.literal: He was deeply devoted to Wang Shouren's teachings; the one he took as his master was Zhou Rudeng.
translations.idiomatic: He was deeply devoted to Wang Yangming's teachings and took Zhou Rudeng as his intellectual master.

sentences.zh: 與弟奭齡皆以講學名。

translations.literal: He and his younger brother Shiling were both famed for lecturing on learning.
translations.idiomatic: He and his younger brother Shiling were both celebrated as lecturers in the Neo-Confucian tradition.

sentences.zh: 卒謚文簡。

translations.literal: Upon death he was given the posthumous name Wen Jian.
translations.idiomatic: After his death he was posthumously honored with the title Wen Jian.

sentences.zh: 李騰芳，字子實，湘潭人。

translations.literal: Li Tengfang, courtesy name Zishi, was a native of Xiangtan.
translations.idiomatic: Li Tengfang, courtesy name Zishi, was from Xiangtan.

sentences.zh: 萬歷二十年進士。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year of Wanli he passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: He became a jinshi in the twentieth year of the Wanli reign.

sentences.zh: 改庶吉士。

translations.literal: He was transferred to be a Hanlin bachelor.
translations.idiomatic: He entered the Hanlin Academy as a bachelor.

sentences.zh: 好學，負才名。

translations.literal: He loved learning and bore a reputation for talent.
translations.idiomatic: A devoted scholar, he enjoyed a strong reputation for literary talent.

sentences.zh: 三王並封旨下，騰芳為書詣朝房投大學士王錫爵略言：「公欲暫承上意，巧借封王，轉作冊立。

translations.literal: When the edict on jointly enfeoffing the three princes was issued, Tengfang wrote a letter, went to the Hanlin office, and delivered it to Grand Secretary Wang Xijue, stating briefly: "Your Excellency wishes temporarily to accede to the emperor's wish, cleverly borrowing the enfeoffment of princes to transform it into investiture as heir.
translations.idiomatic: When the edict arrived to enfeoff all three princes at once, Tengfang wrote a letter, went to the Hanlin office, and handed it to Grand Secretary Wang Xijue. He wrote in brief: "Your Excellency mean to defer to the emperor's wish for the moment, using the enfeoffment of princes as a clever means to turn the affair toward formal investiture of the heir.

sentences.zh: 然恐王封既定，大典愈遲。

translations.literal: But I fear that once the princes' enfeoffment is settled, the great ceremony will be further delayed.
translations.idiomatic: But I fear that once the princes have been enfeoffed, the great ceremony of investiture will only be pushed further off.

sentences.zh: 他日公去而事壞，罪公始謀，何辭以解？

translations.literal: If one day Your Excellency departs and the affair goes bad, blame will fall on Your Excellency as the original planner — with what words could you exonerate yourself?
translations.idiomatic: If one day you leave office and the affair collapses, you will be blamed as the one who first devised it. What defense could you offer then?

sentences.zh: 此不獨宗社憂，亦公子孫禍也。」

translations.literal: This is not only a concern for the altars of state and grain, but also a calamity for Your Excellency's descendants."
translations.idiomatic: This threatens not only the altars of state, but also brings calamity upon your descendants."

sentences.zh: 錫爵讀未竟，遽牽衣命坐，曰：「諸人詈我，我何以自明？

translations.literal: Xijue, before finishing reading, quickly grabbed his robe and ordered him to sit, saying: "Everyone curses me — how can I make myself clear?
translations.idiomatic: Xijue had not finished reading when he seized Tengfang's sleeve and bade him sit. "Everyone reviles me," he said. "How am I to clear myself?

sentences.zh: 如子言，我受教。

translations.literal: As you say, I accept your instruction.
translations.idiomatic: As you say — I accept your counsel.

sentences.zh: 但我疏必親書，謂子孫禍何也？」

translations.literal: But my memorial must be written in my own hand — what do you mean by calamity for descendants?"
translations.idiomatic: But my memorial must be written in my own hand. What do you mean by calamity for my descendants?"

sentences.zh: 騰芳曰：「外廷正以公手書密揭，無由知其詳，公乃欲藉以自解。

translations.literal: Tengfang said: "The outer court precisely because Your Excellency's handwriting is on the secret memorial has no way to know the details — yet Your Excellency still wishes to use this to exonerate yourself.
translations.idiomatic: Tengfang replied: "The outer court knows only that your own hand wrote the secret memorial and has no way to learn the full story — yet you still mean to use that to exonerate yourself.

sentences.zh: 異日能使天子出公手書示天下乎？」

translations.literal: On another day can you make the Son of Heaven produce Your Excellency's handwritten document and show it to the world?"
translations.idiomatic: Can you one day make the Son of Heaven produce your own handwriting and show it to the world?"

sentences.zh: 錫爵憮然淚下，明日遂反並封之詔。

translations.literal: Xijue looked dejected, tears falling; the next day he reversed the joint enfeoffment edict.
translations.idiomatic: Xijue sat stricken, tears streaming down his face. The next day he reversed the edict for joint enfeoffment.

sentences.zh: 屢遷左諭德。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Left Reader.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through successive promotions to Left Reader.

sentences.zh: 騰芳與山顧天飐善。

translations.literal: Tengfang was on good terms with Gu Tianyi of Kunshan.
translations.idiomatic: Tengfang was on close terms with Kunshan Gu Tianyi.

sentences.zh: 天飐險诐無行，為世所指名，被劾去，騰芳亦投劾歸。

translations.literal: Tianyi was treacherous and deceitful with no proper conduct, was pointed out by the world by name, was impeached and dismissed; Tengfang also submitted impeachment and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: Tianyi was treacherous and unscrupulous, notorious throughout the realm. After he was impeached and dismissed, Tengfang too submitted his resignation and went home.

sentences.zh: 時遂有顧黨、李黨之目。

translations.literal: At the time there emerged the designations Gu Clique and Li Clique.
translations.idiomatic: At the time people began to speak of a Gu faction and a Li faction.

sentences.zh: 詔論朝士擅去者罪，貶騰芳太常博士。

translations.literal: An edict discussed punishment for court scholars who left without authorization; Tengfang was demoted to Doctor of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: An edict laid out penalties for court officials who left their posts without permission, and Tengfang was demoted to Doctor of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 三十九年京察，復以浮躁謫江西都司理問。

translations.literal: In the thirty-ninth year, at the capital evaluation, he was again for being frivolous and impetuous demoted to Director of Administration in Jiangxi's military commission.
translations.idiomatic: At the capital evaluation in the thirty-ninth year, he was again found frivolous and impetuous and was demoted to Director of Administration in the Jiangxi military commission.

sentences.zh: 稍遷行人司正，歷太常少卿，掌司業事。

translations.literal: Shortly he was promoted to Director of the Department of Envoys, served as Vice Minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, and managed the affairs of Supervisor of Instruction.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon promoted to Director of the Department of Envoys, then served as Vice Minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and took charge of the Supervisor of Instruction's duties.

sentences.zh: 光宗立，擢少詹事，署南京翰林院。

translations.literal: When Guangzong ascended, he was promoted to Junior Guardian and acted as head of the Nanjing Hanlin Academy.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Guangzong took the throne, Tengfang was promoted to Junior Guardian and placed in charge of the Nanjing Hanlin Academy.

sentences.zh: 旋拜禮部右侍郎，教習庶吉士。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed Right Vice Minister of Rites and instructed Hanlin bachelors.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon appointed Right Vice Minister of Rites and took charge of instructing the Hanlin bachelors.

sentences.zh: 御史王安舜劾騰芳驟遷。

translations.literal: Censor Wang Anshun impeached Tengfang for rapid promotion.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Wang Anshun impeached Tengfang for his sudden rise in rank.

sentences.zh: 騰芳辭位，熹宗不許，竟以省母歸。

translations.literal: Tengfang resigned his post; Xizong did not permit it; ultimately he returned home to visit his mother.
translations.idiomatic: Tengfang offered to resign, but the Xizong Emperor refused. In the end he went home to care for his mother.

sentences.zh: 天啟初，以故官協理詹事府，尋改吏部左侍郎。

translations.literal: Early in Tianqi, with his former rank he assisted in managing the Grand Mentor's office; soon he was changed to Left Vice Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Tianqi reign he returned to his former rank to assist in the Grand Mentor's office, and was soon transferred to Left Vice Minister of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 丁內艱，加禮部尚書以歸。

translations.literal: Upon domestic mourning, he was additionally made Minister of Rites when returning home.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother died he entered mourning and was granted the additional title of Minister of Rites on his return home.

sentences.zh: 魏忠賢惡騰芳與楊漣同鄉。

translations.literal: Wei Zhongxian hated that Tengfang was from the same native place as Yang Lian.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Zhongxian hated Tengfang for being a fellow townsman of Yang Lian.

sentences.zh: 御史王際逵因論騰芳被察驟起，丁憂進官，皆非制。

translations.literal: Censor Wang Jikui therefore discussed Tengfang being rapidly raised after capital evaluation and promoted during mourning — all contrary to regulations.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Wang Jikui then argued that Tengfang's sudden recall after a poor capital evaluation and his promotion while in mourning were both irregular.

sentences.zh: 遂削奪。

translations.literal: Thereupon he was stripped and deprived.
translations.idiomatic: He was thereupon stripped of rank and honors.

sentences.zh: 崇禎初，再以尚書協理詹事府。

translations.literal: Early in Chongzhen, again with the title of Minister he assisted in the Grand Mentor's office.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Chongzhen reign he was again appointed Minister and assigned to assist in the Grand Mentor's office.

sentences.zh: 京師戒嚴，條畫守禦，多稱旨，代何如寵掌部事。

translations.literal: When the capital was under martial law, his plans for defense pleased the throne in many points; he replaced He Ruchong in managing ministry affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When the capital was placed under martial law, his plans for defense largely met with imperial approval, and he replaced He Ruchong in managing the ministry's affairs.

sentences.zh: 卒官。

translations.literal: He died in office.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office.

sentences.zh: 贈太子太保。

translations.literal: Posthumously he was made Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously honored as Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 蔡毅中，字宏甫，光山人。

translations.literal: Cai Yizhong, courtesy name Hongfu, was a native of Guangshan.
translations.idiomatic: Cai Yizhong, courtesy name Hongfu, was from Guangshan.

sentences.zh: 祖鳳翹，平陽同知。

translations.literal: His grandfather Fengqiao was sub-prefect of Pingyang.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Fengqiao served as sub-prefect of Pingyang.

sentences.zh: 父光，臨洮同知。

translations.literal: His father Guang was sub-prefect of Lintao.
translations.idiomatic: His father Guang served as sub-prefect of Lintao.

sentences.zh: 毅中五歲通《孝經》。

translations.literal: At five years of age Yizhong mastered the Classic of Filial Piety.
translations.idiomatic: At the age of five Yizhong had mastered the Classic of Filial Piety.

sentences.zh: 父問：「讀書何為？」

translations.literal: His father asked: "What is reading for?"
translations.idiomatic: His father asked, "Why do you read?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「欲為聖賢耳。」

translations.literal: He replied: "To become a sage or worthy."
translations.idiomatic: He answered, "To become a sage or worthy."

sentences.zh: 萬歷二十九年第進士，改庶吉士，授檢討。

translations.literal: In the twenty-ninth year of Wanli he ranked as an advanced jinshi, was transferred to be a Hanlin bachelor, and was appointed examining editor.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-ninth year of the Wanli reign he passed the jinshi examination with honors, entered the Hanlin Academy as a bachelor, and was appointed examining editor.

sentences.zh: 時礦稅虐民，毅中取《祖訓》、《會典》諸書禁戒礦稅者，集為二卷，註釋以上。

translations.literal: At the time mine taxes oppressed the people; Yizhong took from the Ancestral Instructions, Collected Statutes, and other books passages forbidding mine taxes, compiled them into two volumes, annotated them, and submitted them upward.
translations.idiomatic: At the time mine taxes were crushing the people. Yizhong gathered from the Ancestral Instructions, the Collected Statutes, and other works every passage forbidding mine taxes, compiled them into two annotated volumes, and submitted them to the throne.

sentences.zh: 大學士沈鯉於毅中為鄉先達，與首輔沈一貫不相能。

translations.literal: Grand Secretary Shen Li regarded Yizhong as a senior from the same district; he did not get along with chief assistant Shen Yiguan.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Secretary Shen Li looked on Yizhong as a senior fellow townsman and was at odds with Chief Grand Secretary Shen Yiguan.

sentences.zh: 而溫純參政河南，器毅中於諸生。

translations.literal: Meanwhile Wen Chun was administering Henan and recognized Yizhong's talent among the students.
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile Wen Chun, administering Henan, had recognized Yizhong's talent when he was still a student.

sentences.zh: 至是為都御史，疏侵一貫。

translations.literal: By now he was Censor-in-Chief; his memorial attacked Yiguan.
translations.idiomatic: By then Wen Chun had become Censor-in-Chief and submitted a memorial attacking Yiguan.

sentences.zh: 一貫疑出毅中手，為鯉地，銜之，遂用計典，鐫秩去。

translations.literal: Yiguan suspected it came from Yizhong's hand, to give Shen Li advantage; he nursed resentment, used the capital evaluation, stripped his rank, and dismissed him.
translations.idiomatic: Yiguan suspected the memorial had been written by Yizhong to give Shen Li an advantage. Nursing a grudge, he used the capital evaluation to strip Yizhong of rank and dismiss him.

sentences.zh: 起麻城丞。

translations.literal: He was raised as assistant magistrate of Macheng.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled as assistant magistrate of Macheng.

sentences.zh: 旋以行人司副召擢尚寶丞。

translations.literal: Soon he was summoned as Vice Director of the Department of Envoys and promoted to Assistant Director of the Court of Imperial Stud.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon summoned as Vice Director of the Department of Envoys and promoted to Assistant Director of the Court of the Imperial Stud.

sentences.zh: 移疾歸。

translations.literal: He cited illness and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: He pleaded illness and returned home.

sentences.zh: 四十五年，以浮躁鐫秩。

translations.literal: In the forty-fifth year, for being frivolous and impetuous his rank was stripped.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-fifth year he was again stripped of rank for frivolity and impetuosity.

sentences.zh: 天啟初，大起廢籍，補長蘆鹽運判官。

translations.literal: Early in Tianqi, those on the dismissal register were widely recalled; he was appointed salt transport judge of Changlu.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Tianqi reign, officials on the dismissal register were widely recalled, and he was appointed salt transport judge of Changlu.

sentences.zh: 屢遷國子祭酒，擢禮部右侍郎，仍領祭酒事。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Chancellor of the National University, promoted to Right Vice Minister of Rites, and still oversaw chancellor duties.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through successive promotions to Chancellor of the National University, then to Right Vice Minister of Rites while continuing to oversee the university.

sentences.zh: 楊漣劾魏忠賢得嚴旨，毅中率其屬抗疏言：

translations.literal: Yang Lian's impeachment of Wei Zhongxian received a stern edict; Yizhong led his subordinates in a memorial of resistance, saying:
translations.idiomatic: When Yang Lian's impeachment of Wei Zhongxian drew a stern imperial response, Yizhong led his subordinates in a defiant memorial that read:

sentences.zh: 學校者，天下公議所從出也。

translations.literal: Schools are where public opinion of the realm emerges.
translations.idiomatic: The schools are where the public opinion of the realm finds expression.

sentences.zh: 臣正與諸生講「為君難」一書，忽接楊漣劾忠賢疏，合監師生千有余人，無不鼓掌稱慶。

translations.literal: I was just lecturing to students on the book "The Difficulties of Being a Ruler" when suddenly I received Yang Lian's memorial impeaching Zhongxian; the assembled supervisors and students, more than a thousand in all, all applauded in celebration.
translations.idiomatic: I was just lecturing my students on The Difficulties of Being a Ruler when Yang Lian's memorial impeaching Zhongxian arrived. More than a thousand supervisors and students assembled — not one failed to applaud in celebration.

sentences.zh: 乃皇上不下其奏於九卿，而謂一切朝政皆親裁，以奸珰為忠，代之受過，合監師生無不捫心悉嘆不已也。

translations.literal: Yet the emperor did not send this memorial down to the nine ministers, but said all court affairs are personally decided — treating the treacherous eunuch as loyal and taking blame on his behalf — all supervisors and students could not stop clasping their hearts and sighing without end.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Your Majesty did not refer the memorial to the nine ministers for deliberation, but declared that all court affairs are personally decided — treating a treacherous eunuch as loyal and bearing blame on his behalf. Every supervisor and student present could only clasp his heart and sigh without end.

sentences.zh: 臣惟三代以後，漢、隋、唐、宋諸君，其受權珰之害與處權珰之法，載在《通鑒》。

translations.literal: I consider that after the Three Dynasties, the Han, Sui, Tang, and Song emperors — how they suffered from powerful eunuchs and how they dealt with them — are recorded in the Comprehensive Mirror.
translations.idiomatic: After the Three Dynasties, how the emperors of Han, Sui, Tang, and Song suffered at the hands of powerful eunuchs and how they dealt with them — all this is recorded in the Comprehensive Mirror.

sentences.zh: 我朝列聖受權珰之害與處權珰之法，載在實錄。

translations.literal: Our dynasty's successive sage emperors' suffering from powerful eunuchs and methods for dealing with them are recorded in the Veritable Records.
translations.idiomatic: How our own dynasty's successive sage emperors suffered from powerful eunuchs and how they handled them is recorded in the Veritable Records.

sentences.zh: 臣皆不必多言。

translations.literal: I need not say much more on these.
translations.idiomatic: On these matters I need say no more.

sentences.zh: 但取至近至親如武宗之處劉瑾、神宗之處馮保二事，願皇上遵之。

translations.literal: But take two most recent and close examples — Wuzong's handling of Liu Jin and Shenzong's handling of Feng Bao — I wish the emperor would follow them.
translations.idiomatic: But take only two recent and close examples — how Emperor Wuzong dealt with Liu Jin and how Emperor Shenzong dealt with Feng Bao — and I beg Your Majesty to follow them.

sentences.zh: 瑾在武宗左右，言聽計從，一聞諸臣劾奏，夜半自起，擒而殺之。

translations.literal: Jin was at Wuzong's side; his words were obeyed and plans followed. At first hearing officials' impeachments, at midnight he rose himself, seized Jin, and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: Jin stood at Wuzong's side with his every word obeyed and every plan followed. Yet at the first report of officials' impeachments, the emperor rose at midnight, seized Jin, and had him executed.

sentences.zh: 神宗臨禦方十齡，保左右扶持，盡心竭力。

translations.literal: Shenzong when assuming rule was just ten years of age; Bao supported and assisted at his side, exhausting heart and strength.
translations.idiomatic: When Shenzong first took the throne he was only ten years old. Bao supported him at his side and served him with all his heart and strength.

sentences.zh: 既而少作威福，臺省劾奏，未聞舉朝公疏，神祖遂不動聲色而戍保於南京。

translations.literal: Afterwards he somewhat wielded authority for personal benefit; the censorate impeached him. Though no memorial came from the entire court, the Divine Ancestor quietly, without showing emotion, banished Bao to Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: Later Bao began to wield authority for his own benefit, and the censorate impeached him. Though no memorial came from the entire court, the Divine Ancestor quietly, without a show of emotion, banished Bao to Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 今忠賢無保之功，而極瑾之惡。

translations.literal: Now Zhongxian has none of Bao's merit but the extreme of Jin's evil.
translations.idiomatic: Today Zhongxian has none of Bao's merit, yet equals Jin in wickedness.

sentences.zh: 二十四罪，無一不當悉究。

translations.literal: The twenty-four crimes — not one should fail to be fully investigated.
translations.idiomatic: Of the twenty-four crimes charged against him, not one should go uninvestigated.

sentences.zh: 舉朝群臣欲於朝罷，跪以候旨，忠賢遂要皇上入宮，不禮群臣。

translations.literal: Officials of the entire court wished at the end of court to kneel and wait for an edict; Zhongxian then forced the emperor to enter the palace and showed no courtesy to the officials.
translations.idiomatic: The officials of the entire court wished to kneel after court and await an edict, but Zhongxian forced the emperor to enter the palace and showed no courtesy to the assembled ministers.

sentences.zh: 今又欲於視學之日，群臣及太學諸生面叩陳請矣，而皇上漫不經意。

translations.literal: Now again on the day of the imperial study visit, officials and students of the Imperial Academy wished to face him and petition directly, yet the emperor was completely unconcerned.
translations.idiomatic: Now, on the day of the imperial visit to the academy, ministers and students of the Imperial University wished to face Your Majesty and petition directly — yet Your Majesty has treated the matter with complete indifference.

sentences.zh: 數日以來，但有及忠賢者，留中不發，如此蒙蔽，其中寧可測哉！

translations.literal: In recent days, whatever concerned Zhongxian was held at court unpublished — such concealment; what within can be measured!
translations.idiomatic: In recent days, every memorial touching on Zhongxian has been held at court and never issued. Under such concealment, who can fathom what lies within!

sentences.zh: 乞將漣疏發九卿科道從公究問，即不加劉瑾之誅，而以處馮保之法懲之，則恩威並著，與神祖媲美矣。

translations.literal: I beg that Lian's memorial be sent to the nine ministers and censorate for fair investigation; even if not Liu Jin's execution, punish with the method used on Feng Bao — then grace and authority will both be displayed, matching the Divine Ancestor.
translations.idiomatic: I beg that Yang Lian's memorial be referred to the nine ministers and the censorate for impartial investigation. Even if Your Majesty does not impose Liu Jin's punishment, apply the method used against Feng Bao — then grace and authority will both be displayed, and Your Majesty will stand beside the Divine Ancestor.

sentences.zh: 疏入，忠賢戟手大訽。

translations.literal: When the memorial entered, Zhongxian pointed with his halberd and cursed loudly.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial arrived, Zhongxian shook his fist and cursed loudly.

sentences.zh: 毅中乃再疏乞歸，不許。

translations.literal: Yizhong then submitted another memorial begging to retire; it was not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: Yizhong then submitted another memorial begging to retire, but permission was refused.

sentences.zh: 已，嗾其黨劾罷之。

translations.literal: Shortly after, he incited his faction to impeach and dismiss him.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he incited his faction to impeach Yizhong and have him dismissed.

sentences.zh: 毅中有至性。

translations.literal: Yizhong had utmost filial nature.
translations.idiomatic: Yizhong possessed a deeply filial nature.

sentences.zh: 四歲父病，籲天請代。

translations.literal: At four years of age, when his father fell ill, he cried to heaven asking to substitute.
translations.idiomatic: When he was four his father fell ill, and he cried to heaven, begging to take his father's place.

sentences.zh: 公車時，聞母喪，一慟嘔血數升，終喪斷酒肉，不入內寢。

translations.literal: When going to the capital for the examination, he heard of his mother's death; one sob brought forth several sheng of vomited blood. For the whole mourning period he abstained from wine and meat and did not enter the inner chamber.
translations.idiomatic: While traveling to the capital for the examination, he learned of his mother's death. A single sob brought forth several pints of blood. Throughout the mourning period he abstained from wine and meat and would not enter the inner chamber.

sentences.zh: 方母病，盛夏思冰，盂水忽凍。

translations.literal: When his mother was ill, in midsummer she craved ice — a bowl of water suddenly froze.
translations.idiomatic: While his mother was ill, she craved ice in the height of summer — and a bowl of water in the room suddenly froze.

sentences.zh: 廬居，有紫芝、白鳥、千鴉集墓之異。

translations.literal: Living in a mourning hut, there were wondrous signs of purple fungus, white birds, and a thousand crows gathering at the tomb.
translations.idiomatic: While living in a mourning hut by the grave, there were wondrous signs — purple fungus, white birds, and a thousand crows gathering at the tomb.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈禮部尚書。

translations.literal: On death he was posthumously made Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: After his death he was posthumously honored as Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 公鼐，字孝與，蒙陰人。

translations.literal: Gong Nai, courtesy name Xiaoyu, was a native of Mengyin.
translations.idiomatic: Gong Nai, courtesy name Xiaoyu, was from Mengyin.

sentences.zh: 曾祖奎躋，湖廣副使。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Kuiji was Vice Commissioner of Huguang.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Kuiji served as Vice Commissioner of Huguang.

sentences.zh: 父家臣，翰林編修。

translations.literal: His father Jiache was a Hanlin compiler.
translations.idiomatic: His father Jiache was a Hanlin compiler.

sentences.zh: 鼐舉萬二十上九年進士，改庶吉士，授編修。

translations.literal: In the twenty-ninth year of Wanli, Nai passed the jinshi examination, was transferred to be a Hanlin bachelor, and was appointed compiler.
translations.idiomatic: Nai passed the jinshi examination in the twenty-ninth year of the Wanli reign, entered the Hanlin Academy as a bachelor, and was appointed compiler.

sentences.zh: 屢遷左諭德，為東宮講官。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Left Reader and served as lecturer to the Eastern Palace.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through successive promotions to Left Reader and served as lecturer to the crown prince.

sentences.zh: 進左庶子，引疾歸。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Left Associate Crown Prince, cited illness, and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to Left Associate Crown Prince, he pleaded illness and returned home.

sentences.zh: 光宗立，召拜祭酒。

translations.literal: When Guangzong ascended, he was summoned and appointed Chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Guangzong took the throne, Nai was summoned and appointed Chancellor of the National University.

sentences.zh: 熹宗進鼐詹事，乃上疏曰：「近聞南北臣僚，論先帝升遐一事，跡涉怪異，語多隱藏。

translations.literal: Xizong promoted Nai to Grand Mentor; he then submitted a memorial saying: "Recently I have heard north and south officials discussing the matter of the Former Emperor's death — traces involve strange anomalies, words much hidden.
translations.idiomatic: The Xizong Emperor promoted Nai to Grand Mentor, whereupon he submitted a memorial: "Recently I have heard officials north and south discussing the Former Emperor's death — the accounts involve strange anomalies, and much is left unsaid.

sentences.zh: 恐因委巷之訛傳，流為湘山之稗說，臣竊痛焉。

translations.literal: I fear that alleyway false rumors will flow into Xiangshan apocryphal tales — I am privately pained.
translations.idiomatic: I fear that alleyway gossip will harden into the apocryphal legends of Mount Xiang — and this pains me deeply.

sentences.zh: 皇祖在昔，原無立愛之心。

translations.literal: The imperial grandfather in the past originally had no mind to establish a favorite son.
translations.idiomatic: Our imperial grandfather originally had no intention of favoring one son over another.

sentences.zh: 只因大典遲回，於是繳還冊立之後，有三王並封之事，《憂危竑議》之後，有國本攸關之事。

translations.literal: Only because the great ceremony was delayed; after returning the investiture edict came the matter of jointly enfeoffing three princes; after the "Anxiety and Danger Hidden Discussion" came matters concerning the foundation of the state.
translations.idiomatic: Only because the great ceremony of investiture was long delayed — after the investiture edict was withdrawn came the affair of jointly enfeoffing three princes; after the Hidden Discussion of Anxiety and Danger came affairs that threatened the very foundation of the realm.

sentences.zh: 迨龐、劉之邪謀，張差之梃擊，而逆亂極矣。

translations.literal: Until the evil schemes of Pang and Liu, Zhang Cha's club attack — rebellion reached its extreme.
translations.idiomatic: Then came the wicked plots of Pang and Liu, Zhang Cha's club assault — and treason reached its height.

sentences.zh: 臣嘗備員宮僚，目睹狂謀孔熾，以歸向東宮者為小人，不向東宮者為君子，盡除朝士之清流，陰翦元良之羽翼，批根引蔓，幹紀亂常。

translations.literal: I once served on the palace staff, witnessed raging conspiracy; those oriented toward the Eastern Palace were called petty men, those not oriented toward it were called gentlemen; they purged the clear-stream officials of the court, secretly cut the heir apparent's wings, uprooting and spreading vines, violating discipline and disturbing norms.
translations.idiomatic: I once served on the palace staff and saw the conspiracy rage unchecked. Those who sided with the Eastern Palace were called petty men; those who did not were called gentlemen. The clear-stream officials of the court were purged, the heir apparent's supporters were secretly cut down — roots torn up, tendrils spread — until discipline was broken and order overturned.

sentences.zh: 至今追想，猶為寒心。

translations.literal: Thinking back to this day, one still chills the heart.
translations.idiomatic: To recall it even now still chills the heart.

sentences.zh: 夫臣子愛君，存其真不存其偽。

translations.literal: Ministers and subjects love the ruler — preserve the true, not the false.
translations.idiomatic: Ministers and subjects who love their ruler preserve what is true, not what is false.

sentences.zh: 今實錄纂修在即，請將光宗事跡，別為一錄。

translations.literal: Now the Veritable Records compilation is imminent — I request that Guangzong's deeds be set apart in a separate record.
translations.idiomatic: The compilation of the Veritable Records is now at hand. I ask that Emperor Guangzong's deeds be set apart in a separate volume.

sentences.zh: 凡一月間明綸善政，固大書特書；

translations.literal: All enlightened edicts and good policies within that one month — certainly record them prominently and specially;
translations.idiomatic: Every enlightened edict and worthy policy of that single month should be recorded prominently;

sentences.zh: 其有聞見異詞及宮闈委曲之妙用，亦皆直筆指陳，勒成信史。

translations.literal: Also whatever variant accounts heard and seen and subtle uses within the palace walls — all should be recorded frankly with the straight brush, forged into trustworthy history.
translations.idiomatic: and whatever variant accounts there may be, and whatever subtle measures taken within the palace walls, should likewise be set down frankly with the historian's straight brush and forged into trustworthy history.

sentences.zh: 臣雖不肖，竊敢任之。」

translations.literal: Though I am unworthy, I privately dare undertake it.
translations.idiomatic: Unworthy though I am, I dare undertake this task.

sentences.zh: 疏入，不許。

translations.literal: The memorial was submitted; permission was not granted.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial was submitted, it was not approved.

sentences.zh: 天啟元年，鼐以紀元甫及半載，言官獲譴者至十余人，上疏切諫，並規諷輔臣。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tianqi, as less than half a year had passed since the new reign era began, more than ten censorial officials had been punished; Nai submitted a memorial with blunt admonition and also remonstrated against the chief ministers.
translations.idiomatic: In 1621, with barely half a year elapsed in the new reign, more than ten censorial officials had already been punished; Nai submitted a sharp memorial of admonition and also remonstrated against the chief ministers.

sentences.zh: 忤旨，譙責。

translations.literal: Defying the imperial intent, he was rebuked and reprimanded.
translations.idiomatic: Defying the imperial will, he was publicly rebuked.

sentences.zh: 尋遷禮部右侍郎，協理詹事府，充實錄副總裁。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to Right Vice Minister of Rites, concurrently managing the Household of the Heir Apparent, and appointed deputy chief compiler of the Veritable Records.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon transferred to Right Vice Minister of Rites, given concurrent charge of the Household of the Heir Apparent, and appointed deputy chief compiler of the Veritable Records.

sentences.zh: 鼐好學博聞，磊落有器識。

translations.literal: Nai loved learning and was broadly informed, upright and possessed of judgment and insight.
translations.idiomatic: Nai was a devoted scholar of wide learning, upright in character and possessed of sound judgment.

sentences.zh: 見魏忠賢亂政，引疾歸。

translations.literal: Seeing Wei Zhongxian's disorder of government, he cited illness and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing Wei Zhongxian's perversion of government, he pleaded illness and retired.

sentences.zh: 初，廷議李三才起用不決，鼐飏言曰：「今封疆倚重者，多遠道未至。

translations.literal: Initially, when court deliberated Li Sancai's recall without reaching a decision, Nai spoke openly, saying: "Those now relied upon for border defense are mostly from afar and have not yet arrived.
translations.idiomatic: When the court debated recalling Li Sancai without reaching a decision, Nai spoke openly: "Those now relied upon for border defense are mostly still en route from distant posts.

sentences.zh: 三才猷略素優，家近輦轂，可朝發夕至也。」

translations.literal: Sancai's strategy and planning have always been excellent; his home is near the imperial capital and he could arrive by evening if dispatched in the morning.
translations.idiomatic: Li Sancai's strategy has always been excellent; he lives near the capital and could arrive within a day.

sentences.zh: 侍郎鄒元標趣使盡言，以言路相持而止。

translations.literal: Vice Minister Zou Yuanbiao urged him to speak his full mind; because the remonstrance faction was deadlocked, it stopped there.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Minister Zou Yuanbiao urged him to say all he wished, but the deadlock among the remonstrance officials brought the matter to a halt.

sentences.zh: 後御史葉有聲追論鼐與三才為姻，徇私妄薦，遂落職閑住。

translations.literal: Later Censor Ye Yousheng pursued the matter, arguing that Nai and Sancai were related by marriage and that he had recommended out of private favor recklessly; he was consequently stripped of office and made to live in retirement.
translations.idiomatic: Later Censor Ye Yousheng charged that Nai and Li Sancai were related by marriage and that his recommendation had been a reckless act of favoritism; Nai was stripped of office and retired.

sentences.zh: 未幾卒。

translations.literal: Before long he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died soon after.

sentences.zh: 崇禎初，復官賜恤，謚文介。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Chongzhen, his office was restored, mourning grants were bestowed, and he was posthumously titled Wenjie.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Chongzhen reign his office was restored, mourning grants were bestowed, and he was posthumously honored as Wenjie.

sentences.zh: 羅喻義，字湘中，益陽人。

translations.literal: Luo Yuyi, courtesy name Xiangzhong, was a native of Yiyang.
translations.idiomatic: Luo Yuyi, courtesy name Xiangzhong, came from Yiyang.

sentences.zh: 萬歷四十一年進士。

translations.literal: In the forty-first year of Wanli he passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: In 1613 he passed the jinshi examination.

sentences.zh: 改庶吉士，授檢討。

translations.literal: He was made a Metropolitan Graduate and appointed Reviser.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed a junior Hanlin scholar and then Reviser.

sentences.zh: 請假歸。

translations.literal: He requested leave and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: He took leave and returned home.

sentences.zh: 天啟初還朝，歷官諭德，直經筵。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianqi he returned to court, served through posts as Preceptor, and attended the Classics Lectern.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Tianqi reign he returned to court, rose through posts as Preceptor, and attended the Classics Lectern.

sentences.zh: 六年擢南京國子祭酒。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he was promoted to Grand Master of the Imperial Academy in Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: In 1626 he was promoted to Grand Master of the Nanjing Imperial Academy.

sentences.zh: 諸生欲為魏忠賢建祠，喻義懲其倡者，乃已。

translations.literal: The students wished to build a shrine to Wei Zhongxian; Yuyi punished the ringleaders, and only then did it cease.
translations.idiomatic: When students proposed building a shrine to Wei Zhongxian, Yuyi punished the ringleaders, and the plan was abandoned.

sentences.zh: 忠賢黨輯東林籍貫，湖廣二十人，以喻義為首。

translations.literal: Zhongxian's faction compiled the native places of the Donglin faction; of twenty from Huguang, Yuyi was listed first.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongxian's faction compiled a roster of Donglin adherents by native place; Yuyi headed the list of twenty from Huguang.

sentences.zh: 莊烈帝嗣位，召拜禮部右侍郎，協理詹事府。

translations.literal: When the Sublime Emperor succeeded to the throne, he was summoned and appointed Right Vice Minister of Rites, concurrently managing the Household of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Chongzhen succeeded to the throne, he was recalled and appointed Right Vice Minister of Rites with concurrent charge of the Household of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 尋充日講官，教習庶吉士。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed Daily Lecturer and instructed the Metropolitan Graduates.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon appointed Daily Lecturer and given charge of instructing junior Hanlin scholars.

sentences.zh: 喻義性嚴冷，閉戶讀書，不輕接一客。

translations.literal: Yuyi's nature was stern and aloof; he shut his doors to read and did not lightly receive a single guest.
translations.idiomatic: Yuyi was stern and reserved by nature; he kept to his books behind closed doors and rarely received visitors.

sentences.zh: 後見中外多故，將吏不習兵，銳意講武事，推演陣圖獻之。

translations.literal: Later, seeing many troubles at home and abroad and that generals and officers did not train in warfare, he devoted himself zealously to military affairs, worked out formations and diagrams, and presented them.
translations.idiomatic: Later, seeing turmoil at home and abroad and that commanders had neglected military training, he devoted himself to military affairs, worked out battle formations, and submitted them to the throne.

sentences.zh: 帝為褒納。

translations.literal: The emperor praised and accepted them.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor praised and accepted his proposals.

sentences.zh: 以時方用兵，而督撫大吏不立軍府，財用無所資，因言：「武有七德，豐財居其一。

translations.literal: As troops were then being deployed but grand coordinators and governors did not establish military treasuries and funds had no source, he therefore said: "War has seven virtues, and abundant resources ranks among them.
translations.idiomatic: As the empire was at war yet grand coordinators and governors had established no military treasuries and funds had no source, he argued: "War has seven virtues, and abundant resources is one of them.

sentences.zh: 正餉之外，宜別立軍府，朝廷勿預知。

translations.literal: Beyond regular pay, a separate military treasury should be established; the court should not be forewarned of its affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Beyond regular pay, a separate military treasury should be established, its operations kept from prior scrutiny by the court.

sentences.zh: 饗士、賞功、購敵，皆取給於是。」

translations.literal: Feasting soldiers, rewarding merit, and purchasing intelligence from the enemy—all should be drawn from this.
translations.idiomatic: Feasting soldiers, rewarding merit, and purchasing intelligence from the enemy—all should be drawn from this fund.

sentences.zh: 又極陳車戰之利。

translations.literal: He also exhaustively expounded the advantages of chariot warfare.
translations.idiomatic: He also expounded at length on the advantages of chariot warfare.

sentences.zh: 帝下軍府議於所司，令喻義自制戰車。

translations.literal: The emperor referred the military treasury proposal to the relevant offices and ordered Yuyi to design war chariots himself.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor referred the military treasury proposal to the relevant offices and ordered Yuyi to design the war chariots himself.

sentences.zh: 喻義復上言按畝加派之害，而以戰車營造職在有司，不肯奉詔。

translations.literal: Yuyi again memorialized on the harm of surcharges levied per mu, and because the construction of war chariots was the duty of the relevant offices, he refused to obey the edict.
translations.idiomatic: Yuyi memorialized again on the harm of surcharges levied by the mu, and because constructing war chariots was the responsibility of the relevant offices, he declined to follow the edict.

sentences.zh: 帝不悅，疏遂不行。

translations.literal: The emperor was displeased, and the memorial was not implemented.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was displeased, and the proposal was never carried out.

sentences.zh: 明年九月，進講《尚書》，撰《布昭聖武講義》。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of the following year, he lectured on the Book of Documents and composed the "Lecture Notes on Displaying Sacred Martial Prowess."
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of the following year he lectured on the Book of Documents and composed the Lecture Notes on Displaying Sacred Martial Prowess.

sentences.zh: 中及時事，有「左右之者不得其人」語，頗傷執政；

translations.literal: Within it he touched on current affairs, with the phrase "those at his side are not the right men," which rather wounded those in power.
translations.idiomatic: In it he touched on current affairs, including the line "those at the emperor's side are not the right men"—a remark that stung those in power.

sentences.zh: 末陳祖宗大閱之規，京營之制，冀有所興革。

translations.literal: At the end he set forth the regulations for the ancestral grand inspections and the metropolitan garrison system, hoping for reforms.
translations.idiomatic: At the end he set out the regulations for the ancestral grand inspections and the metropolitan garrison system, hoping reforms might follow.

sentences.zh: 呈稿政府，溫體仁不懌，使正字官語喻義，令改。

translations.literal: He submitted the draft to the government; Wen Tizhong was displeased and sent a proofreader to tell Yuyi to revise it.
translations.idiomatic: He submitted the draft to the Grand Secretariat; Wen Tizhong was displeased and sent a proofreader to instruct Yuyi to revise it.

sentences.zh: 喻義造閣中，隔扉誚體仁。

translations.literal: Yuyi went to the Grand Secretariat and, through the partition, reproached Tizhong.
translations.idiomatic: Yuyi went to the Grand Secretariat and, through the partition, rebuked Wen Tizhong.

sentences.zh: 體仁怒，上言：「故事，惟經筵進規，多於正講，目講則正多規少。

translations.literal: Tizhong was angered and submitted a memorial: "By precedent, remonstrance at the Classics Lectern comes mostly in the main lecture, while in the Daily Lecture the main text is more and remonstrance less.
translations.idiomatic: Wen Tizhong was angered and submitted a memorial: "By precedent, remonstrance at the Classics Lectern comes mostly in the main lecture, while in the Daily Lecture the main text is more and remonstrance less.

sentences.zh: 今喻義以日講而用經筵之制，及令刪改，反遭其侮，惟聖明裁察。」

translations.literal: Now Yuyi uses the Classics Lectern format in the Daily Lecture, and when ordered to delete and revise, he instead suffers insult; I pray the Sacred Intelligence will judge.
translations.idiomatic: Now Yuyi applies the Classics Lectern format to the Daily Lecture, and when told to revise his text he is insulted instead; I pray Your Majesty will judge.

sentences.zh: 遂下吏部議。

translations.literal: The matter was then sent down to the Ministry of Personnel for deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: The case was referred to the Ministry of Personnel for deliberation.

sentences.zh: 喻義奏辨曰：「講官於正文外旁及時事，亦舊制也。

translations.literal: Yuyi submitted a defense: "For lecturers to touch on current affairs beyond the main text is also an old institution.
translations.idiomatic: Yuyi submitted a defense: "For lecturers to touch on current affairs beyond the main text is also an established practice.

sentences.zh: 臣展轉敷陳，冀少有裨益。

translations.literal: Your servant repeated and elaborated, hoping for some small benefit.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant elaborated at length, hoping to offer some small benefit.

sentences.zh: 體仁刪去，臣誠恐愚忠不獲上達，致忤輔臣。

translations.literal: Tizhong deleted it; your servant truly feared that sincere but foolish loyalty would not reach above and so offended the chief minister.
translations.idiomatic: When Tizhong cut those passages, your servant feared that sincere but unpolished loyalty would never reach Your Majesty, and thus gave offense to the chief minister.

sentences.zh: 今稿草具在，望聖明省覽。」

translations.literal: The draft is complete and at hand; your servant hopes the Sacred Intelligence will examine it.
translations.idiomatic: The draft still survives; your servant prays Your Majesty will examine it.

sentences.zh: 吏部希體仁指，議革職閑住，可之。

translations.literal: The Ministry of Personnel, reading Tizhong's intent, recommended stripping office and ordering retirement; this was approved.
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of Personnel, following Tizhong's wishes, recommended that Yuyi be stripped of office and retired; the emperor approved.

sentences.zh: 喻義雅負時望，為體仁所傾，士論交惜。

translations.literal: Yuyi had long carried public esteem; brought down by Tizhong, opinion among scholars everywhere lamented.
translations.idiomatic: Yuyi had long enjoyed public esteem; when Tizhong brought him down, scholars everywhere lamented.

sentences.zh: 瀕行乞恩，請乘傳，帝亦報可。

translations.literal: On the verge of departure he begged imperial favor to request post-horses; the emperor also granted approval.
translations.idiomatic: Before departing he petitioned for the favor of post-horses for his journey; the emperor granted his request.

sentences.zh: 家居十年，卒。

translations.literal: He lived at home ten years, then died.
translations.idiomatic: He lived in retirement for ten years, then died.

sentences.zh: 姚希孟，字孟長，吳縣人。

translations.literal: Yao Ximeng, courtesy name Mengchang, was a native of Wu County.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Ximeng, courtesy name Mengchang, came from Wu County.

sentences.zh: 生十月而孤，母文氏勵誌鞠之。

translations.literal: Ten months after his birth he lost his father; his mother, née Wen, steeled her resolve and raised him.
translations.idiomatic: He lost his father when ten months old; his mother, Lady Wen, steeled her resolve and raised him alone.

sentences.zh: 稍長，與舅文震孟同學，並負時名。

translations.literal: When somewhat grown, he studied with his maternal uncle Wen Zhenmeng; both bore contemporary renown.
translations.idiomatic: As he grew, he studied alongside his maternal uncle Wen Zhenmeng; both enjoyed considerable renown.

sentences.zh: 舉萬歷四十七年進士，改庶吉士。

translations.literal: In the forty-seventh year of Wanli he passed the jinshi examination and was made a Metropolitan Graduate.
translations.idiomatic: In 1619 he passed the jinshi examination and was appointed a junior Hanlin scholar.

sentences.zh: 座主韓爌、館師劉一燝器之。

translations.literal: His chief examiner Han Kuang and tutor Liu Yijuan valued him highly.
translations.idiomatic: His chief examiner Han Kuang and tutor Liu Yijuan thought highly of him.

sentences.zh: 兩人並執政，遇大事多所咨決。

translations.literal: Both came to hold power; on major affairs they often consulted him for decisions.
translations.idiomatic: Both later rose to power, and on major affairs they often consulted him.

sentences.zh: 天啟初，震孟亦取上第，入翰林，甥舅並持清議，望益重。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianqi, Zhenmeng also took top honors and entered the Hanlin; uncle and nephew both upheld pure remonstrance, and their standing grew weightier.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Tianqi reign Zhenmeng also placed at the top of his cohort and entered the Hanlin; uncle and nephew alike upheld stern moral criticism, and their standing only grew.

sentences.zh: 尋請假歸。

translations.literal: Soon he requested leave and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: He soon took leave and returned home.

sentences.zh: 四年冬還朝，趙南星、高攀龍等悉去位，黨禍大作，希孟郁郁不得誌。

translations.literal: In the fourth winter he returned to court; Zhao Nanxing, Gao Panlong, and others were all removed from office; the factional catastrophe erupted on a grand scale; Ximeng was dejected and unable to fulfill his aspirations.
translations.idiomatic: He returned to court in the winter of the fourth year; Zhao Nanxing, Gao Panlong, and others had all been removed, the factional purge was at its height, and Ximeng was dejected and unable to make his mark.

sentences.zh: 其明年，以母喪歸。

translations.literal: The following year, on his mother's death, he returned home.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he returned home upon his mother's death.

sentences.zh: 甫出都，給事中楊所修劾其為繆昌期死黨，遂削籍。

translations.literal: Just after leaving the capital, Supervising Secretary Yang Suoxiu impeached him as a sworn partisan of Miu Changqi; he was consequently struck from the rolls.
translations.idiomatic: Hardly had he left the capital when Supervising Secretary Yang Suoxiu impeached him as a sworn partisan of Miu Changqi; he was struck from the rolls.

sentences.zh: 魏忠賢敗，其黨倪文煥懼誅，使使持厚賄求解，希孟執而鳴之官。

translations.literal: When Wei Zhongxian fell, his partisan Ni Wenhuan feared execution and sent an envoy with a heavy bribe seeking release; Ximeng seized him and reported him to the authorities.
translations.idiomatic: When Wei Zhongxian fell, his partisan Ni Wenhuan, fearing execution, sent an envoy bearing a heavy bribe to buy his way free; Ximeng seized the envoy and reported the matter to the authorities.

sentences.zh: 崇禎元年，起左贊善。

translations.literal: In the first year of Chongzhen he was recalled as Left Tutor to the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In 1628 he was recalled as Left Tutor to the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 歷右庶子，為日講官。

translations.literal: He rose through Right Sub-Expositor and served as Daily Lecturer.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Right Sub-Expositor and served as Daily Lecturer.

sentences.zh: 三年秋，與諭德姚明恭主順天鄉試。

translations.literal: In the autumn of the third year, together with Preceptor Yao Minggong he presided over the Shuntian provincial examination.
translations.idiomatic: In the autumn of 1630 he presided over the Shuntian provincial examination together with Preceptor Yao Minggong.

sentences.zh: 有武生二人冒籍中式，給事中王猷論之，遂獲譴。

translations.literal: Two military students had passed the examination by false registration; Supervising Secretary Wang You discussed the matter, and they were punished.
translations.idiomatic: Two military students had passed the examination under false registration; Supervising Secretary Wang You raised the matter, and Ximeng was punished.

sentences.zh: 希孟雅為東林所推。

translations.literal: Ximeng had long been promoted by the Donglin faction.
translations.idiomatic: Ximeng had long been championed by the Donglin faction.

sentences.zh: 韓爌等定逆案，參其議。

translations.literal: When Han Kuang and others settled the case of the rebels, he participated in their deliberations.
translations.idiomatic: When Han Kuang and others settled the catalogue of rebels, he took part in their deliberations.

sentences.zh: 群小惡希孟，謀先之。

translations.literal: The petty men hated Ximeng and plotted to get to him first.
translations.idiomatic: The petty faction hated Ximeng and plotted to strike at him first.

sentences.zh: 及華允誠劾溫體仁、閔洪學，兩人疑疏出希孟手，體仁遂借冒籍事修隙，擬旨覆試，黜兩生下所司，論考官罪，擬停俸半年。

translations.literal: When Hua Yuncheng impeached Wen Tizhong and Min Hongxue, the two suspected the memorial came from Ximeng's hand; Tizhong then used the false-registration affair to nurture a grudge, drafted a rescript ordering a retest, dismissed the two students to the relevant offices, judged the examiners' crime, and proposed withholding salary for half a year.
translations.idiomatic: When Hua Yuncheng impeached Wen Tizhong and Min Hongxue, the two suspected the memorial had been drafted by Ximeng; Tizhong seized on the false-registration affair to settle a score, drafting a rescript for a retest, dismissing the two students to the relevant authorities, finding the examiners guilty, and proposing that their salaries be withheld for half a year.

sentences.zh: 體仁意未慊，令再擬。

translations.literal: Tizhong's intent was not yet satisfied; he ordered a redraft.
translations.idiomatic: Tizhong was not satisfied and ordered a redraft.

sentences.zh: 希孟時已遷詹事，乃貶二秩為少詹事，掌南京翰林院。

translations.literal: Ximeng had by then been transferred to Director of the Household of the Heir Apparent; he was demoted two ranks to Junior Director of that Household, directing the Nanjing Hanlin Academy.
translations.idiomatic: Ximeng had by then been promoted to Director of the Household of the Heir Apparent; he was now demoted two ranks to Junior Director and given charge of the Nanjing Hanlin Academy.

sentences.zh: 尋移疾歸，家居二年，卒。

translations.literal: Soon citing illness he returned home; he lived at home two years and died.
translations.idiomatic: He soon pleaded illness and retired; after two years at home he died.

sentences.zh: 許士柔，字仲嘉，常熟人。

translations.literal: Xu Shirou, courtesy name Zhongjia, was a native of Changshu.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Shirou, courtesy name Zhongjia, came from Changshu.

sentences.zh: 天啟二年進士。

translations.literal: In the second year of Tianqi he passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: In 1622 he passed the jinshi examination.

sentences.zh: 改庶吉士，授檢討。

translations.literal: He was made a Metropolitan Graduate and appointed Reviser.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed a junior Hanlin scholar and then Reviser.

sentences.zh: 崇禎時，歷遷左庶子，掌左春坊事。

translations.literal: During the Chongzhen reign he rose through promotions to Left Sub-Expositor, managing affairs of the Left Spring Office.
translations.idiomatic: During the Chongzhen reign he rose to Left Sub-Expositor with charge of the Left Spring Office.

sentences.zh: 先是，魏忠賢既輯《三朝要典》，以《光宗實錄》所載與《要典》左，乃言葉向高等所修非實，宜重修，遂恣意改削牴牾《要典》者。

translations.literal: Earlier, after Wei Zhongxian had compiled the Essential Canon of Three Reigns, because what was recorded in the Veritable Records of Emperor Guangzong conflicted with the Essential Canon, he said what Ye Xianggao and others had compiled was not factual and ought to be recompiled; he then arbitrarily revised and cut whatever contradicted the Essential Canon.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, after Wei Zhongxian had compiled the Essential Canon of Three Reigns, finding that the Veritable Records of Emperor Guangzong contradicted the Essential Canon, he declared that the version compiled by Ye Xianggao and others was unreliable and ought to be rewritten; he then arbitrarily revised away whatever conflicted with the Essential Canon.

sentences.zh: 崇禎改元，毀《要典》而所改《光宗實錄》如故。

translations.literal: When Chongzhen changed the reign era, the Essential Canon was destroyed but the revised Veritable Records of Guangzong remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: When Chongzhen ascended and the reign era changed, the Essential Canon was destroyed—but the revised Veritable Records of Guangzong remained unchanged.

sentences.zh: 六年，少詹事文震孟言：「皇考實錄為魏黨曲筆，當改正從原錄。」

translations.literal: In the sixth year, Junior Director Wen Zhenmeng said: "The Veritable Records of the late emperor were distorted by Wei faction pens and ought to be corrected to follow the original record.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year Junior Director Wen Zhenmeng argued: "The Veritable Records of the late emperor were distorted by Wei faction pens and ought to be corrected to follow the original record.

sentences.zh: 時溫體仁當國，與王應熊等陰沮之，事遂寢。

translations.literal: At the time Wen Tizhong held power; together with Wang Yingxiong and others he secretly obstructed it, and the matter was dropped.
translations.idiomatic: Wen Tizhong was then in power; with Wang Yingxiong and others he secretly blocked the proposal, and the matter was dropped.

sentences.zh: 士柔憤然曰：「若是，則《要典》猶弗焚矣。」

translations.literal: Shirou said indignantly: "If so, then the Essential Canon might as well not have been burned.
translations.idiomatic: Shirou said indignantly: "If so, the Essential Canon might as well never have been burned.

sentences.zh: 乃上疏曰：「皇考實錄總記，於世系獨略。

translations.literal: He then submitted a memorial saying: "In the general summary of the Veritable Records of the late emperor, the imperial lineage alone is scant.
translations.idiomatic: He then submitted a memorial: "In the general summary of the Veritable Records of the late emperor, the imperial lineage alone is scant.

sentences.zh: 皇上娠教之年，聖誕之日，不書也。

translations.literal: The year when Your Majesty received embryonic instruction and the day of sacred birth are not recorded.
translations.idiomatic: The year when Your Majesty received embryonic instruction and the day of Your Majesty's birth are not recorded.

sentences.zh: 命名之典，潛邸之號，不書也。

translations.literal: The naming ceremony and the style of the hidden residence are not recorded.
translations.idiomatic: The naming ceremony and the style of the hidden residence are not recorded.

sentences.zh: 聖母出何氏族，受何封號，不書也。

translations.literal: From what clan the empress dowager came and what title she received are not recorded.
translations.idiomatic: From what clan the empress dowager came and what title she received are not recorded.

sentences.zh: 此皆原錄備載，而改錄故削之者也。

translations.literal: All these were fully recorded in the original record, yet the revised record deliberately cut them.
translations.idiomatic: All these were fully recorded in the original version, yet the revised record deliberately omitted them.

sentences.zh: 原錄之成，在皇上潛邸之日，猶詳慎如彼。

translations.literal: The completion of the original record, during the days when Your Majesty was in the hidden residence, was still so thorough and cautious.
translations.idiomatic: The original record was compiled while Your Majesty was still in the hidden residence, yet it was thorough and cautious in just that way.

sentences.zh: 新錄之進，在皇上御極之初，何以率略如此，使聖朝父子、母後、兄弟之大倫，皆暗而不明，缺而莫考。

translations.literal: The submission of the new record, at the very beginning when Your Majesty ascended the throne—how can it be so cursory, making the great bonds of the sacred dynasty between father and son, empress and mother, and brothers all dim and unclear, deficient and beyond inquiry?
translations.idiomatic: The revised record was submitted at the very start of Your Majesty's reign—how could it be so cursory, leaving the great bonds of father and son, empress and mother, and brothers within the dynasty dim, obscure, and beyond recovery?

sentences.zh: 其於信史謂何？」

translations.literal: What does this mean for trustworthy history?
translations.idiomatic: What kind of trustworthy history is this?

sentences.zh: 疏上，不省。

translations.literal: When the memorial was submitted, it received no response.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was submitted but drew no response from the throne.

sentences.zh: 體仁令中書官檢穆宗總記示士柔，士柔具揭爭之曰：「皇考實錄與列聖條例不同。

translations.literal: Tizhong ordered a Secretariat officer to retrieve the general summary of Emperor Muzong and show Shirou; Shirou submitted a detailed rebuttal, saying: "The Veritable Records of the late emperor differ from the precedents of the successive emperors.
translations.idiomatic: Wen Tizhong ordered a Secretariat officer to retrieve the general summary of Emperor Muzong and show it to Shirou; Shirou submitted a detailed rebuttal: "The Veritable Records of the late emperor differ from the precedents of the successive emperors.

sentences.zh: 列聖在位久，登極後事，編年排纂，則總記可以不書。

translations.literal: The successive emperors reigned long; after their ascension, events were arranged chronologically, so the general summary need not be written.
translations.idiomatic: The successive emperors reigned long; after their ascension, events were arranged chronologically, so the general summary need not be written.

sentences.zh: 皇考在位僅一月，三後誕育聖躬皆在未登極以前，不書之總記，將於何書也？

translations.literal: The late emperor reigned only one month; the birth and nurture of the sacred person by the three empresses all came before ascension—if not written in the general summary, where will they be written?
translations.idiomatic: The late emperor reigned only one month; the three empresses who bore and nurtured Your Majesty all did so before his ascension—if these are omitted from the general summary, where else can they be recorded?

sentences.zh: 穆廟大婚之禮，皇子之生，在嘉靖中，故總記不載，至於冊立大典，編年未嘗不具載也。

translations.literal: Emperor Muzong's grand wedding ceremony and the birth of the imperial son occurred during the Jiajing reign, so the general summary does not record them; yet as for the great ceremony of investiture as heir, the chronicle never failed to record it fully.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Muzong's grand wedding and the birth of the imperial son occurred during the Jiajing reign, so the general summary omits them—but the chronicle always records the investiture ceremony in full.

sentences.zh: 皇考一月易世，熹廟之冊立當書，皇上之冊封獨不當書乎？」

translations.literal: The late emperor changed the world in one month—the investiture of Emperor Xizong ought to be written; should the enfeoffment of Your Majesty alone not be written?
translations.idiomatic: The late emperor's reign lasted only one month—the investiture of Emperor Xizong ought to be recorded; should Your Majesty's own enfeoffment alone go unrecorded?

sentences.zh: 體仁怒，將劾之，為同列沮止。

translations.literal: Tizhong was angered and was about to impeach him, but was stopped by his colleagues.
translations.idiomatic: Wen Tizhong was furious and was about to impeach him, but his colleagues dissuaded him.

sentences.zh: 士柔復上疏曰：「累朝實錄，無不書世系之例。

translations.literal: Shirou again submitted a memorial: "In the Veritable Records of successive reigns, there has never been a precedent of failing to record the imperial lineage.
translations.idiomatic: Shirou submitted another memorial: "In the Veritable Records of successive reigns, there has never been a precedent of failing to record the imperial lineage.

sentences.zh: 臣所以抉擿改錄，正謂與累朝成例不合也。

translations.literal: The reason your servant picks out and exposes the revised record is precisely that it does not accord with established precedents of successive reigns.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant has called out the revised record precisely because it departs from the established precedents of successive reigns.

sentences.zh: 孝端皇后，皇考之嫡母也，原錄具書保護之功，而改錄削之，何也？

translations.literal: Empress Xiaoduan was the late emperor's legitimate mother; the original record fully recorded her protective merit, yet the revised record cut it—why?
translations.idiomatic: Empress Xiaoduan was the late emperor's legitimate mother; the original record fully records her devoted care, yet the revised record omits it—why?

sentences.zh: 當日國本幾危，坤寧調護，真孝慈之極則，顧復之深恩，史官不難以寸管抹摋之，此尤不可解也。」

translations.literal: In those days the foundation of the state nearly wavered; the nurturing care from the Kunning Palace was the utmost norm of filial piety and compassion, a profound debt of rearing—what difficulty is there for the historiographer's slender brush to blot it out? This is especially incomprehensible.
translations.idiomatic: In those days the succession itself nearly foundered; the devoted care from the Kunning Palace embodied the highest filial and maternal virtue, a profound debt of nurture—yet the historiographer's slender brush could blot it out without difficulty. This is especially incomprehensible.

sentences.zh: 疏上，報聞。

translations.literal: When the memorial was submitted, acknowledgment was returned.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was submitted; the court noted receipt and took no further action.

sentences.zh: 體仁滋不悅。

translations.literal: Tizhong grew still more displeased.
translations.idiomatic: Wen Tizhong grew still more displeased.

sentences.zh: 會體仁嗾劉孔昭劾祭酒倪元璐，因言士柔族子重熙私撰《五朝註略》，將以連士柔。

translations.literal: Tizhong then incited Liu Kongzhao to impeach Chancellor Ni Yuanlu, alleging that Shirou's clansman Chongxi had privately compiled Annotations on Five Reigns, intending to implicate Shirou as well.
translations.idiomatic: Wen Tizhong then incited Liu Kongzhao to impeach University Chancellor Ni Yuanlu, alleging that Shirou's clansman Chongxi had privately compiled Annotations on Five Reigns and intending to implicate Shirou as well.

sentences.zh: 士柔亟以《註略》進，乃得解。

translations.literal: Shirou hurriedly submitted the Annotations to the throne and was thus cleared.
translations.idiomatic: Shirou hurriedly presented the Annotations to the throne and was cleared of the charge.

sentences.zh: 尋出為南京國子祭酒。

translations.literal: Soon he was sent out as Nanjing Chancellor of the National University.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was posted as Chancellor of the Nanjing National University.

sentences.zh: 體仁去，張至發當國，益謀逐士柔。

translations.literal: When Tizhong left office, Zhang Zhifa held power and plotted all the more to drive Shirou away.
translations.idiomatic: After Wen Tizhong left office, Zhang Zhifa became chief minister and plotted all the more to drive Shirou from court.

sentences.zh: 先是，高攀龍贈官，士柔草詔詞送內閣，未給攀龍家。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Gao Panlong was granted posthumous office, Shirou drafted the edict text and sent it to the Grand Secretariat, but it was never delivered to Gao's family.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Gao Panlong was granted posthumous honors, Shirou drafted the edict text and sent it to the Grand Secretariat, but it was never delivered to Gao's family.

sentences.zh: 故事，贈官誥，屬誥敕中書職掌。

translations.literal: By precedent, edicts for posthumous office fell under the charge of the Secretariat drafters of edicts and patents.
translations.idiomatic: By precedent, edicts conferring posthumous office were the responsibility of the Secretariat drafters of edicts and patents.

sentences.zh: 崇禎初，褒恤諸忠臣，翰林能文者或為之，而中書以為侵官。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Chongzhen, loyal ministers were honored and comforted; Hanlin scholars skilled in letters sometimes drafted the texts, but the Secretariat drafters regarded this as encroachment on their office.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Chongzhen reign, loyal ministers were honored and comforted; Hanlin scholars skilled in letters sometimes drafted the texts, but the Secretariat drafters regarded this as encroachment on their duties.

sentences.zh: 崇禎三年禁誥文駢儷語。

translations.literal: In Chongzhen 3 parallel prose in patent edicts was forbidden.
translations.idiomatic: In Chongzhen 3 the court forbade parallel prose in patent edicts.

sentences.zh: 至是攀龍家請給，去士柔草制時數年矣，主者仍以士柔前撰文進。

translations.literal: By then Gao's family requested delivery; several years had passed since Shirou drafted the text, yet those in charge still submitted Shirou's earlier composition.
translations.idiomatic: By then Gao's family requested delivery; several years had passed since Shirou drafted the text, yet the officials in charge still submitted his earlier composition.

sentences.zh: 中書黃應恩告至發誥語違禁，至發喜，劾士柔，降二級調用。

translations.literal: Secretariat drafter Huang Ying'en reported to Zhifa that the patent language violated the prohibition; Zhifa was pleased and impeached Shirou, who was demoted two ranks and transferred.
translations.idiomatic: Secretariat drafter Huang Ying'en reported to Zhang Zhifa that the patent language violated the prohibition; delighted, Zhang impeached Shirou, who was demoted two ranks and transferred.

sentences.zh: 司業周鳳翔抗疏辯曰：「詞林故事，閣臣分屬撰文，或手加詳定，或發竄改，未有徑自糾參者也。

translations.literal: Vice Director Zhou Fengxiang submitted a forceful memorial in defense, saying: "By Hanlin precedent, Grand Secretaries assigned drafting duties; they might personally revise and approve, or order alterations—never was a drafter impeached directly in this fashion.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Director Zhou Fengxiang submitted a forceful memorial in defense: "By Hanlin precedent, Grand Secretaries assigned drafting duties; they might personally revise and approve or order alterations—never was a drafter impeached directly in this fashion.

sentences.zh: 誥敕用寶，歲有常期，未有十年後用寶進呈，吹求當制者也。

translations.literal: Patent edicts receive the imperial seal on fixed annual schedules; never has a text sealed and submitted ten years later been scrutinized against present regulations.
translations.idiomatic: Patent edicts receive the imperial seal on fixed annual schedules; never has a text sealed and submitted ten years later been scrutinized against present regulations.

sentences.zh: 贈誥專屬中書，崇禎三年所申飭，未有追咎元年之史官，詆為越俎者也。」

translations.literal: Posthumous patents belong solely to the Secretariat drafters; the admonition issued in Chongzhen 3 did not authorize blaming the historiographer of the first year and denouncing him for overstepping his office.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumous patents belong solely to the Secretariat drafters; the admonition issued in Chongzhen 3 did not authorize blaming the historiographer of the first year and denouncing him for overstepping his office.

sentences.zh: 不報。

translations.literal: No response was given.
translations.idiomatic: The throne gave no response.

sentences.zh: 士柔尋補尚寶司丞，遷少卿，卒。

translations.literal: Shirou soon was restored as Vice Director of the Imperial Seals Office, was promoted to Junior Director, and died.
translations.idiomatic: Shirou was soon restored as Vice Director of the Imperial Seals Office, promoted to Junior Director, and died in office.

sentences.zh: 子琪詣闕辨誣，乃復原官。

translations.literal: His son Qi went to court to clear the slander, and Shirou's former rank was restored.
translations.idiomatic: His son Qi went to court to clear the slander, and Shirou's former rank was restored posthumously.

sentences.zh: 贈詹事兼侍讀學士。

translations.literal: He was posthumously made Grand Tutor and Concurrent Hanlin Reader-in-Waiting.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made Grand Tutor and Concurrent Hanlin Reader-in-Waiting.

sentences.zh: 顧錫疇，字九疇，昆山人。

translations.literal: Gu Xichou, styled Jiuchou, was a native of Kunshan.
translations.idiomatic: Gu Xichou, courtesy name Jiuchou, came from Kunshan.

sentences.zh: 年十三，以諸生試南京，魏國公以女女之。

translations.literal: At thirteen, as a student he took the examination at Nanjing; the Duke of Wei gave him his daughter in marriage.
translations.idiomatic: At thirteen, while still a student, he took the examination at Nanjing; the Duke of Wei gave him his daughter in marriage.
