sentences.zh: 第萬歷四十七年進士，改庶吉士，授檢討。

translations.literal: He placed among the jinshi of Wanli 47, was made a Hanlin bachelor, and was appointed Reviser.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in 1619, was made a Hanlin bachelor, and was appointed Reviser.

sentences.zh: 天啟四年，魏忠賢勢大熾，錫疇偕給事中董承業典試福建，程策大有譏刺。

translations.literal: In Tianqi 4, as Wei Zhongxian's power blazed, Xichou together with Supervising Secretary Dong Chengye presided over the Fujian provincial examination; the examination essays contained much satirical criticism.
translations.idiomatic: In 1624, as Wei Zhongxian's power reached its height, Xichou and Supervising Secretary Dong Chengye presided over the Fujian provincial examination, and the examination essays contained sharp satirical criticism.

sentences.zh: 忠賢黨遂指為東林，兩人並降調。

translations.literal: Wei's faction then denounced them as Donglin partisans; both men were demoted and transferred.
translations.idiomatic: Wei's faction denounced them as Donglin partisans, and both men were demoted and transferred.

sentences.zh: 已，更削籍。

translations.literal: Later their names were further stricken from the rolls.
translations.idiomatic: Later their names were stricken from the rolls altogether.

sentences.zh: 崇禎初，召復故官。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Chongzhen he was recalled to his former office.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Chongzhen reign he was recalled to his former office.

sentences.zh: 歷遷國子祭酒。

translations.literal: He rose through offices to Chancellor of the National University.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through the ranks to become Chancellor of the National University.

sentences.zh: 疏請復積分法，禮官格不行。

translations.literal: He memorialized to restore the cumulative-points system; the Ministry of Rites blocked it and it was not implemented.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized to restore the cumulative-points system, but the Ministry of Rites blocked it and the proposal was not implemented.

sentences.zh: 錫疇復申言之，且請擇監生為州縣長。

translations.literal: Xichou repeated the request and also asked that Imperial University students be selected as prefectural and county magistrates.
translations.idiomatic: Xichou repeated the request and also asked that Imperial University students be selected to serve as prefectural and county magistrates.

sentences.zh: 已，請正從祀位次，進士為國子博士者得與考選。

translations.literal: Later he asked to rectify the order of collateral sacrifices and that jinshi serving as National University lecturers be allowed to take part in evaluation and selection.
translations.idiomatic: He later asked to rectify the order of collateral sacrifices and that jinshi serving as National University lecturers be allowed to take part in evaluation and selection.

sentences.zh: 帝並允行。

translations.literal: The emperor approved all.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved every proposal.

sentences.zh: 省親歸，乞在籍終養。

translations.literal: Returning home to visit his parents, he asked to complete his filial nurturing in his native place.
translations.idiomatic: Returning home to visit his parents, he asked to remain in his native place and complete his period of filial mourning.

sentences.zh: 母服除，起少詹事，進詹事，拜禮部左侍郎，署部事。

translations.literal: When mourning for his mother ended, he was raised to Junior Director of the Palace Library, advanced to Director, appointed Left Vice Minister of Rites, and directed ministry affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When mourning for his mother ended, he was made Junior Director of the Palace Library, promoted to Director, appointed Left Vice Minister of Rites, and put in charge of ministry affairs.

sentences.zh: 帝嘗召對，問理財用人。

translations.literal: The emperor once summoned him for audience and asked about managing finances and employing men.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor once summoned him for a private audience and asked about managing finances and employing men.

sentences.zh: 錫疇退，列陳用人五失，曰銓敘無法，文網太峻，議論太多，資格太拘，鼓舞未至。

translations.literal: Xichou withdrew and set forth five failures in employment: no method in appointments, literary prohibitions too severe, discussion too abundant, qualifications too rigid, and encouragement not reaching men.
translations.idiomatic: Xichou withdrew and set forth five failures in employment: no sound method of appointment, literary prohibitions too severe, discussion too abundant, qualifications too rigid, and encouragement not reaching men.

sentences.zh: 請先令用人之地一清其源。

translations.literal: He asked first to cleanse the source where men are employed.
translations.idiomatic: He asked first to cleanse the source of official appointments.

sentences.zh: 「精心鑒別，隨才器使，一善也。

translations.literal: Careful discernment and assignment according to talent and capacity is the first good.
translations.idiomatic: Careful discernment and assignment according to talent and capacity is the first remedy.

sentences.zh: 赦小過而不終廢棄，二善也。

translations.literal: Pardoning minor faults and not discarding men forever is the second good.
translations.idiomatic: Pardoning minor faults and not discarding men forever is the second.

sentences.zh: 省議論而專責成，三善也。

translations.literal: Reducing discussion and insisting on results is the third good.
translations.idiomatic: Reducing empty discussion and insisting on results is the third.

sentences.zh: 拔異才而不拘常格，四善也。

translations.literal: Raising unusual talent without binding it to routine rules is the fourth good.
translations.idiomatic: Raising unusual talent without binding it to routine rules is the fourth.

sentences.zh: 急獎勵而寬督責，五善也。」

translations.literal: Urgent reward and relaxed supervision and blame is the fifth good.
translations.idiomatic: Swift reward and relaxed supervision and blame is the fifth.

sentences.zh: 末極陳耗財之弊，仍歸本於用人。

translations.literal: At the end he set forth at length the evils of waste in expenditure, still returning to the root in employment of men.
translations.idiomatic: At the end he set forth at length the evils of waste in expenditure, still tracing the problem back to how men were employed.

sentences.zh: 帝善其奏。

translations.literal: The emperor approved his memorial.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved his memorial.

sentences.zh: 楊嗣昌疏請撫流寇，有「樂天者保天下」及「善戰服上刑」語。

translations.literal: Yang Sichang memorialized requesting pacification of roving bandits, using the phrases "he who delights in Heaven secures the realm" and "skilled in battle, he submits to the supreme punishment."
translations.idiomatic: Yang Sichang memorialized requesting pacification of the roving bandits, citing the phrases "he who delights in Heaven secures the realm" and "skilled in battle, he submits to the supreme punishment."

sentences.zh: 錫疇抗言此諸侯交鄰事，稱引不倫，與嗣昌大忤。

translations.literal: Xichou protested forcefully that these were matters of feudal lords dealing with neighbors; the citations were incongruous, and he clashed sharply with Sichang.
translations.idiomatic: Xichou protested forcefully that these were matters of feudal lords dealing with neighbors, that the citations were incongruous, and he clashed sharply with Yang Sichang.

sentences.zh: 嗣昌秉政，諸詞臣多攻之，嗣昌頗疑錫疇。

translations.literal: When Sichang held power, many literary officials attacked Xichou; Sichang came to suspect him considerably.
translations.idiomatic: When Yang Sichang held power, many literary officials attacked Xichou, and Yang came to suspect him deeply.

sentences.zh: 會駙馬都尉王昺有罪，錫疇擬輕典，嗣昌構之，遂削其籍。

translations.literal: When Commandant-in-Chief of the Embroidered-Guard Horse Wang Bing committed an offense, Xichou drafted a light penalty; Sichang framed him, and Xichou's name was stricken from the rolls.
translations.idiomatic: When Commandant-in-Chief of the Embroidered-Guard Horse Wang Bing committed an offense, Xichou drafted a light penalty; Yang Sichang framed him, and Xichou's name was stricken from the rolls.

sentences.zh: 十五年，廷臣交薦，召還。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year court officials jointly recommended him and he was recalled.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year court officials jointly recommended him and he was recalled.

sentences.zh: 御史曹溶、給事中黃雲師復言其不當用。

translations.literal: Censor Cao Rong and Supervising Secretary Huang Yunshi again said he ought not be employed.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Cao Rong and Supervising Secretary Huang Yunshi again argued that he ought not be employed.

sentences.zh: 帝不聽，起為南京禮部左侍郎。

translations.literal: The emperor would not heed them and raised him as Left Vice Minister of Rites at Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor would not listen and appointed him Left Vice Minister of Rites at Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 福王立，進本部尚書。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Fu was enthroned, he was advanced to Minister of the ministry.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Fu was enthroned, he was promoted to Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 時尊福恭王為恭皇帝，將議廟祀，錫疇請別立專廟。

translations.literal: At the time the Prince of Fu's father was honored as Emperor Gong; as temple sacrifices were to be debated, Xichou asked that a separate dedicated temple be established.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the Prince of Fu's father was honored as Emperor Gong; as court debated temple sacrifices, Xichou asked that a separate dedicated temple be established.

sentences.zh: 俄請補建文帝廟謚、景皇帝廟號及建文朝忠臣贈謚，並從之。

translations.literal: Soon he asked to supply the temple posthumous title of the Jianwen Emperor, the temple name of the Jing Emperor, and posthumous honors for loyal ministers of the Jianwen reign; all were approved.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he asked to supply the temple posthumous title of the Jianwen Emperor, the temple name of the Jing Emperor, and posthumous honors for loyal ministers of the Jianwen reign; all were approved.

sentences.zh: 東平伯劉澤清言：「宋高宗即位南京，即以靖康二年五月為建炎元年，從民望也。

translations.literal: Eastern Pacification Earl Liu Zeqing said: "When Song Gaozong took the throne at Nanjing, he made the fifth month of Jingkang 2 the first year of Jianyan, following the people's hopes.
translations.idiomatic: Eastern Pacification Earl Liu Zeqing said: "When Song Gaozong took the throne at Nanjing, he made the fifth month of Jingkang 2 the first year of Jianyan, following the people's hopes.

sentences.zh: 乞以今歲五月為弘光元年。」

translations.literal: I beg that the fifth month of this year be made the first year of Hongguang.
translations.idiomatic: I beg that the fifth month of this year be made the first year of Hongguang.

sentences.zh: 錫疇言明詔已頒，不可追改，乃已。

translations.literal: Xichou said the clear edict had already been promulgated and could not be retroactively changed; the matter was dropped.
translations.idiomatic: Xichou said the imperial edict had already been promulgated and could not be retroactively changed, and the matter was dropped.

sentences.zh: 時定大行皇帝廟號為思宗，忻城伯趙之龍言「思」非美稱，援證甚核，錫疇亦以為然，疏請改定。

translations.literal: At the time the late emperor's temple name was fixed as Sizong; Xincheng Earl Zhao Zhilong said "Si" was not a fine designation and cited evidence very closely; Xichou also agreed and memorialized requesting a change.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the late emperor's temple name was fixed as Sizong; Xincheng Earl Zhao Zhilong argued that "Si" was not a fine designation and cited evidence in detail; Xichou agreed and memorialized requesting a change.

sentences.zh: 大學士高弘圖以前議自己出，力持之，遂寢。

translations.literal: Grand Secretary Gao Hongtu, because the earlier decision had come from himself, held firmly to it, and the matter was dropped.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Secretary Gao Hongtu, because the earlier decision had been his own, held firmly to it, and the matter was dropped.

sentences.zh: 溫體仁之卒也，特謚文忠，而文震孟、羅喻義、姚希孟、呂維祺皆不獲謚。

translations.literal: When Wen Tizhong died he was specially given the posthumous name Wenzhong, while Wen Zhenmeng, Luo Yuyi, Yao Ximeng, and Lü Weiqi all failed to receive posthumous names.
translations.idiomatic: When Wen Tizhong died he was specially given the posthumous name Wenzhong, while Wen Zhenmeng, Luo Yuyi, Yao Ximeng, and Lü Weiqi all failed to receive posthumous names.

sentences.zh: 錫疇言：「體仁得君，行政最專且久，其負先帝，罪大且深，乞將文忠之謚，或削或改，而補震孟諸臣，庶天下有所勸懲。」

translations.literal: Xichou said: "Tizhong won the ruler's trust and administered most exclusively and long; his betrayal of the late emperor was a crime great and deep. I beg that the posthumous name Wenzhong be either stripped or changed, and that Zhenmeng and the other ministers be supplied with honors, so that the realm may have encouragement and warning.
translations.idiomatic: Xichou argued: "Wen Tizhong won the ruler's trust and governed with exclusive power for a long time; his betrayal of the late emperor was a grave offense. I beg that the posthumous name Wenzhong be either stripped or changed, and that Zhenmeng and the other ministers receive posthumous honors, so that the realm may have both encouragement and warning.

sentences.zh: 報可。

translations.literal: Approval was granted.
translations.idiomatic: The throne approved.

sentences.zh: 遂謚諸人，削體仁謚。

translations.literal: Posthumous names were then granted to those men, and Tizhong's posthumous name was stripped.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumous names were then granted to those men, and Wen Tizhong's posthumous name was stripped.

sentences.zh: 吏部尚書張慎言去位，代者徐石麒未至，命錫疇攝之。

translations.literal: Minister of Personnel Zhang Shenyan left office; his replacement Xu Shiqi had not yet arrived, and Xichou was ordered to act in his stead.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Personnel Zhang Shenyan left office; his replacement Xu Shiqi had not yet arrived, and Xichou was ordered to act in his stead.

sentences.zh: 時馬士英當國，錫疇雅不與合。

translations.literal: At the time Ma Shiying held power; Xichou had never been on good terms with him.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Shiying was then in power, and Xichou had never been on good terms with him.

sentences.zh: 給事中章正宸、熊汝霖劾之，遂乞祭南海去。

translations.literal: Supervising Secretaries Zhang Zhenchen and Xiong Rulin impeached him, and he asked leave to perform sacrifices at the Southern Sea and depart.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising Secretaries Zhang Zhenchen and Xiong Rulin impeached him, and he asked leave to perform sacrifices at the Southern Sea and depart.

sentences.zh: 明年春，御史張孫振力頌體仁功，請復故謚。

translations.literal: The next spring, Censor Zhang Sunzhen forcefully praised Tizhong's achievements and asked that his former posthumous name be restored.
translations.idiomatic: The following spring, Censor Zhang Sunzhen forcefully praised Wen Tizhong's achievements and asked that his former posthumous name be restored.

sentences.zh: 遂勒錫疇致仕。

translations.literal: Xichou was then compelled to retire.
translations.idiomatic: Xichou was then compelled to retire.

sentences.zh: 南都失守，錫疇鄉邑亦破。

translations.literal: When the Southern Capital fell, Xichou's home district was also overrun.
translations.idiomatic: When the Southern Capital fell, Xichou's home district was overrun as well.

sentences.zh: 時方遭父喪，間關赴閩。

translations.literal: He was then in mourning for his father and made his way with difficulty to Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: He was then in mourning for his father and made his way with difficulty to Fujian.

sentences.zh: 唐王命以故官，力辭不拜，寓居溫州江心寺。

translations.literal: The Prince of Tang ordered him to his former office; he firmly declined and did not accept, lodging at Jiangxin Temple in Wenzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Tang offered him his former office; he firmly declined and lodged at Jiangxin Temple in Wenzhou.

sentences.zh: 總兵賀君堯撻辱諸生，錫疇將論劾。

translations.literal: Regional Commander He Junyao flogged and humiliated students; Xichou was about to memorialize in impeachment.
translations.idiomatic: Regional Commander He Junyao flogged and humiliated students, and Xichou was about to memorialize in impeachment.

sentences.zh: 君堯夜使人殺之，投屍於江。

translations.literal: Junyao by night sent men to kill him and cast the body into the river.
translations.idiomatic: He Junyao sent men by night to kill him and cast the body into the river.

sentences.zh: 溫人覓之三日，乃得棺殮。

translations.literal: The people of Wenzhou searched for three days before the body could be coffined and buried.
translations.idiomatic: The people of Wenzhou searched for three days before the body could be recovered for burial.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：吳山等雍容館閣，揚歷臺省，固所謂詞苑之鴻儒，廟堂之巋望也。

translations.literal: The appraiser says: Wu Shan and the others, composed and dignified in the academies and halls, rising through the censorial and secretarial offices, were indeed what are called great scholars of the literary garden and steadfast pillars of the court.
translations.idiomatic: The appraiser says: Wu Shan and his fellows, composed and dignified in the academies and halls and rising through the censorial and secretarial offices, were indeed the great scholars of the literary garden and the steadfast pillars of the court.

sentences.zh: 要其守正自立，不激不爭，淳靜敦雅，承平士大夫之風流，概可想見矣。

translations.literal: In sum, their upholding rectitude and standing on their own, neither provocative nor contentious, pure, tranquil, and refined—the cultivated bearing of scholar-officials in an age of peace—may broadly be imagined.
translations.idiomatic: Above all, their upholding of rectitude, their refusal to be provocative or contentious, and their pure, tranquil refinement—the cultivated bearing of scholar-officials in an age of peace—can readily be imagined.
